title: Cylinder Spectrum & Polygon Plexus
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"Cylinder Spectrum" & "Polygon Plexus" are two visual art exhibitions by Toronto artist Angela Julian (Native Torontonian and OCADU graduate). Both shows are located inside the Sun Gallery at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center. The collected works are a group of large scale colorful abstract paintings done in plaster. They range in size, scale, shape, and number, but they are all tied together through the mediums of plaster and acrylic paint.


On one side of the gallery is the show "Cylinder Spectrum", which is a group of acrylic paintings done on distinctly rounded canvases that were covered in layers of mixed-media and plaster. These are shown both as individual works and presented as a group that makeup a larger installation. The circular nature of the canvases and surfaces links the entire show by their rounded nature. On the opposite side of the gallery is the show "Polygon Plexus" which is a group of hand-made canvases and surfaces that were created to form irregular shapes. These outer shapes are deliberately jagged, pointed, elongated, and heavily textured surfaces, and each painting is covered with a either a geometric or abstract pattern. Both exhibitions demonstrate a variety of different color schemes and embrace vibrant, highly-saturated colors.


The Sun Gallery is the twin space to the Star Gallery on the property, and it is an airy and brilliantly lit space with wide sky-lights that allow for beautiful natural day-light. The gallery space is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably the beautiful wooden beams of its ceilings. These are two very fun shows and run until the end of October, 2026.

Upcoming Events | 918 Bathurst Centre for Culture, Arts, Media and Education https://www.918bathurst.com/events

title: The Face is a Landscape
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"The Face is a Landscape" is a visual arts exhibition by Toronto artist Angela Julian. The large body of art features colorful works done in Portraiture. The show is comprised of drawings and paintings created in a highly-detailed contemporary style. She explores painterly and drawn techniques in both wet and dry mediums. The faces are designed using many layers of blended line-work, impressions, and cross-hatchings. She uses very fine brushes and drawing instruments to achieve these micro-techniques that makeup the broader whole of the picture. The works are located in the Star Gallery and fill up the room from floor to ceiling. The subjects of each portrait are all well-known authors, writers, or philosophers by nature. Angela is penning her first book series in the high-fantasy genre, she has included portraits in the show based on writers that had a direct impact on her as a reader and aspiring author. The exhibition is largely a homage to those writers and thinkers who influenced her.


The Star Gallery is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably its beautiful wooden ceilings. The show runs until the end of October 2026, don't miss it!

location: Half Note 416,3357 Kingston Road, Scarborough, ON M1M 1R3, Canada
description:
Art on a Tuesday returns to Toronto on Friday, October 23 for an intimate, curated night of live entertainment, art, food and connection.

Taking place at Half Note 416 in Scarborough, the evening brings multiple forms of entertainment together under one roof — live R&B, comedy, magic and mentalism, spoken word, violin, visual art, featured creatives and DJs.

The October 23 lineup includes comedians Sai Kit Lo and Moe Ismail, magician and mentalist Francisco Perez, R&B singer Rose SHIKU, violinist Daniela Olano, spoken word artist Marie-Lauren Gregoire Drummond (MLG), along with featured visual artists and creatives.

Come early, grab dinner and drinks, explore the art, meet people and settle in for a show designed to keep the night moving from one experience to the next.

title: Free Friday night movie @ Innis Town Hall. Deliverance
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
🏕️ Free Movie Night: Deliverance — A Classic That Will Make You Think Twice About Camping!

Looking for something a little darker this Halloween season? Join us Friday, October 23 at Innis Town Hall for a FREE screening of the 1972 survival thriller Deliverance. 🎬

📍 Innis Town Hall
2 Sussex Avenue, Toronto
🎬 Movie starts: 7:10 PM
⏱️ Runtime: 109 minutes

🌲 About the Movie

Four friends head into the wilderness for a canoe trip down a remote river before a proposed dam changes the landscape forever.

What begins as an adventurous weekend quickly becomes a fight for survival as they encounter increasingly dangerous circumstances deep in the backcountry.

Starring Jon Voight, Burt Reynolds, Ned Beatty and Ronny Cox, Deliverance is one of the most famous—and unsettling—survival movies ever made.

Not sure about your schedule yet? That's okay! You can simply just show up if you're unsure whether you'll be able to make it. No pressure to RSVP.

Come out, meet some fellow movie fans, and experience one of the most iconic—and unforgettable—films of the 1970s. 🏕️🎬

Just remember: this is probably not the movie to watch right before planning your next canoe trip. 😬

title: Question Everything: Evaluating in an era of bias, spin and social polarization
description:
Part of the Think, Research, Create: Intro to Library Research Series (3 out of 4)
Not all information is created equally—and not all search tools work the same way. This interactive workshop will help you compare popular tools for information discovery from AI to academic search platforms. You’ll learn the differences between misinformation, disinformation, malinformation, AI hallucinations and deepfakes. We’ll show you practical fact-checking tools and strategies to help you figure out what’s real and what’s not. You’ll also practice evaluating sources, including academic ones, so you can choose the most reliable information for your assignments. By the end, you’ll feel more confident navigating the information jungle!

title: One Last Backcountry Weekend in Frontenac
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/weekend-in-frontenac)**

**Fall (aka shoulder season) camping brings the serene beauty of the backcountry, without the crowds and bugs.**

At this time of year, Frontenac will be less busy and the trail into Big Clear Lake belongs mostly to us. It's a 9km hike to reach the site, working through root tangled trails and stretches of open granite typical of this stretch of the Canadian Shield. Only the most stubborn leaves will remain on the trees and you’ll enjoy long sightlines through bare branches where the canopy used to be. The pace is steady and moderate the whole way in, never technical but never quite letting up either.

We set up camp on the shore of Big Clear Lake as the light starts to drop, we get a fire going, and cook dinner together. Late October nights out here are serene, with a sky full of stars over the lake.

In the morning, we’ll take our time over breakfast before packing up and heading out along the other side of Big Salmon Lake: a different stretch of trail from the one we hiked in on, with its own look at the park before we're back where we started.

By the time we're back at the cars, you'll have had that sweet final night of the year in the backcountry.

What's included

* Professional & certified guides
* ‍All camp meals, cooking equipment and mess kits
* ‍Tents

Sleeping bags and sleep pads can be rented from WU for a small fee.

**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com

**Highlights**
**Last Trip of the Season:** The final overnight on the calendar before WU's backcountry program pauses for winter
**Shoulder Season Solitude**: Long, quiet stretches of trail, with the lake mostly to yourselves.
**A Clear Night Sky:** Bare branches and dry autumn air make for some of the best stargazing conditions of the year at the campsite.

**Event cost: $265+HST. $70 optional transport also available. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/weekend-in-frontenac)**

**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.

Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!

***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: 🍂 Fall Walk: Rouge National Urban Park and  Picnic🌳
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🍂🌳 Fall Walk: Rouge National Urban Park 🌳🍁

### A Real Hike, Beautiful Fall Colours & a Picnic Together

Want to get out of the city without actually leaving Toronto?

**Rouge National Urban Park** is Canada's only urban national park — and one of the most popular hikes we do.
Once you get onto the trail, it can be hard to believe you're still in Toronto. Forest paths, rolling hills, changing leaves, and quiet stretches of wilderness make this feel much more like a trip outside the city than a walk through it.
And fall is one of the best times to experience it.

This is **a real hike**, though. There are some hills and ups and downs, so it isn't the best choice if you're looking for an easy, flat walk.
But if you're up for the challenge, there's something satisfying about reaching the end knowing you did it together.
And then we'll have a picnic. 🧺

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 🥾 What We'll Do

We'll meet at **Don Mills Station** and take the 85C bus together toward Rouge National Urban Park.
Once we arrive, we'll begin our hike through the park.
Along the way we'll:

* Hike through forest and open spaces 🌳
* Enjoy the fall colours 🍂
* Navigate the hills and changing terrain
* Take in some beautiful views
* Stop for a short break along the route
* Finish at the Park's Welcome Centre
* Have a **30–40 minute group picnic** afterward 🧺

The hike takes approximately **2½ hours**, plus a short break.
Afterward, we'll take some time to relax, eat, and enjoy each other's company.

***

## 🍁 Fall Weather & Expectations

This is a **moderately challenging hike**, not a casual stroll.
There are hills, uneven sections, and some ups and downs, so good walking or hiking shoes are important.
Please come prepared for typical fall weather and bring enough water for the hike.

If you're comfortable walking for a couple of hours and handling some elevation changes, you'll be fine.
If you're looking for something completely flat and easy, **this probably isn't the walk for you.**

***

## 🚌 Meetup Details

### 🚇 By TTC

📍 **Meetup Location:** Don Mills Station — on the platform for the **85C bus**
🫎 **Look for me in my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time:** **9:45 AM**
🚌 **Bus Leaves:** **10:06 AM sharp**
I'll wait for the bus, but if you miss it, **you won't be able to join the group afterward.**
**Early is on time. On time is late.**

### 🚗 By Car

Parking is **not available at our TTC meeting point.**

If you're driving, please park at the **Toronto Zoo** and walk to the **Park's Welcome Centre (the house)**.
🚗 **Car Meetup Time:** 11:00 AM

We may be a few minutes late arriving, depending on the bus and traffic.

***

## 🧺 The Picnic

After the hike, we'll have a **30–40 minute group picnic** at the end.
Please bring something small to share — nothing too large or heavy. The goal is simply to have something to eat together after the hike.
🥪 Sandwiches
🍎 Fruit
🍪 Snacks
🥤 Drinks
Whatever is easy to carry and share is perfect.

***

## 🧢 Meetup Details at a Glance

🥾 **Hike:** Approximately 2½ hours + short break
🧺 **Picnic:** 30–40 minutes
🏁 **End Point:** Park's Welcome Centre
💲 **Meetup Fee:** $5 cash or e-transfer
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**

***

## 🎒 What to Bring

💧 Water
🥾 Good walking shoes or hiking shoes
🥪 A snack
🧺 Something small to share for the picnic
🧥 A fall jacket or layers

***

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This hike is great for:

* People who enjoy a little challenge
* Anyone who wants to explore Rouge National Urban Park
* People who love fall colours 🍂
* Hikers looking for a social outing
* Anyone comfortable walking hills and uneven terrain
* People who want to meet others while getting outside

This isn't the easiest walk we do.
**But sometimes the harder walks are the ones you remember.**

You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**

Questions? Post on the event wall or email **torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com**

**Come for the hike.**
**Stay for the picnic.**
**Leave with a new connection — and maybe a new friend.** 🍂💛

title: Lost Libraries of the Ancient World (LECTURES - 5TH ANNIVERSARY SPECIAL)
description:
Toronto History Walks
**The Toronto History Walks Explorer Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!**

**The location of this Lecture might change in the next few months so stay tuned for more information regarding the venue! As of now the location will still be Old City Hall at the northeast corner of Queen Street West and Bay Street until further notice.**

We have an amazing "Lecture on the Go" series for 2026/2027. New topics and fascinating stories abound! Join me, and uncover the world and keep active, warm and cool during the winter and summer months!

I started this walking classroom when we were under that horrible cloud called Covid. This series was popular and helped people get back into society and life. The first Lecture on the Go was **Walking North America** and that was in October of 2021. Hard to believe it's been 5 years of lectures. So I wanted to do something special to celebrate 5 years of exploration.

The "Lecture on the Go" Series is open to members who have purchased the YEARLY MEMBERSHIP PASS, it's free for those members. If you wish to attend a lecture and you are not a yearly pass member then the price **per** lecture is $20.00.

Let's get started.

What if some of humanity's greatest discoveries were made thousands of years ago, and then lost forever?

What if entire histories, scientific breakthroughs, literary masterpieces, and eyewitness accounts of the ancient world once existed, only to disappear into the flames of war, and the collapse of civilizations?

Join me for a fascinating journey into the world's lost libraries, from the legendary Library of Alexandria to the vanished collections of ancient empires whose treasures may be lost forever.

At the heart, stands the Library of Alexandria, the most famous library in history. Founded over two thousand years ago, it sought to gather all the knowledge of the known world. Scholars from across the Mediterranean came to study astronomy, mathematics, geography, medicine, philosophy, and literature. Yet one of history's greatest mysteries remains: what happened to this remarkable institution, and what priceless knowledge disappeared with it?

Was it destroyed in a single catastrophe, or did it slowly fade away over centuries from neglect?

Beyond Alexandria, we will explore a forgotten world of lost libraries and vanished collections stretching from Mesopotamia and ancient Egypt to medieval Europe, Baghdad, and China. Discover the remarkable stories of librarians, scholars, explorers, and rulers who dedicated their lives to preserving knowledge.

We will encounter lost books, missing histories, ancient scientific works, and literary treasures that survive today only as fragments.
This lecture is an exploration of one of history's most compelling questions: What have we forgotten?

And how libraries shaped civilization and why their loss continues to fascinate us centuries later. Whether you are a lover of history, literature, archaeology, or simply enjoy a good mystery, this special Lecture on the Go will leave you wondering. What secrets of the past may still lie hidden, just waiting to be rediscovered? Fascinating indeed!

Upcoming topics in the 2026 series:

\*Philosophy 1: Great Minds of the Western World: Goethe to Kant! - (2027)
\*Philosophy 2: Great Minds of the Eastern
World: Chuang Tzu to Dalai Lama - (2027)
Legacy of Triangle: How a New York Factory Scandal changed North America - (September 2027)

So book your plans now!

This event is for all levels and walkers, there are a few steps here and there to navigate, but mostly on one level. This event in a non-walking event.

The lecture begins on the steps of Old City Hall at the northeast corner of Bay Street and Queen Street West, and
has a ticket price of $20.00 per person, but **free with the yearly membership pass**.

**Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

description:
Do you want to know how to sew your own clothes? Do you know absolutely nothing about sewing clothes? Barbie and I can help!
There's a lot more that goes into making clothes than poking a string through some cloth. This is a workshop for people who want to sew but have no idea how to get started. Everyone who attends will design a piece of clothing, make the pattern, prepare the fabric, cut the pieces, and hand-stitch it together in a 3-hour period. The catch is that it won't be for you, it'll be for Barbie.
Don't worry though! Once you've seen the process through and learned each step, the skills can be scaled up to whatever dimensions your real body has. Barbie is a convenient model because she's just shy of twelve inches tall, but the process is exactly the same for humans too.

Saturday, October 24, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $80, TBG Members $70 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature-focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.

title: CLOSING RECEPTION of VENUS VS PINK Exhibition presented by Susan N Stewart and Catharina Goldnau
location: Dignam Gallery in the Women's Art Association of Canada,23 Prince Arthur Avenue, Toronto, ON M5R 1B2, Canada
description:
VENUS VS PINK EXHIBITION

Two artists. Two very different worlds. One seriously colourful encounter.

Susan N Stewart brings the heat with bold, vibrant paintings that swing from pure joy and excitement to moments of unexpected calm and serenity.

Catharina Goldnau's VENUS sculptures are a different kind of force. Each figure is hand-crafted from custom clay, capturing a distinct emotional state — raw, imperfect, powerful, and unapologetically human. And holding it all together?
A solid foundation of Canadian Shield rock.


Paint meets clay. Colour meets earth. Pink meets Venus.

Come see what happens when these worlds collide at the Dignam Gallery in the Women's Art Association of Canada! Talk to the incredible artists and enjoy the beautiful space with refreshments on Saturday October 24th, 2026 from 1-4PM.


ARTIST STATEMENTS

Susan N Stewart

"PINK PUTS UP A FIGHT"

After two months of artistic combat and a mounting body count of discarded paintings, I was ambushed by PINK.

PINK was everything I distrusted: frivolous, girlish, cheerful and entirely lacking in gravitas.

I attacked with brushes, scrapers and considerable indignation. PINK retaliated with MAGENTA.

The battle was ugly. The casualties were numerous.

Then something unexpected happened. I finally began to like my paintings.

PINK has since retained legal counsel and is demanding full credit.


Catharina Goldnau

At the heart of my sculptural practice is femininity in all its messy, magnificent complexity. My Venuses aren’t here to pose, please, or conform. They are raw, imperfect, sensual, vulnerable, and strong — bodies that carry stories, contradictions, and the marks of being human.

As a mother of two daughters and grandmother to five girls, I’m deeply invested in how we experience girlhood and womanhood, both physically and psychologically. I draw on lived experience, observation, and intuition to create figures that challenge the polished ideals imposed on the female body.

I’m interested in what happens when we stop trying to fix, flatten, or idealize women — and start seeing them as they are. My work is an invitation to question who gets to define beauty, to embrace imperfection, and to claim the freedom to inhabit our bodies on our own terms.

location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:

About Linda Borris
Linda is a Toronto-based artist, specializing in watercolour painting techniques. She focuses on her interests in botanical studies and constantly strives to discover interesting ways to portray her work. Linda’s painting compositions depict her particular attention to detail. Her art generally consists of bright, bold colours and forms. Mostly working with florals, Linda occasionally completes a fun landscape. Her paintings’ subject matter are usually taken from her own photography images. Linda loves to share her enjoyment in the lively and vibrant world of botanical essences. Her art can be seen in both group exhibits and separate venues.
 
She is a member of the Beach Guild of Fine Art and former member of Botanical Artists of Canada.
 
Also visit Linda’s work on Instagram: @watercolourslinda

title: The Sultan and the Detective: Sherlock Holmes’ Curious Adventures in the Ottoman Empire
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall, Ground floor
description:
The Friends of the Arthur Conan Doyle Collection: 2026 Cameron Hollyer Memorial Lecture
Historical fact: the last great Ottoman sultan, Abdülhamid II, fell asleep each night to the adventures of Sherlock Holmes, read aloud to him by a palace attendant. This unlikely obsession is the starting point for Andrew Finkel's novel
The Adventure of the Second Wife.
In this talk, Finkel explores how the world of Arthur Conan Doyle intersected with the late Ottoman Empire, and what this reveals about storytelling, translation, and the unexpected ways stories travel across languages, cultures, and empires to take on meanings the author never intended.
Andrew Finkel is a journalist and author who has reported from Turkey for major international outlets including
The Times, The Economist, TIME, CNN,
and
The New York Times
. He co-founded Platform24 (P24), an Istanbul-based NGO that supports independent journalism and freedom of expression, and is the author of
Turkey: What Everyone Needs to Know
.
Admission is Free. All are welcome. Please note, refreshments will be provided at this event.

title: Série Portraits et autoportraits: Quand la représentation sociale cède la place aux sentiments.
description:
Du Néoclassicisme à l’Académisme, de David à Ingres, les commandes de portraits furent souvent le moyen d’affirmer son rang dans la société. Du Romantisme à l’Impressionnisme, une sensibilité nouvelle se fait jour : l’on pose en communion avec la nature et non plus dans la magnificence de sa demeure, les regards traduisent des sentiments (Renoir) et non plus une volonté de puissance, les gestes sont spontanés (Degas, Manet) et non plus codifiés. Quant aux artistes, ils valorisent, dans leurs autoportraits, l’acte créateur, l’inspiration (Girodet, Delacroix), voire les tourments intérieurs (Courbet, Baudelaire).
Cette conférence vous est proposée par Gilles Genty, historien de l’art, en partenariat avec l’
Alliance française de Toronto
.
Accessibilité:
Le sous-titrage en direct ou automatique, l’interprétation en langue des signes, les services d’intervenant, ou les services d’accompagnement sont disponibles sur demande. Veuillez soumettre votre demande au moins deux semaines à l’avance à : tpl.ca/accessibility-events

title: Water Marbling Bookmarks Workshop
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Immerse yourself in the mesmerizing world of water marbling — an ancient technique of floating pigments on water and transferring them onto paper to create intricate, fluid designs.

Practiced for centuries across the Islamic world, particularly in regions such as Türkiye, Iran, and the Indian subcontinent, water marbling has been used to adorn calligraphy, manuscripts, and decorative papers. In this introductory workshop, you will explore its rich history and cultural significance while mastering traditional tools and methods to produce a variety of classic patterns. Guided step-by-step, you will create between five and eight unique marbled bookmarks to take home — each a one-of-a-kind reflection of colour, movement, and your own creative expression.

The latest film from writer-director Cristian Mungiu is a gripping high-stakes courtroom drama driven by a profound moral dilemma, where private lives are laid bare for public scrutiny. In the latest from masterful Cristian Mungiu (*Graduation,* TIFF ’16; *R.M.N*, TIFF ’22), Lisbet (Renate Reinsve, TIFF ’25’s*Sentimental Value*) and Mihai Gheorghiu (Sebastian Stan, TIFF ’23’s *Dumb Money*) are a conservative Christian couple who’ve relocated from Romania to an isolated Norwegian town with their five children. Unlike their new neighbours, the Gheorghius enforce daily bible study and don’t allow trappings like smartphones and YouTube. title: Halloween in Evil Bloody York - (2026)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

Muddy York, Toronto after 1834 was a **not so innocent** little town as one might think.

It had its share of death and destruction. arson, murder, plenty of murder, and ghost sightings after these events. Wild stories to tell children around the camp fire. But these stories are true. Join me on a walk around old Toronto, and prepare for the Halloween season just ahead.

Have you heard about the Mad Dog of Jarvis street? Or what happened in the old York Town Hall on a day when William Lyon was about to pull the curtain down on the Family Compact, you could say it got very sticky, very quickly.

And after this you could say that people were hooked on all the stories. You could also say that people got hung up on William. Ok enough fun talk, let's go exploring. A walking tour into the dark heart and secrets of the Toronto we all love so much.

Stories that will make your Halloween! And chill your blood. Sounds like a plan!

Let's explore stories of Toronto's bloodiest side!

This walking tour is for all levels and walkers. This tour is for children over the age of 12!

The tour begins on the steps of the Yorkville Library on Yorkville Avenue just west of Yonge Street. The tour ends at King Street East, and Church Street.

And just look for me. I'll be there, or at least my spirit will be.......

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00. Please **book early** as this tour fills up pretty quick.

(Toronto // youth garage-rock duo)


Wavelength is excited to host a gritty, rock-centric night in celebration of Imperial Filth, the new release by Ian Blurton’s Future Now project. Featuring vintage gear and a powerhouse rhythm section, Future Now is a manifestation of Blurton’s 40+ years in the Canadian music scene (Change Of Heart, C’mon, Public Animal).


The seasonally appropriate Ace of Wands brings gothic-glam aesthetics and dreamy fuzz, alongside rural Quebec quintet Tonnerre’s bluesy invocation of nature and what lies beyond. Starting the night is tween brothers Lego Money: a beacon of hope for Gen Alpha everywhere.


Inspired by this next wave of young musicians, Wavelength is delighted to announce the implementation of Pay What You Can youth pricing! Audience members 25 and under can set their own ticket price at Wavelength shows: 25 tickets will be available online and 25 tickets will be available at the door, arrive by 7:30 to claim your spot.


Get your pointer and your pinky finger ready for this multi-generational line-up of rockers!

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: 🍂🌿 NEW FALL WALK: Discover Biidaasige Park 🌿🍂
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 🍂🌿 **NEW FALL WALK: Discover Biidaasige Park** 🌿🍂

### A Brand-New Toronto Park, Fall Colours & Waterfront Trails

We're trying something **new**!

Join us for our first group walk to **Biidaasige Park**, one of the newest and most ambitious parks in Toronto. Opened as part of the massive transformation of the Port Lands, the park sits on **Ookwemin Minising**, Toronto's new island where the Don River meets Lake Ontario.

This isn't a walk we've done before, which makes it a little more exciting. We'll spend much of the afternoon actually **exploring the park rather than rushing through it** — following its trails, enjoying the waterfront, taking in the fall scenery, and stopping along the way to appreciate the new landscape.
The park is enormous, with more than **50 acres already open** and more sections being added as the Port Lands transformation continues.

There are curated trails and paths, viewpoints, natural areas, and places to get down closer to the new Don River.
And because we're doing this in the fall, we'll get to experience the park at a completely different time of year — cooler air, changing leaves, open skies, and fewer summer crowds. 🍂

We'll meet at the **Young Centre in the Distillery District** simply because it's an easy and convenient meeting point before we head toward the park. We won't be spending the day touring the Distillery District — **the park is the destination.**

📲 **Don't Forget to join our WhatsApp Group – [\[CLICK HERE!\]](http://xn--%5Bclick%20here!%5D(%20join%20our%20whatsapp%20group-cu832c:%20Click%20here%20to%20join)/)**

***

## 🚶‍♂️ **What We'll Do**

We'll meet outside the **Young Centre for the Performing Arts** and make our way toward Biidaasige Park.
Once we reach the park, we'll slow things down and spend about **90 minutes exploring the trails and waterfront**.
Along the way we'll:

* 🍂 Enjoy the fall colours
* 🌿 Explore the park's trails and green spaces
* 🌊 Walk along the new waterfront landscape
* 📸 Stop for photos and scenic views
* 🌳 Explore the natural areas around the new Don River
* 🌆 Take in views toward the Toronto skyline and Toronto Islands
* 🚶‍♂️ Enjoy plenty of time to walk and talk with the group

The walk itself will be approximately **2 hours**, but we're not trying to race through it.
**This is about experiencing the park.**
It's our first time doing this walk, so we'll take our time and actually enjoy discovering what has been created here.

***

## 🌊 **Why Biidaasige Park?**

Biidaasige Park is part of one of the biggest transformations Toronto has seen in decades.
The new Don River was created as part of the Port Lands Flood Protection project, transforming former industrial land into a new river valley, wetlands, parkland and public spaces.

The first phase of Biidaasige Park opened in July 2025.
The park includes **accessible trails, cycling paths, river access, wetlands, viewpoints and waterfront promenades**, with views toward the Toronto Islands, Inner Harbour and skyline.

And there's something particularly fun about visiting a place that is still **brand new**.
We're not revisiting an old Toronto favourite.
**We're discovering somewhere new together.**

***

## 🍺 **After the Walk: The Keating Channel Pub & Grill**

After exploring the park, we'll head over to **The Keating Channel Pub & Grill** for lunch.
The pub sits right on the Keating Channel and has been a local fixture in the area for more than 20 years. After years of Port Lands construction made the neighbourhood difficult to reach, the transformation of the area has brought new life and new visitors back to the waterfront.
It's a nice way to finish the day: **a brand-new park followed by one of the neighbourhood's old survivors.**
Lunch is optional, but everyone is welcome to join us.

***

## 🍂 **Fall Weather & Expectations**

This is a **social urban walk**, not a difficult hike.
We'll be walking for approximately two hours, including our time exploring the park, so you should be comfortable being on your feet for that length of time.
Please dress for typical Toronto fall weather. The waterfront can be cooler and windier than other parts of the city, so a warm layer is a good idea.

***

## 🧢 **Meetup Details**

📍 **Meetup Location:** Outside the **Young Centre for the Performing Arts**, 50 Tank House Lane, in the Distillery District. Young Centre for the Performing Arts
🫎 **Look for me in my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time: 11:00 AM sharp**
I will only wait **5 minutes**.
**Early is on time. On time is late.**
🏁 **End Point:** The Keating Channel Pub & Grill

***

## 🎟️ **Meetup Fee**

**$5 cash in person or e-transfer**
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**
This fee helps support the group and allows us to continue organizing walks and events throughout Toronto.

***

## 🎒 **What to Bring**

💧 Water
👟 Comfortable walking shoes
🥪 A snack
🧥 Weather-appropriate clothing
📸 Your phone or camera for photos

***

## 🌈 **Who Is This For?**

This walk is great for:

* People who enjoy discovering new places in Toronto
* Anyone who likes parks and waterfront trails
* People who want a relaxed social walk
* Anyone interested in seeing Toronto's newest public spaces
* People who enjoy exploring somewhere they've never been before
* Anyone who wants to spend a fall day outside with good people

The park may be new.
**The idea is the same: come out, walk with us, and meet some people along the way.**

***

📲 **You're welcome to RSVP ahead of time — or just show up on the day if you're unsure about your schedule.**
Sometimes things happen and events may need to be cancelled or changed, so please keep an eye on the event page for updates.

👤 **Organizer: Mathew**

Questions? Post on the event wall or email:
📧 **torontomoviesandoutings@hotmail.com**

**Come discover a new park.**
**Stay for the fall colours.**
**Stay a little longer for lunch and friendship.** 🍂🌿🍺

description:
Date: Sunday, October 25, 2026
Time: 12:00 pm to 4:00 pm
Location: Bata Shoe Museum
Tickets: Included with General Admission 
Celebrate the opening of our fall exhibition, Brilliant: The Art of Beaded Footwear around the World — an exhibition spanning 400 years of history and five corners of the globe, from Indigenous North America and West Africa to South and Southeast Asia, Europe, and Western fashion. 
Join us for a full afternoon of family-friendly fun, with guided tours through over 85 extraordinary objects, hands-on beading crafts for all ages, and conversations with artists who have dedicated their practice to this meticulous, centuries-old art form. Discover how a single bead — fragile, painstaking, and deeply symbolic — has adorned footwear across cultures, and explore what the future of this remarkable craft might look like. 
A perfect day out for the whole family. Come curious, leave inspired!

location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Discover the beauty and meaning behind Fasayfisa’ — an Arabic term for small, colourful pieces of marble or stone arranged side by side to form a unified design.

Through this hands-on workshop, participants will create a small ornament using vibrant glass tiles, inspired by the intricate patterns found in Islamic art and architecture. Drawing from examples in the Aga Khan Museum Collections, explore how these repeating designs embody harmony, balance, and creativity, a tradition that has flourished for centuries.

title: Colour Impressions: Exploring Gelli Plate Monoprinting Workshop
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Inspired by the Museum’s collections, this hands-on workshop explores the foundational elements of Islamic art, from geometry and proportion to rhythm and ornament, with a particular focus on geometric and floral motifs.

Through guided exploration and mindful experimentation with Gel plate monoprinting, participants will learn techniques such as layering, masking, and texture transfer to create original prints. This relaxed, process-oriented workshop invites reflection on the interplay between colour, form, and pattern, resulting in vibrant, one-of-a-kind works inspired by the timeless beauty of our collections.

title: Embroidery and Watercolor Workshop
location: Cedarvale Park,443 Arlington Avenue, York, ON M6C 3A2, Canada
description:
A beginner-friendly workshop where you'll learn the basics of embroidery and discover how to incorporate watercolour with embroidery to create charming, fall-inspired designs.

No prior experience required; come as you are, and all materials are provided. By the end of the session, you'll take home a cute, small piece of fabric art that you made yourself!

What you'll learn

  * Embroidery basics: Get familiar with embroidery hoops, needles, threads, and how to prepare your fabric.
  * Two foundational stitches: Learn the back stitch and French knot, and practice using them to create simple motifs.
  * Watercolour on fabric: Learn how to use watercolour to create soft washes and colourful backgrounds on fabric.
  * Combining paint & thread: Explore how watercolour and embroidery can work together, and use your painted fabric as a canvas for your stitches.
  * Create your own fall-inspired piece: Bring everything together to embroider a cute autumn or Halloween-inspired motif — think pumpkins, apples, ghosts, and more!

title: Introductory Piano: Adult Learning Circles in 4 Sessions
location: North York Central Library, Auditorium, 2nd floor
description:
Have you ever wanted to learn how to play the piano?
If you are 18 years or older, no age limit, join us for four adult learning circles led by a professional pianist. You will learn the basic piano including note recognition, finger placing, and simple songs. There will be opportunities for one-on-one instruction for each participant on a baby grand piano.
For absolute beginners only. One-time registration for all four sessions starts on Monday, October 5, 2026 at 10am on tpl.ca. Since each session builds on the last and space is limited, we ask that you only register if you can attend all four weeks.
Please do not register if you have previously participated at the piano circles at the Toronto Public Library.
No drop-ins, by registration only.

title: Ghosts of West Toronto - Halloween Event 2026
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

Halloween is the best time to take in the ghosts that haunt our minds and our city. The city is not quite asleep yet and things roam. They cross our paths with the stories we tell. At the core of this tour, two brutal stories that have impacted Toronto, are explored, but have a ghostly following. You could say this tour explores the old stories that stir the blood, even after 150 years.

Toronto is not a squeaky clean polished town, it has plenty to chill the blood. Stories of horror and crime and things that go bump in the night abound.

From the true horror of the Mercer Reformatory to the Central Prison in Liberty Village, and the ghosts of the exhibition grounds, things that should be left alone will be dug up.

Many other unexplained happenings will be talked about, this tour will haunt, or at least you hope so! Well let's get through this one alive.

This walking tour is for all levels and walkers. The tour begins at the TTC Exhibition Streetcar loop at the corner of Dufferin Street, and Springhurst Avenue in Parkdale.

This tour has a ticket price of $15.00 per person.

Hope to see you there. And at the end of the tour hopefully you are still around. Well maybe.....

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket price when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

title: Cylinder Spectrum & Polygon Plexus
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"Cylinder Spectrum" & "Polygon Plexus" are two visual art exhibitions by Toronto artist Angela Julian (Native Torontonian and OCADU graduate). Both shows are located inside the Sun Gallery at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center. The collected works are a group of large scale colorful abstract paintings done in plaster. They range in size, scale, shape, and number, but they are all tied together through the mediums of plaster and acrylic paint.


On one side of the gallery is the show "Cylinder Spectrum", which is a group of acrylic paintings done on distinctly rounded canvases that were covered in layers of mixed-media and plaster. These are shown both as individual works and presented as a group that makeup a larger installation. The circular nature of the canvases and surfaces links the entire show by their rounded nature. On the opposite side of the gallery is the show "Polygon Plexus" which is a group of hand-made canvases and surfaces that were created to form irregular shapes. These outer shapes are deliberately jagged, pointed, elongated, and heavily textured surfaces, and each painting is covered with a either a geometric or abstract pattern. Both exhibitions demonstrate a variety of different color schemes and embrace vibrant, highly-saturated colors.


The Sun Gallery is the twin space to the Star Gallery on the property, and it is an airy and brilliantly lit space with wide sky-lights that allow for beautiful natural day-light. The gallery space is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably the beautiful wooden beams of its ceilings. These are two very fun shows and run until the end of October, 2026.

Upcoming Events | 918 Bathurst Centre for Culture, Arts, Media and Education https://www.918bathurst.com/events

title: The Face is a Landscape
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"The Face is a Landscape" is a visual arts exhibition by Toronto artist Angela Julian. The large body of art features colorful works done in Portraiture. The show is comprised of drawings and paintings created in a highly-detailed contemporary style. She explores painterly and drawn techniques in both wet and dry mediums. The faces are designed using many layers of blended line-work, impressions, and cross-hatchings. She uses very fine brushes and drawing instruments to achieve these micro-techniques that makeup the broader whole of the picture. The works are located in the Star Gallery and fill up the room from floor to ceiling. The subjects of each portrait are all well-known authors, writers, or philosophers by nature. Angela is penning her first book series in the high-fantasy genre, she has included portraits in the show based on writers that had a direct impact on her as a reader and aspiring author. The exhibition is largely a homage to those writers and thinkers who influenced her.


The Star Gallery is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably its beautiful wooden ceilings. The show runs until the end of October 2026, don't miss it!

title: Guilhem Lavaux (University of Waterloo)
description:
Title: From Galaxy Catalogs to the Initial Conditions: Building a Digital Twin of the Nearby Universe

Abstract: In our current cosmological paradigm, every observable structure, from the Milky Way to massive galaxy clusters, grew from a specific realization of primordial gravitational-potential fluctuations. Can we infer the realization that gave rise to the galaxies we observe? And can we evolve it forward to obtain a physical "digital twin" of our cosmic neighborhood?

Modern surveys, including Rubin-LSST, Euclid and DESI, are now mapping millions to billions of galaxies. However, cosmological analyses still rely mostly on two-point statistics, discarding much of the small-scale information. Field-level inference, developed over the past fifteen years, follows a different route: it forward-models the full three-dimensional galaxy field and samples the primordial fluctuations directly.

In this talk, I will present the Manticore digital twins, inferred with the BORG (Bayesian Origin Reconstruction from Galaxies) framework. Manticore-Local is built from the 2M++ galaxy compilation. Manticore-Deep adds the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) to reach redshift 0.7 in a 4 Gpc/h box. A Local Group sibling focuses on the Milky Way and M31. I will first explain what goes into these reconstructions and where the models fall short. I will then show how we validate the twins against independent data, such as cluster masses and galaxy distances. Finally, I will discuss the new answers and new problems emerging from them: the impact on local measurements of the Hubble constant, the mass of the Local Group, and new challenges for the subgrid models of hydrodynamical simulations such as the FLAMINGO suite.

title: Author Talk featuring Sally Hayden
description:
[at Ben McNally Books]
Join us at Ben McNally Books for a special evening with journalist Sally Hayden, former winner of the Irish Book of the Year (
My Fourth Time, We Drowned
), and author of
This is Also a Love Story: A Reporter's Search for Goodness in a Cruel World
.
Sally with be joined in conversation by journalist Katie Engelhart.
Order a copy of
This is Also a Love Story
here.
About the Book
An acclaimed reporter takes us on an unforgettable journey, capturing the human capacity for love and connection against all odds.
We live in an era defined by crisis—whether it be war and displacement, climate collapse, or growing inequality, and how the powerful profit from violence and exploitation. Celebrated foreign correspondent Sally Hayden has spent her career on the frontlines, uncovering some of the darkest moments of our time. Yet even in the face of unimaginable adversity, she’s witnessed the incredible goodness of regular people.
In
This Is Also a Love Story
, Hayden reexamines catastrophe through the love stories she has come across. She introduces us to a mother in northeast Nigeria who risks everything to save her daughter from forced marriage to Boko Haram militants, and to a group of Syrian women who have tirelessly searched for their missing spouses and children, while launching a call for justice. We meet a couple separated by the Russian invasion of Ukraine and read letters from the bereaved to the dead, still being written over a decade after the tsunami that devastated Japan. Through these stories, which crisscross the globe, from Uganda to Lebanon, Ghana, Rwanda and Iraq, she challenges us to reconsider what it means to be alive on this planet today.
What if news was recounted through the prism of the actions and decisions people take for those they love? Would it become harder to dehumanize those who seem different to us?
This Is Also a Love Story
dares us to recognize how innate generosity and self-sacrifice can be found in even the most difficult of times, and—as a result—to question what might be needed to create a better world.
About the Author
Sally Hayden is an Irish journalist focused on migration, conflict, and humanitarian crises. Sally’s work has been featured by
The New York Times, the Irish Times, The Washington Post, Financial Times, The Guardian, CNN International, Al Jazeera, Time, BBC
, and other outlets across the world. Sally’s first book
My Fourth Time, We Drowned
was the winner of the Orwell Prize and the Irish Book of the Year, and was a finalist for the Baillie Gifford Prize and the New York Public Library’s Helene Bernstein Book Award for excellence in journalism.

title: Festival Select: Mad Love (1935) and Mark of the Vampire (1935)
description:
Join the Society and Recreation department of the North York Central Library for monthly screenings of fiction and non-fiction films that push the boundaries of the medium. This month we are showing
Mad Love
(1935) and
Mark of the Vampire
(1935).
Synopsis (Criterion Pictures):
Mad Love
: Doctor Gogol is a renowned surgeon who is obsessed with stage performer Yvonne Orlac. So much so that he he actually goes to the theater every evening just to see her. He is disappointed to learn from her that she is leaving the show to join her husband, famed pianist Stephen Orlac, on a much delayed honeymoon. The Orlacs no sooner set off than they are involved in an accident where Stephen's hands are crushed. She begs Dr. Gogol to do anything to save her husband. He decides to graft new hands to replace those that are crushed and uses those from a recently executed prisoner, Rollo the Knife Thrower. When Stephen regains the use of his hands those around him find that he has also undergone a personality change and is now prone to violent fits of temper. He's also very good at knife throwing.
Mark of the Vampire
: After Sir Karell Borotin is found dead in his study, drained of his blood, the local doctor determines that he was killed by a vampire. The coroner and police Inspector Neumann dismiss the suggestion but a year later, Sir Karell's daughter is attacked and bite marks are found on her throat. Neumann calls in the eminent Professor Zelin who thinks the story of vampires is true. The locals are convinced that Count Mora and his daughter Luna are the perpetrators of the crime, creatures of the night that can turn themselves into bats. There may be another solution however and the Professor sets a trap.
No registration required.

title: Reclayming Space to Build Community
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:
Reclayming Space to Build Community            
                                
    



    
         
    




	

	


			
Events
	







	

	

	


				







	


			

    
        
             
                
                    Mondays October 26 to November 16, 2026
6:00 pm – 8:00 pm
 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    For ages 18+ 
How do we nurture love for ourselves, one another, and our world? 
The simple practice of breath connects us with our shared humanity. Together, we’ll explore how to breathe slower, relaxing into the core of our body, breathing low and slow with clay to be in rhythm with all things. Through clay, breath, and presence we remember a sense of belonging. Moving with the malleability of clay, we connect with our own spirit of generosity and possibility. As a community of practice, we generate spaciousness for all beings, past, present, and future. 
Join us in clayming a sustainable, thriving future for our communities and future generations and, in the process, share wisdom about what thriving means to us now. In this 4-week workshop guided by a Zen Buddhist practitioner and registered art therapist, explore the dance between breath and clay through a series of hand-building exercises designed to awaken you the present moment and encourage you to experience through your senses. Moving with one body, one breath, one human family, we learn to interrupt habits of separation and create space for all to thrive. 

At the end of the workshop we return the clay to its original form, letting go of what was created and ready to begin anew. 
This workshop welcomes everyone, whether you are new to or familiar with clay, breath, and presence.

                    Suzanne Thomson is ceramic artist, registered psychotherapist, and art therapist with over 30 years of experience integrating these practices to facilitate healing, community building and social transformation work. As a practitioner of Zen Buddhism with training in contemplative arts, sensorimotor psychotherapy, narrative therapy, and trauma-informed approaches she offers psychotherapy, clinical supervision, and has taught at the Toronto Art Therapy Institute and the University of Toronto. Transformation by Fire: Women Overcoming Violence Through Clay, a 10-year retrospective at the Gardiner Museum facilitated by Suzanne, won the 2013 OMA Award of Excellence in Exhibitions. title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: The InSECT Program, on Science Education, Citizenship, and Truth
description:
Harry Collins (Cardiff / UCL Institute of Education)
A proposed new interdisciplinary teaching program in which science and engineering students learn alongside arts and humanities students, so that science teaching also becomes an education in democratic knowledge making instead of a purely technical exercise. Over the past half-century, historians, sociologists and philosophers have shown how scientific truth is constructed. From this many have concluded that science should be levelled down and brought into line with social values. We argue the opposite: science is an institution committed to correspondence truth about the observable world and to the moral duty of scientists to report their findings honestly. This makes science a model for democratic decision making and a bulwark against populists and autocrats, who are trying to erode truth in order to redefine ‘the will of the people’ however they please.
This is a virtual event as our speaker is joining us from the UK; please register in advance by emailing stsadmin@yorku.ca ( mailto:stsadmin@yorku.ca ) to receive meeting link.

title: Bill Unruh (UBC)
description:
Title: Black Holes-- Entropy container or creator

Abstract: The usual model of a black hole is that after it has been created it contains entropy proportional to M^2, (or 1/4 the surface area of the horizon). It is like the cooling off of a hot lump of coal or the emission of radiation by a hot black body radiator. I will argue that a better analogy is an amplifier (like in your radio) for which there is a constant flux of radiation which is created by the amplification process, but which does not have a large internal
entropy which slowly leaks out. I will illustrate this by a simple, exactly solvable model of an amplifier and of a 2-D black hole.
Host: Anupam Mazumdar

title: Cylinder Spectrum & Polygon Plexus
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"Cylinder Spectrum" & "Polygon Plexus" are two visual art exhibitions by Toronto artist Angela Julian (Native Torontonian and OCADU graduate). Both shows are located inside the Sun Gallery at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center. The collected works are a group of large scale colorful abstract paintings done in plaster. They range in size, scale, shape, and number, but they are all tied together through the mediums of plaster and acrylic paint.


On one side of the gallery is the show "Cylinder Spectrum", which is a group of acrylic paintings done on distinctly rounded canvases that were covered in layers of mixed-media and plaster. These are shown both as individual works and presented as a group that makeup a larger installation. The circular nature of the canvases and surfaces links the entire show by their rounded nature. On the opposite side of the gallery is the show "Polygon Plexus" which is a group of hand-made canvases and surfaces that were created to form irregular shapes. These outer shapes are deliberately jagged, pointed, elongated, and heavily textured surfaces, and each painting is covered with a either a geometric or abstract pattern. Both exhibitions demonstrate a variety of different color schemes and embrace vibrant, highly-saturated colors.


The Sun Gallery is the twin space to the Star Gallery on the property, and it is an airy and brilliantly lit space with wide sky-lights that allow for beautiful natural day-light. The gallery space is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably the beautiful wooden beams of its ceilings. These are two very fun shows and run until the end of October, 2026.

title: The Face is a Landscape
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"The Face is a Landscape" is a visual arts exhibition by Toronto artist Angela Julian. The large body of art features colorful works done in Portraiture. The show is comprised of drawings and paintings created in a highly-detailed contemporary style. She explores painterly and drawn techniques in both wet and dry mediums. The faces are designed using many layers of blended line-work, impressions, and cross-hatchings. She uses very fine brushes and drawing instruments to achieve these micro-techniques that makeup the broader whole of the picture. The works are located in the Star Gallery and fill up the room from floor to ceiling. The subjects of each portrait are all well-known authors, writers, or philosophers by nature. Angela is penning her first book series in the high-fantasy genre, she has included portraits in the show based on writers that had a direct impact on her as a reader and aspiring author. The exhibition is largely a homage to those writers and thinkers who influenced her.


The Star Gallery is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably its beautiful wooden ceilings. The show runs until the end of October 2026, don't miss it!

title: Climate Talks Water, Canada-Germany: Road to the UN Water Conference
location: Executive Dining Room, ELC | Seymour Schulich Building, Keele Campus
description:
York University, in collaboration with the Embassy and Consulates of Germany in Canada, will bring together Canadian and German experts for an afternoon of conversations on water sustainability, climate resilience and innovation.
As we look ahead to the 2026 UN Water Conference in Abu Dhabi, the event will explore how emerging technologies, data and AI can contribute to more sustainable water management and strengthen international cooperation.
The event will feature York University researchers Satinder Kaur Brar, Sapna Sharma and Usman Khan, alongside Diana Nenz from Germany’s Federal Ministry for the Environment and Mark Fisher, President of the Canadian Water Agency. Expert contributions will also come from Katherine Balpataky (DataStream), Henning Oppel (Okeanos), Heather Crochetiere (Foresight Canada) and Julian Klaus (University of Bonn), bringing together perspectives from research, government, industry and civil society.
Through expert presentations, panel discussions and thematic conversations, participants will exchange ideas, share perspectives and identify opportunities for a water-secure future.
Date: October 27, 2026Time: 1:00 pm to 4:30 pmLocation: Schulich School of Business, York University
RSVP here
For more information, please contact Ellianne Feenstra at ellianne@yorku.ca ( mailto:ellianne@yorku.ca ).

title: Modernize Databases Faster with AI-Assisted Migration and Optimization
description:
Microsoft Reactor Toronto
Database modernization has never had a magic button. Migrations can take weeks or months of converting code, resolving incompatibilities, and validating that applications still work as expected. AI is changing that. In this session, we’ll use Visual Studio Code, Microsoft Foundry, and GitHub Copilot to accelerate an end-to-end migration to PostgreSQL on Azure HorizonDB.

We’ll assess the existing application, convert schemas and SQL code, fix migration gaps, and progressively validate data, application logic, business behavior, and workloads.

Through a practical, end-to-end migration, we’ll show how AI can accelerate database modernization and help teams migrate faster and with greater confidence.

description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.

title: NEW EVENT - 👻🌙 The Ghosts of Cabbagetown
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 👻🌙 The Ghosts of Cabbagetown

### A 90-Minute Evening Ghost Walk Through One of Toronto’s Most Historic Neighbourhoods

Cabbagetown has beautiful Victorian houses, quiet streets, old cemeteries, and a history that goes back generations.
It also has ghosts.

Join me for a **90-minute evening walking tour through Cabbagetown**, where we'll explore some of the neighbourhood's strangest stories, unsettling legends, and darker pieces of Toronto's past.

We'll begin beneath the glass of **Allan Gardens**, then make our way through the streets of Cabbagetown, stopping along the way for stories of mysterious creatures, haunted buildings, old prisons, cemeteries, restless spirits, and the people who may never have quite left.
This isn't a traditional history walk.

It's a **ghost tour** — so expect some history, some local legends, a little mystery, and a few stories that are difficult to explain.
And, of course, we'll have a few laughs along the way.

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 👻 What We'll Explore

Our route will take us through some of Cabbagetown's most atmospheric locations, including:
🌿 **Allan Gardens** — ghosts beneath the glass
🐾 **Winchester Square Park** — the strange story of Cabbagetown's Tunnel Monster
🍸 **The Winchester Hotel** — spirits that may have never checked out
🏚️ **Winchester Street** — haunted houses and Victorian secrets
⛓️ **The Don Jail & Bridgepoint** — where the walls remember everything
🐄 **Riverdale Farm** — and its strange connection to the old Don Jail
⚰️ **The Toronto Necropolis** — a city of the dead beneath a city of the living
🕯️ **St. James Town & St. James' Cemetery** — where the living and the dead share the same neighbourhood
And much, much more...

***

## 🌙 What Makes This Tour Different?

This is a **new ghost walk for the group**, created specifically around Cabbagetown.
Rather than simply walking from one location to another, the route has been **curated around the stories** so that each stop connects to the next.

We'll move through the neighbourhood at a comfortable pace, stopping along the way while I share the stories behind the places we're visiting.
Some stories are historical.
Some are local legends.
Some are downright strange.
You'll have to decide for yourself which ones you believe. 👻

***

## 🕯️ A Little About the Tour

This is a **90-minute evening walk**.
We will be walking outdoors throughout the tour and will **not be entering buildings**.
Some locations may be viewed from outside or from nearby public spaces.
Please be respectful of residents, private property, and cemetery grounds as we make our way through the neighbourhood.

***

## 📍 Meetup Details

🕚 **Meeting Time:** 6:30 PM
I will only wait **5 minutes** before we begin.
🫎 **Meeting Location:** Outside the **Palm House at Allan Gardens (this BIG WHITE building)**
Look for me in my **Moose Hat!**
🏁 **End Point:** Parliament Street & Wellesley Street East
🚶 **Walking Time:** Approximately 90 minutes
👻 **Pace:** Comfortable, steady walking pace

***

## 🎟️ Meetup Fee

title: Book Club
description:
Come join the readers at Long Branch each month. We share opinions and thoughts of the books selected. For the Month of October take a look at "Children of the Moon" by Anthony DeSa.
From critically-acclaimed author Anthony De Sa, a raw and compelling story of love, war and the differences that both divide and unite us. In the wispy grasslands of Tanzania in the 1950s, a Maasai woman gives birth to a miracle. The other villagers see the baby as a curse. The baby--a daughter, named Kibo--has skin as white as bone, and from her first moments on earth, she is forced to claim her life in spite of the violence she incites. As she grows, Kibo sheds her identity to become Liloe, and then Po, continuously trying to adjust herself so that she can fit into the world around her. Further south, in Portuguese-controlled Mozambique, a young boy, Ezequiel, has been adopted by two missionaries. Zeca, too, struggles with a lack of acceptance. Not recognized by his Portuguese father's community, or by his Makonde mother's tribe, Zeca lives his life on the borders of both worlds. And when civil war erupts in Mozambique, Zeca must choose what--and who--he is willing to leave behind
No Registration Required. Drop in.
All Welcome

title: Connection Beyond Breath: Living Relationships with Our Dead
description: Queer Death Salon is a virtual community space for all 2SLGBTQIA+ people to come together to discuss death, dying and grief. In this collective conversation, grievers are invited to connect over ways they are or want to be in relation with their dead. This is not an instructional session but rather a container for folks to share and hear about the variety of ways our dead show up in our lives - in dreams, memories, conversations, spaces, through animal sightings, cultural and spiritual practices, etc. - and how ongoing relationships with our dead can transform how we live, in tough, tender, and touching ways. Fueled by years of cultivating relationships with their dead, Case hopes participants leave this conversation both feeling more resourced to build and maintain relationships with theirs, and imagining how we, too, will want to be remembered and connected with when we join them. “Time is queer and so is grief: grief queers time inexorably. Lose a friend and find how the lines between life and death are also a perpetual spectrum. Who knew loving our dead and naming our dying while trying to survive could be so fucking queer? I would love to meet you here.” ‍

title: Moonlight Hike - Ajax Waterfront
description:
GTA Hiking & Stuff
Join us for our second moonlight hike of the season. We plan to post hikes throughout the year during the nights around the full moon. These hikes are all about the energy of the moon. We can share interesting facts about that months full moon.

We will hike at a easy pace doing 5 - 6 km in 2 hrs or less. Please bring a headlamp or a flashlight.

This month we will walk the path along the Ajax waterfront. Watching the moon rise over **Lake Ontario** is quite the experience. The moon looks bigger when it rises because of a trick of perception known as the Moon illusion. Since there will be no obstructions at the waterfront we can put this illusion to the test.

Let's hope it will be clear so we can see the sun at night. The moon can get bright enough to turn off our headlamps while we hike so, if you haven't experienced a night hike, come out and enjoy the adventure. Just don't be the last in line.😬
