title: Seagoing Women: Author Sara Donnelly & Panel Talk with Water Women At Work
description:
Journalist, mariner, and author of
Seagoing Women: At Work
,
Sara Donnelly
, creates captivating portraits of thirty-three women who have built remarkable careers on the water, everything from tugboat operators and commercial fishers to naval architects and whale researchers.
Through vivid first-person accounts, this panel talk will offer a rare glimpse at offshore life: the physical demands, long stretches away from home, ingenuity required in unpredictable conditions and deep sense of purpose shared by those whose lives are tied to the ocean.
Moderated by Donnelly, this panel talk will feature:
Ocean Rutherford
- West Coast Canadian mariner, tugboat deckhand, commercial fisher, and children's book author from Prince Rupert, British Columbia. Ocean Rutherford made headlines in December 2023 as part of the first all-female tugboat crew in SAAM Towage Canada's 70-year history.
Weyla Chipp
s - After raising four children and working as an education assistant in the Sooke School District, Weyla Chipps of the Scia’new First Nation seized the chance to train for a new life at sea: working on anchor handlers in the North Sea and embarking on adventures through the Bermuda Triangle and along the Panama Canal.
Connie Bell-Irving -
Originally from Australia, Connie Bell-Irving became the first woman on the BC coast to command oil barges and later the first in Canada to receive Transport Canada's full endorsement as Supervisor of an Oil Transfer Operation. Today she is part of HaiSea Marine in Kitimat, the world's first partnership of its kind between the Haisla Nation and Seaspan, operating the most sustainable tug fleet in the industry.
Join in to be inspired by the stories and career experiences that highlights determination, skill and resilience in a profession defined by adventure, challenge and reward.
Presented as part of Women's History Month. Please note that the program time is

title: The Lede: A Live Editorial Meeting Experience
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL and the Canadian Journalism Foundation present a special Media Literacy week event!
Three journalists. One front page. Only one story leads.
The Lede pulls back the curtain on a process most people never see: how editors weigh impact, timeliness, public interest and audience relevance under pressure, in real time.
Three journalists from The Globe and Mail, Canada's national newspaper, deputy head of investigations Robyn Doolittle, politics and economy editor Ryan MacDonald and senior visuals editor Solana Cain, will each pitch the story they believe deserves the lead position in tomorrow's news. Editor-in-chief David Walmsley will question their assumptions, challenge their reasoning and make the final call, live, in front of the audience.
The audience does not just watch. Before Walmsley announces his decision, they vote on which story should lead, then see how their judgment compares with his.
Join us for a chance to understand not just what the news is, but how it gets made, and to walk away a sharper, more critical reader of it.
About this event’s guests:
David Walmsley
is
The Globe and Mail
’s editor-in-chief and the current president of the World Editors Forum. He is the co-creator of World News Day, a global day of education involving more than 1,000 publishers across 100 countries explaining the role of journalism and how it can make the world a better place. Under his editorship, The Globe has won the annual Canadian Michener Award for meritorious public service journalism five times and has dominated the annual National Newspaper Awards.
Robyn Doolittle
is the deputy head of investigations at
The Globe and Mail
. Doolittle came to
The Globe
in 2014 to join the investigative unit. After a decade on the i-Team, she spent time in the Report on Business covering corporate law. She has investigated political and business corruption, a series of shootings and arsons targeting Canadian waste giant GFL, the Hockey Canada scandal, gender inequities in the workforce and Canada’s broken freedom of information system as part of the Secret Canada project. Her two books, “Had It Coming – What’s Fair In The Age of #MeToo?,” and “Crazy Town: The Rob Ford Story,” were both national bestsellers.
Ryan MacDonald
is the editor of politics and economy at
The Globe and Mail
, leading a talented team of reporters covering the intersection of business and economic policy, including energy, finance, trade and fiscal matters. Since joining
The Globe
in 2007, MacDonald has held multiple editorial positions and was notably part of the team that won the 2022 CJF Climate Solutions Reporting Award for its narrative-shifting stories on how to re-engineer Canada’s economy to adapt to and capitalize on climate change. Prior to joining
The Globe
, MacDonald served as the national editor at the
Ottawa Citizen
.
Solana Cain
is a senior visuals editor at
The Globe and Mail
, Canada’s national newspaper. She joined
The Globe
through the 2019 summer program, quickly distinguishing herself as a perceptive and composed photo editor. In 2020, Cain helped establish Room Up Front, a mentorship initiative supporting BIPOC photojournalists. The program received a special citation at the 2023 National Newspaper Awards for its significant contribution to Canadian journalism. A dedicated mentor and educator, she actively advises emerging photographers and lectures at Toronto Metropolitan University, Sheridan College, and Loyalist College.

description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.

Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.

title: Cylinder Spectrum & Polygon Plexus
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"Cylinder Spectrum" & "Polygon Plexus" are two visual art exhibitions by Toronto artist Angela Julian (Native Torontonian and OCADU graduate). Both shows are located inside the Sun Gallery at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center. The collected works are a group of large scale colorful abstract paintings done in plaster. They range in size, scale, shape, and number, but they are all tied together through the mediums of plaster and acrylic paint.


On one side of the gallery is the show "Cylinder Spectrum", which is a group of acrylic paintings done on distinctly rounded canvases that were covered in layers of mixed-media and plaster. These are shown both as individual works and presented as a group that makeup a larger installation. The circular nature of the canvases and surfaces links the entire show by their rounded nature. On the opposite side of the gallery is the show "Polygon Plexus" which is a group of hand-made canvases and surfaces that were created to form irregular shapes. These outer shapes are deliberately jagged, pointed, elongated, and heavily textured surfaces, and each painting is covered with a either a geometric or abstract pattern. Both exhibitions demonstrate a variety of different color schemes and embrace vibrant, highly-saturated colors.


The Sun Gallery is the twin space to the Star Gallery on the property, and it is an airy and brilliantly lit space with wide sky-lights that allow for beautiful natural day-light. The gallery space is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably the beautiful wooden beams of its ceilings. These are two very fun shows and run until the end of October, 2026.

Upcoming Events | 918 Bathurst Centre for Culture, Arts, Media and Education https://www.918bathurst.com/events

title: The Face is a Landscape
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"The Face is a Landscape" is a visual arts exhibition by Toronto artist Angela Julian. The large body of art features colorful works done in Portraiture. The show is comprised of drawings and paintings created in a highly-detailed contemporary style. She explores painterly and drawn techniques in both wet and dry mediums. The faces are designed using many layers of blended line-work, impressions, and cross-hatchings. She uses very fine brushes and drawing instruments to achieve these micro-techniques that makeup the broader whole of the picture. The works are located in the Star Gallery and fill up the room from floor to ceiling. The subjects of each portrait are all well-known authors, writers, or philosophers by nature. Angela is penning her first book series in the high-fantasy genre, she has included portraits in the show based on writers that had a direct impact on her as a reader and aspiring author. The exhibition is largely a homage to those writers and thinkers who influenced her.


The Star Gallery is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably its beautiful wooden ceilings. The show runs until the end of October 2026, don't miss it!

title: Maxime Van de Moortel (University of Toronto, Maths Department)
description:
Title: The interior of dynamical black hole

Abstract: The celebrated singularity theorem of Penrose predicts the existence of an incomplete causal geodesic in the interior of a black hole; however, this situation is compatible with the absence of a curvature singularity, e.g., at the Cauchy horizon of a Kerr black hole.

The Strong Cosmic Censorship conjecture, on the other hand, claims the presence of a (curvature) singularity generically, which preserves the deterministic evolution of the Einstein equations: in particular, the Kerr Cauchy horizon is non-generic.

We'll review recent progress towards a proof of the conjecture and towards understanding gravitational collapse for rotating black holes in classical gravity.
Host: Soumendra Kishore Roy

title: Get Things Done with AI: Build Your Own Productivity System
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if your to-do list could check in on you, notice what's been stuck for weeks, and offer to help instead of just sitting there?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll explore a personal productivity system built around an AI agent and a weekly-review practice. See how the agent loads goals, counts what actually got done, flags the items that keep slipping, and drafts next week's plan. It can support without cheerleading, asking "Why has this been stuck for three weeks? Here are your options." You'll try it yourself with a practice set of goals, and leave with the plain-text templates and a clearer map of how an AI might support you, ready to build your own system at home.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start September 9, 2026 at 9:00 AM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached. If you wish to save your work from this hands-on program, please bring your own USB stick.
About the AI Tools Used in This Program
This program includes activities that use agentic AI tools (listed below) on library laptops.
You do not need to create your own account for this program.
Participants are encouraged to follow the Resident’s guidance throughout sessions, which include best practices on using AI.

title: Ideas to Strengthen Democracy
description:
On the heels of the municipal election, this conversation will explore the small steps and giant leaps we could take to make democracy more welcoming, accessible, and sustainable for everyone. As public trust, civic participation, and expectations of government continue to evolve, Canadians are asking important questions about how to strengthen democratic engagement, lower barriers to participation, and create healthier conditions for public service.
This session will bring together people who have served in elected office and government
Moderator and panelists
leadership alongside leading thinkers in democratic innovation and public policy. Drawing on their diverse experiences, they will examine how we can make democracy work better both for the public and for those who choose to serve within it. The discussion will explore how to create more constructive public dialogue, encourage broader participation in civic life, support current and future leaders, and strengthen the institutions that underpin democratic governance.
From rebuilding civic trust and fostering respectful debate to reimagining pathways into public service and revisiting conversations about electoral reform, panelists will share practical ideas for renewing democracy and ensuring it is fit for the challenges and opportunities of the future.
Conversation to be followed by a reception from 7:30-8:30 pm.
Featuring:
Dominique Anglade
, former Deputy Premier of Quebec, former leader of the Quebec Liberal Party, and business community leader;
The Honourable Christine Elliott
, former Deputy Premier of Ontario, former Minister of Health of Ontario, and longtime public servant with decades of experience in provincial politics and public policy;
Peter MacLeod
, founder of MASS LBP and co-author of
Democracy's Second Act: Why Politics Needs the Public
;
Sean Speer
, senior fellow at the University of Toronto's Munk School of Global Affairs and Public Policy, fellow in strategic competitiveness at the Public Policy Forum, and Editor-at-large at The Hub
Moderated by:
Jennifer Hollett, Executive Director, The Walrus
Toronto's municipal election takes place on October 26, 2026. Check out the
KnowYourVote.TO
website and the
Celebrate Democracy
page to learn more about the upcoming election, access important voter resources, and discover more activities and interactive library programs for all ages happening at a branch near you.
This initiative is generously supported by the McConnell Foundation and Max Bell Foundation.

title: Marlon James: The Disappearers
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL presents Booker Prize-winning author Marlon James in conversation with Kamal Al-Solaylee at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon.
In his triumphant return to the Jamaica of his Booker Prize-winning
A Brief History of Seven Killings
, Marlon James delivers
The Disappearers
, an epic, unflinching novel about survival in the aftermath of violence. Written with the language-rich, urgent style that has made James one of the most acclaimed novelists working today, this is a story of men forced to make impossible compromises to survive a society that demands their erasure.
At once a detective story and a searing sociocultural history,
The Disappearers
plunges into the tragic, ongoing consequences of violent homophobia, rendering its characters' inner lives with the vivid imagery, sharp dialogue, and unrelenting energy that have defined James's celebrated body of work.
Join one of the most acclaimed novelists of his generation, in conversation with Kamal Al-Solaylee, for an evening exploring rage, resilience, and the price of queer solidarity in a world built to deny it.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

title: Virtual World Ballet Day 2026: How Stories are Made
description:
Experience Toronto
**Note: You can come and go any time throughout the event and I recommend casting to your TV**

**A global celebration of dance, World Ballet Day returns Thursday, October 29, 2026** (from Wednesday, October 28th through October 29th EDT). This year’s theme explores storytelling, both onstage and behind the scenes, and the preparation that makes creation possible. **World Ballet Day** is an annual celebration of [ballet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballet "Ballet") held since 2014 in October or November. It is a collaboration between major [ballet companies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ballet_company "Ballet company") around the world, which stream live video of their behind-the-scenes preparations in their respective time zones, with the lead co-producer being the Royal Opera House, Covent Garden, London.

This year, **The National Ballet of Canada** will offer a behind-the-scenes look at the creation of *The Beginning of Forever* by Resident Choreographer **David Dawson**, which will have its world wide premiere next June. (An event will be posted). Through in-depth interviews, discover how Dawson creates the space for collaboration and brings a new work to the stage, working alongside composer **Peter Gregson**, Music Director and Principal Conductor **David Briskin** and Artistic Director **Hope Muir**. The National Ballet will also unveil the premiere of a stunning film of Dawson's internationally celebrated pas de deux *On the Nature of Daylight*, directed by **Derrick Belcham**, featuring Principal Dancers **Genevieve Penn Nabity** and **Ben Rudisin**.

Ballet companies worldwide will stream and share content from their individual platforms.

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: Lea Bertucci & Norbert Rodenkirchen + Slow Attack Ensemble
location: Church of the Holy Trinity,10 Trinity Square, Toronto, ON M5G 1B1, Canada
description:
Composer Lea Bertucci brings her newest piece for archaic flutes in 8 channels featuring master flautist Norbert Rodenkirchen to the ethereal environment at Church of the Holy Trinity. Minimalist ambient act Slow Attack Ensemble opens the night.

Norbert Rodenkirchen (of early music ensemble Sequentia) plays a collection of flutes dating from the Renaissance to Medieval to Neolithic in Bertucci’s piece “The Days Pass Quickly Immersed in the Shadow of Eternity”, filtered through an 8 channel array via Lea’s live electronic sequencing. Lush flutters and chattering notes mingle with drone-like breaths and haunting tones that whistle underneath it all. Electronic experimenter Chuck Blazevic's Slow Attack Ensemble creates subtle ambient soundscapes that evolve with the soft creeping drift of errant fog as digital delay pulls playful tones out of sampled guitar notes. Hypnotic sounds stretch and warble as if on some cosmic conveyor belt.

Curated by Tad Michalak.

title: Many Voices: Japanese Languages in Canada
description:
Japanese languages have been spoken in Canada since the late 1800s. From nisei nihongo to language schools to the rise of Japanese as a global language, Many Voices: Japanese Languages in Canada explores how Japanese languages have been used through multiple waves of migration, settlement, and displacement. Featuring ethnographic comics by Dr. Ai Taniguchi based on interviews with Japanese Canadians, the exhibit celebrates the breadth of experience with the language amongst the Japanese Canadian community. The exhibit's companion new media art piece, The Exophonia by Xuan Ye, interrogates the permeability of native and non-native speaker distinctions through the metaphor of a rhizome stemming from linguistic markedness. Check it out here . Many Voices: Japanese Languages in Canada was developed in partnership the Canadian Language Museum and the University of Toronto Mississauga. Please join us for the opening reception on October 29! Find more information here . Images: 2. A Group Portrait of Toronto Japanese Language School, 1960. title: The Exophonia
description:
Xuan Ye’s animation, The Exphonia , transforms the ICNALE corpus, hundreds of L2 (second language) English essays on part‑time jobs and smoking bans, into a living monument to exophony, the act of speaking and writing in a non‑native tongue. Each essay becomes a root system that germinates, forks, and twists in real time. Grammatical deviations and non‑native word combinations physically warp the tendrils and diverge the rhizomes. The metaphor of the rhizome is reimagined as a cross‑cultural ecology in which linguistic markedness is not a flaw, but the very soil from which an astonishing forest emerges. Developed through a residency at the JCCC over the summer of 2026, Exophonia acts as a companion piece to the Many Voices: Japanese Languages in Canada exhibit in the Moriyama Nikkei Heritage Centre, extending its insights on linguistic non-standardness and non-nativeness to our hyper-globalized reality. Artist bio: Xuan Ye makes noise as a compass, navigating the intersections of art, music, and technology. Their practice unfolds across software, sound, image, installation, performance, publication, and teaching, tracing the diffraction and resonance across technological, biological, and ecological systems. Their work has been exhibited at the Centre for Culture and Technology (2025), Kamias Triennial (2024), MOCA Toronto (2022), UCCA Shanghai (2022), Venice Architecture Biennale (2021), MUTEK Montreal (2021), InterAccess (2020), and Goethe-Institut Beijing (2018), among others. They have been recognized with residencies at the Banff Centre for Arts and Creativity (2026), University of Toronto (2025/26), ZHdK (2024), and Pro Helvetia (2023), and have received grants from the Canada Council for the Arts, Ontario Arts Council, Toronto Arts Council, Partners in Art, and SSHRC. Their work has been featured in Peripheral Review, Canadian Art, ArtAsiaPacific, KUNSTFORUM International, and Musicworks. Originally from China, Ye lives in Toronto/Tkaronto and is an Assistant Professor at the University of Waterloo.

title: Cylinder Spectrum & Polygon Plexus
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"Cylinder Spectrum" & "Polygon Plexus" are two visual art exhibitions by Toronto artist Angela Julian (Native Torontonian and OCADU graduate). Both shows are located inside the Sun Gallery at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center. The collected works are a group of large scale colorful abstract paintings done in plaster. They range in size, scale, shape, and number, but they are all tied together through the mediums of plaster and acrylic paint.


On one side of the gallery is the show "Cylinder Spectrum", which is a group of acrylic paintings done on distinctly rounded canvases that were covered in layers of mixed-media and plaster. These are shown both as individual works and presented as a group that makeup a larger installation. The circular nature of the canvases and surfaces links the entire show by their rounded nature. On the opposite side of the gallery is the show "Polygon Plexus" which is a group of hand-made canvases and surfaces that were created to form irregular shapes. These outer shapes are deliberately jagged, pointed, elongated, and heavily textured surfaces, and each painting is covered with a either a geometric or abstract pattern. Both exhibitions demonstrate a variety of different color schemes and embrace vibrant, highly-saturated colors.


The Sun Gallery is the twin space to the Star Gallery on the property, and it is an airy and brilliantly lit space with wide sky-lights that allow for beautiful natural day-light. The gallery space is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably the beautiful wooden beams of its ceilings. These are two very fun shows and run until the end of October, 2026.

title: The Face is a Landscape
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"The Face is a Landscape" is a visual arts exhibition by Toronto artist Angela Julian. The large body of art features colorful works done in Portraiture. The show is comprised of drawings and paintings created in a highly-detailed contemporary style. She explores painterly and drawn techniques in both wet and dry mediums. The faces are designed using many layers of blended line-work, impressions, and cross-hatchings. She uses very fine brushes and drawing instruments to achieve these micro-techniques that makeup the broader whole of the picture. The works are located in the Star Gallery and fill up the room from floor to ceiling. The subjects of each portrait are all well-known authors, writers, or philosophers by nature. Angela is penning her first book series in the high-fantasy genre, she has included portraits in the show based on writers that had a direct impact on her as a reader and aspiring author. The exhibition is largely a homage to those writers and thinkers who influenced her.


The Star Gallery is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably its beautiful wooden ceilings. title: Adrian Bayer (Flatiron Institute, CCA)
description:
Title: Why a Tiny Neutrino Inspired Me to Reconstruct the Entire Universe with AI

Abstract: Measuring neutrino mass is a central goal of particle physics and cosmology. Its imprint on cosmic structure offers a route to that measurement, but extracting this information requires inference that can handle high-dimensional data, expensive simulations, and multimodal datasets. AI is transforming how we address these challenges.

In this talk, I will motivate field-level inference, which uses the full spatial information in cosmic maps to reconstruct the Universe’s initial conditions and optimally infer cosmological parameters. I will show how neural networks improve reconstruction and measurements of baryon acoustic oscillations using data from the DESI galaxy survey, and discuss the challenge of ensuring that AI-based inference remains robust, interpretable, and efficient. I will also showcase recent work using large language models to discover and improve reconstruction algorithms and accelerate science more broadly.

Beyond galaxy surveys, the next generation of cosmological discovery will be defined by combining information from multiple cosmological datasets—including weak lensing and the cosmic microwave background—to tighten constraints, mitigate systematics, and detect otherwise undetectable signals. I will end by highlighting work from the Simons Observatory’s Sky Modeling group to enable such joint analyses and accelerate fundamental physics discovery over the coming decade.

These sessions are designed for seniors with low income and those who advise them.
Registration not required. Drop-in welcome.
Thursday Oct 1: What Do Seniors Get?
Learn about benefits for older adults living in Ontario, including Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Old Age Security (OAS), Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), and Guaranteed Annual Income Supplement (GAINS).
Thursday Oct 15: Understanding the Personal Income Tax System.
What is a taxable income and how can tax credits, deductions, entitlements and exemptions help to reduce taxable income.
Thursday Oct 29: Protecting Your Retirement Income.
Learn how to reduce claw backs to GIS and GAINS payments if receiving additional income from employment, a private pension, or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP).
Thursday Nov 12: Coming to Canada and Leaving Canada.
Learn about eligible benefits for those that resided in Canada for fewer than 40 years between the ages of 18 and 65, or for those planning on emigrating from Canada after retiring.
Thursday Nov 26: Tax Credits and Benefits for Seniors and People with Disabilities.
Learn about other tax credits and benefits for seniors, people with disabilities, and caregivers, including the disability tax credit, the Canada caregiver credit, and the home accessibility tax credit.
One-on-one support is available at select branches. Meet with Financial Empowerment staff for free financial counselling. Book your free appointment today. Speak with branch staff or visit

for more information.

title: Disaster Seminar Series: Five Things I’d Tell My 2018 Self: Reflections on Building a Career in Health Emergency Management
location: 109 Atkinson Building (Harry Crowe Room) @ 4700 Keele Street, York University, North York, ON M3J 1P3, Canada
description:
Join Y-EMERGE for our ongoing Disaster Seminar Series. This session will feature Moira Hennebury, Manager of Emergency Preparedness at Sunnybrook Health Sciences Centre.
Abstract: When Moira Hennebury completed York University’s Master of Disaster and Emergency Management program in December 2018, she was just beginning to envision what a career in emergency management could look like. Since then, she has progressed from intern to analyst, specialist, and manager, supporting dozens of emergency responses and leading high-impact preparedness initiatives across Ontario’s health sector.
Today, Moira leads the Emergency Preparedness team at Sunnybrook, a nationally leading and globally recognized academic health sciences centre, and home to Canada’s first and largest trauma centre. Most recently, she provided leadership for health and medical planning in support of Toronto’s hosting of the FIFA World Cup 2026™. Drawing on lessons learned throughout her career journey, Moira will share five insights she wishes she had known when starting out in the profession. The session will explore how emergency management theory translates into practice, the skills and experiences that matter most in an increasingly complex and evolving field, and the realities of building a meaningful career. Through these reflections, Moira will offer lessons for emerging professionals while highlighting what has sustained her passion for healthcare emergency management over the past eight years.
For more information on the weekly Disaster Seminar Series visit the website: https://www.yorku.ca/research/yemerge/disaster-seminar-series/ ( https://www.yorku.ca/research/yemerge/disaster-seminar-series/ )

title: AI for School: Responsible Success for Teens
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
AI can help with schoolwork. So why does it feel like walking a tightrope? How do you use it for learning without fooling yourself?
In this youth-focused class with our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll learn to use AI as a tutor, quiz partner, and explainer, not an answer machine. You'll practice the tutor loop using provided examples: starting with what your interests are, what you want to learn, how you like to learn, and what you already understand. title: 👻 Ghost Tour of Old Toronto🌙!
description:
Toronto Movies & Social Group - Celebrating 14 Years!
# 👻 Ghost Tour of Old Toronto 🌙

### Haunted Hotels, Dark History & The Ghosts of Downtown

Toronto has a long history — and some of it is considerably darker than the history books make it sound.

Join us for an evening walk through **Old Toronto**, where we'll uncover stories of haunted hotels, gruesome executions, mysterious deaths, and some of the stranger legends that have become part of the city's history.
We'll walk through the downtown core as the city settles into the evening, stopping along the way for stories about the ghosts, tragedies, and unusual events connected to the streets and buildings around us.
And yes, we'll even explore **why Toronto has a long-standing fear of clowns.** 🤡👻

This isn't simply a walk through downtown.
It's a **curated storytelling experience** that looks at some of Toronto's history from a decidedly darker perspective.

📱 Don't forget to join our **WhatsApp Group – [CLICK HERE](https://chat.whatsapp.com/H59mSCbsAi018gYANrKAnc)**

***

## 👻 What We'll Explore

We'll begin outside the **Royal York Hotel** and make our way through Old Toronto toward the **Hockey Hall of Fame**.
Along the way, we'll hear stories about:

* 🤡 **Why Toronto doesn't like clowns**
* 🏨 **The ghosts of downtown's historic hotels**
* 💀 **Gruesome executions and forgotten tragedies**
* 🔫 **A deadly reminder of why you should never play with guns**
* 👻 **Restless spirits and strange encounters**
* 🕯️ And much, much more…

We'll remain outside throughout the experience and **will not be entering the buildings**.

***

## 🕯️ A Little About the Experience

This is one of our **curated ghost walks**, rather than a regular social walk.
I've researched the stories, developed the route, and brought together some of the stranger pieces of Toronto's history to create an evening experience that is part history, part ghost story, and part “what the hell happened here?”
You don't have to believe in ghosts.
**You just have to enjoy a good story.** 👻

***

## 🧢 Meetup Details

📍 **Meetup Location:** In front of the **Royal York Hotel**
🫎 **Look for me in my Moose Hat!**
⏰ **Meetup Time:** **6:30 PM sharp**
I will only wait **5 minutes**.
**Early is on time. On time is late.**
🚶‍♂️ **Pace:** Steady walking pace
🏁 **End Point:** **Hockey Hall of Fame**

***

## 🎟️ Meetup Fee

**$10 cash in person or e-transfer**
📧 **mathewmaclean@hotmail.com**
This is a **curated ghost-walking experience**, rather than one of our regular social walks. The route, stories, and history have been researched and brought together specifically for this experience.
The fee helps support the time and work that goes into creating these walks.

***

## 🎒 What to Bring

👟 Comfortable walking shoes
🧥 Weather-appropriate clothing
💧 Water
📱 Your phone for photos

***

## 🌈 Who Is This For?

This experience is great for:

title: Colour & Atmosphere
description:
Join us for an online special career series with the
2026 Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence
, Elly MacKay! In this series, Elly will share insights into building a career in children’s book illustration, covering topics such as the journey to working as an illustrator, an overview of classic children’s books, portfolios, and colour. Details about each session follow:
Thursday, October 8, 7pm:
Becoming an Illustrator
Elly MacKay shares her early and current work, her career path, and her process for creating miniature 3D worlds. Her talk also covers developing your style, illustration trends, and how to stand out.
Thursday, October 15, 7pm: Looking at Picture Books
Elly MacKay gives an overview of famous picture books, the various styles, what works, and how they’ve changed over the years. She looks at cover design, structure, page turns, and how visual storytelling and words work together.
Thursday, October 22, 7pm: From Portfolio to Book
Elly MacKay discusses portfolios and what to include, as well as working with agents and publishers. She also looks at what goes into creating your first picture book.
Thursday, October 29, 7pm: Colour and Atmosphere
Elly MacKay considers colour in picture books—how it can be used to strengthen a message, or to alter the mood. She looks at how illustrators have used colour in unconventional ways in their books.
Workshops will be recorded and available for replay through Zoom until October 31, 2026.
About Elly MacKay
Elly MacKay is a children’s book author and illustrator and a paper artist. She studied printmaking and illustration at NSCAD University in Halifax and University of Canterbury in Christchurch. Elly creates miniature worlds with drawing, painting and cutting, and photographs them for illustrations in children’s books. She has more than 20 books published in Canada and the US, including The Enchanted Symphony by Julie Andrews and Emma Walton Hamilton, I Am a Meadow Mermaid and The Secret Fawn by Kallie George. Elly is both author and illustrator of Frostfire, In the Clouds and Red Sky at Night and others. She lives with her family in Owen Sound, Ontario.
About the Joanne Fitzgerald Illustrator in Residence Program
The
Illustrator in Residence
program honours the memory of illustrator Joanne Fitzgerald (1956-2011), and is a joint program of IBBY Canada, Toronto Public Library, and the Young Family.

title: Jesse Wente: Tough Lies
location: North York Central Library, Concourse Event Space
description:
Award-winning author Jesse Wente shares his highly-anticipated new book exploring how we can heal from colonialism.
In Tough Lies, Wente explores his own healing path and how it informs what he sees as necessary for reconciliation between Nations, asking us to consider several pressing questions.
What does healing from colonialism look like for First Nations? What about non-Indigenous people? What are the barriers to this healing, and what can we do to move past them?
Through a lens of healing and anti-colonial thought, Wente examines his reaction to incidents that have hit close to home, chronicling his personal journey and what it has taught him about the present and future of reconciliation in Canada.
Jesse Wente speaks with professor Kim Anderson about Tough Lies and the path for healing between Nations.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:
Jesse Wente
Kim Anderson

title: Social Fluency: Halloween Edition 🎃
description:
Try New Things in Toronto!
Halloween weekend is the MOST social event of the year and it’s a time when strangers expect to talk to each other. Let's make sure you're ready.

What do you have planned? A costume party, a bar crawl, a work event, or maybe you’re handing out candy to the neighbors, whatever you are getting up to, the whole weekend is packed with chances to meet people. Our 60-minute live, virtual workshop gets you warmed up before you walk in the door.

**What you’ll walk away with**

**The infinite opener in your pocket.** Costumes, décor, snacks, and the host are all built-in conversation starters. You'll learn how to use them, even if you're not in costume yourself.

**A way to keep the conversation going**. No more "nice costume!" followed by an awkward silence. You'll practice turning small talk into a real conversation (and having fun doing it).

**What to do to make sure you see them again.** The best party conversations usually die on November 1st. You'll learn how to turn a good chat into an actual plan, like a horror movie night, a haunted house, or a post-Halloween brunch.

**What we’ll do**

* Workshop openers live, with real-time feedback on yours
* Practice in small breakout groups
* Learn how to join a group, exit gracefully, and work a room without feeling awkward
* Pick a weekend mission and go try it out

**This is for you if…**

* You love Halloween but get nervous about the social part
* You tend to end up in the corner of the snack table
* You want to turn "we should hang out sometime" into something that actually happens
* You're new in town, rebuilding your social circle, or just ready to meet more people

**Stop sitting on the sidelines of life, jump in and join us!**

description:
Participants will gain a clearer, more grounded understanding of how common misconceptions about the Middle East are formed and why they persist. They will learn to recognize how media narratives, language, and framing shape interpretation, often in subtle ways.
The session will offer practical tools for questioning familiar assumptions, evaluating information more critically, and approaching discussions about the region with greater nuance and context. Presented by Dr. Hamid Yazdi

title: Cylinder Spectrum & Polygon Plexus
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"Cylinder Spectrum" & "Polygon Plexus" are two visual art exhibitions by Toronto artist Angela Julian (Native Torontonian and OCADU graduate). Both shows are located inside the Sun Gallery at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center. The collected works are a group of large scale colorful abstract paintings done in plaster. They range in size, scale, shape, and number, but they are all tied together through the mediums of plaster and acrylic paint.


On one side of the gallery is the show "Cylinder Spectrum", which is a group of acrylic paintings done on distinctly rounded canvases that were covered in layers of mixed-media and plaster. These are shown both as individual works and presented as a group that makeup a larger installation. The circular nature of the canvases and surfaces links the entire show by their rounded nature. On the opposite side of the gallery is the show "Polygon Plexus" which is a group of hand-made canvases and surfaces that were created to form irregular shapes. These outer shapes are deliberately jagged, pointed, elongated, and heavily textured surfaces, and each painting is covered with a either a geometric or abstract pattern. Both exhibitions demonstrate a variety of different color schemes and embrace vibrant, highly-saturated colors.


The Sun Gallery is the twin space to the Star Gallery on the property, and it is an airy and brilliantly lit space with wide sky-lights that allow for beautiful natural day-light. The gallery space is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably the beautiful wooden beams of its ceilings. These are two very fun shows and run until the end of October, 2026.

Upcoming Events | 918 Bathurst Centre for Culture, Arts, Media and Education https://www.918bathurst.com/events

Saffron Maeve
is a Toronto-based critic, film curator, and researcher. A regular contributor to The Globe and Mail, her writing has also appeared in numerous publications.
Pascal Plante
is a Canadian film director and screenwriter from Quebec, whose debut feature film, Fake Tattoos, premiered in 2017. His second film, Nadia, Butterfly, premiered in 2020 in the official selection of the Cannes Film Festival. His third feature film, Red Rooms, garnered widespread critical acclaim.

is a critic, teacher, and author, whose books include critical surveys of the Coen Brothers, Paul Thomas Anderson, and most recently, in Mind Games, the filmmaker David Fincher. title: The Face is a Landscape
location: 918 Bathurst Arts and Culture Center,918 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5R 3G5, Canada
description:
"The Face is a Landscape" is a visual arts exhibition by Toronto artist Angela Julian. The large body of art features colorful works done in Portraiture. The show is comprised of drawings and paintings created in a highly-detailed contemporary style. She explores painterly and drawn techniques in both wet and dry mediums. The faces are designed using many layers of blended line-work, impressions, and cross-hatchings. She uses very fine brushes and drawing instruments to achieve these micro-techniques that makeup the broader whole of the picture. The works are located in the Star Gallery and fill up the room from floor to ceiling. The subjects of each portrait are all well-known authors, writers, or philosophers by nature. Angela is penning her first book series in the high-fantasy genre, she has included portraits in the show based on writers that had a direct impact on her as a reader and aspiring author. The exhibition is largely a homage to those writers and thinkers who influenced her.


The Star Gallery is located at 918 Bathurst Arts & Culture Center in the Annex neighborhood (Bloor / Bathurst area). The center is a historic building in Toronto and was formerly a Buddhist Temple before it became a venue for Arts and Culture. It has an in-house audience that ranges from both broad to local. With many disappearing gallery spaces in Toronto, it proudly boasts its survival and longevity as a space within the landscape of an ever-changing metropolis city. The interior of 918 Bathurst is a mix of modern design elements in conjunction with its preserved historic architecture, notably its beautiful wooden ceilings. The show runs until the end of October 2026, don't miss it!

title: Robotics Institute Seminar: Tongjia Zheng, “Scalable Autonomy: From Robot Swarms to Soft Continuum Robots”
location: Myhal Centre for Engineering Innovation & Entrepreneurship, Room 580, or on Zoom, 55 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5S 0C9, Canada
description:
Scalable Autonomy: From Robot Swarms to Soft Continuum Robots
Join in-person (MY580) or online (Zoom) 
Abstract
My research is motivated by the scalability challenge in autonomous systems. As systems grow in scale—from single robots to large swarms, or from rigid-body mechanisms to infinite-dimensional soft continuum bodies—many traditional methods become impractical. My work addresses this challenge by identifying physics-based, system-level invariances that remain tractable independent of scale, using tools from continuum mechanics, control theory, and applied math.

I will first present a density-based estimation and control framework for robot swarms, inspired by diffusion processes, that drives large robot populations to desired spatial distributions using only local sensing and communication. I will then discuss hydrodynamics-inspired strategies for robot-assisted human evacuation, where a small number of mobile robots guide large crowds through adaptive interaction. Last, I will present a dynamic state estimation framework for soft continuum robots that estimates their distributed states from sparse sensing, based on elastic beam theory and energy principles.
About Tongjia Zheng
Tongjia Zheng is a Postdoctoral Fellow in the Continuum Robotics Laboratory and the Robotics Institute at the University of Toronto and an incoming assistant professor in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at the University of Alberta in January 2027. He received his Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering from the University of Notre Dame in 2024, where he was awarded the department’s Research Excellence Award. He also earned a Master’s degree in Interdisciplinary Mathematics from Notre Dame in 2023. Prior to that, he obtained his Bachelor’s degree in Automation (2015) and a Master’s degree in Control Theory and Control Engineering (2017) from South China University of Technology. His research is motivated by the scalability challenge in autonomous systems, with a current focus on swarm robotics and soft continuum robotics. He is a recipient of the Schmidt AI in Science Postdoctoral Fellowship.

title: Artists in the Library: Origami Lotus Flowers
description:
This is a six-part workshop series that creates a space for exploring belonging and not belonging through conversation and hands-on art-making. Guided by reflective questions, participants engage in practices such as origami with washi, drawing, dyeing, and writing, using the lotus as a shared symbol of transformation and resilience across cultures. The workshops foster an inclusive, supportive environment, particularly for those who feel marginalized or disconnected. The series culminates in a collaborative public floral installation in the library, sharing participants’ work with the wider community.
Led by artists "Being~inbetween"
The workshops are open to youth, ages 13-17, and require no prior artistic experience.

title: October Social: Characters
description:
[Ben McNally Books Social]
Join us for our third social!
This time around we'll be introducing themes to our gatherings, and for October our theme will be Characters!
And, since we'll be gathering so close to Halloween, we invite everyone who is brave enough to come dressed as their favourite literary character! We'll have special prizes for everyone who comes in costume.
Come join us to meet with fellow booklovers, and to talk to them (and us) about your favourite literary characters.
We'll have some nibbles and some drinkies, and we invite you to come join the festivities.
We'll do a bit of a presentation to talk about some our own favourite characters, we'll share some news, as well as some upcoming plans for the shop.
But, more than anything, we wanted to create a space for people to mingle and socialize and get to know fellow booklovers.

title: Adult Horror Movie Screening: The Sixth Sense
description:
Join us for spooky season with a screening of The Sixth Sense (1999) by director M. Night Shyamalan.
Young Cole Sear (Haley Joel Osment) is haunted by a dark secret: he is visited by ghosts. Cole is frightened by visitations from those with unresolved problems who appear from the shadows. He is too afraid to tell anyone about his anguish, except child psychologist Dr. Malcolm Crowe (Bruce Willis). As Dr. Crowe tries to uncover the truth about Cole's supernatural abilities, the consequences for client and therapist are a jolt that awakens them both to something unexplainable.
Runtime: 107 minutes.

title: BOOK READING: THE SUN WILL SHINE ON MY TOMORROW, BY SANDEE MACGREGOR
description:
📚☀️🌅The book "The Sun Will Shine on My Tomorrow,” by Sandee MacGregor, tells the true story of Dorice Lusuli, a young girl in Nairobi, Kenya, who lost both of her parents and was left facing fear, grief, and uncertainty about what would come next. Through the care of her grandmother and the support of a caring village, Baba Nyumbani, she found the food, school fees, and protection she needed, along with a renewed sense of hope for her future.
Sandee Macgregor is a Canadian author based in Southern Ontario. Trained as a teacher, she is the author of two bestselling devotionals as well as two children’s books, "Lucy's Adoption Story" and "Can I Take It to Heaven?"
Meet the author and learn about Dorice's story of resilience growing up as an orphan and about the organization that supported every step of the way.
Free to attend. All are welcome! #ReadDifferently📚

title: Native Plant Series: Collecting Native Seed
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for an engaging workshop where you’ll learn about biodiversity, native plants and how to enhance your garden!
Nature needs your help and it’s as simple as using native plants in your garden! Biodiversity, the variety of all living things necessary to sustain life, is declining because of climate change, habitat loss from increasing urbanization and agricultural practices. Come understand the importance of native plants, how to grow them to welcome pollinators and enhance the beauty of your garden.
 
Session 1: Collecting Native Seed
Discover a simple and rewarding way to grow your garden while supporting plant diversity! Join us for an engaging workshop on ethical seed collecting, where you’ll learn best practices for gathering and caring for seeds. We’ll head out into the Toronto Botanical Garden for a guided session collecting a limited amount of seed, then return indoors to explore seed cleaning and storage techniques. You will keep the seed you collect. To help you get started, the Toronto Master Gardeners will also share a limited selection of seeds collected earlier in the year.
 
Saturday, October 31, 10 a.m. to 12 p.m.
Registration: Public $20, TBG Members $15 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Tina Cesaroni and Pat Concessi
Toronto Master Gardeners Tina and Pat are transitioning their home gardens to more natural environments, which includes adding native plants, shrubs and trees. They collect seed each fall and grow native plants from seed for their own gardens and to share with their communities.
 
About Toronto Master Gardeners
Toronto Master Gardeners (TMG) is a volunteer not-for-profit organization that shares current, science-based horticultural information with the gardening public through various channels, including in person, in print, through the media, and online. Our committed volunteers support and inspire the community, and continually update the sound knowledge required to help them. Learn more and ask your questions Toronto Master Gardeners – Helping Gardeners.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Additional Program Information



Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.
To learn more about the Toronto Botanical Garden and our programs, please review our list of Frequently Asked Questions.

title: Survivalist Series: Introduction to Firecraft
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fire-craft-intro-4)**
***Discover the ancient art of safely creating and maintaining fire without lighters or matches!***
For thousands of years, fire has been our greatest ally for warmth, safety, cooking, and survival. But in the wild, fire doesn’t come easy. It takes knowledge, patience, and the right technique.
We are back for the fourth installment of this popular course to teach you the beautiful art of fire. You’ll begin to master the craft with hands-on guidance from our expert firecraft instructor - guide Kyle.
You'll be shown and encouraged to practice:
1\. Ferrocerium rod techniques with multiple tinders
2\. Traditional flint & steel fire lighting
3\. The art of hand\-drill friction fire
This course will give you the foundation to create fire anywhere, anytime.
**Included:** Your own high-quality ferro rod to take home and keep the fire burning wherever you go.
**Who It’s For:** This course is for beginners and intermediate survivalists alike. Bring your curiosity, a willingness to learn, and a love of getting outside. This is an amazing opportunity not only to learn from our expert, but it's a fun, practical lesson at a uniquely low price.
**About this series:** The Survivalist Series is an expert-led set of courses designed to develop applicable and life-saving skills in the outdoors. Keep your eyes peeled for more courses on many other topics coming soon!
**Due to the cost of parking at Bronte Creek, WU transport is recommended for this course.**
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**Ancient techniques:** Learn unique firecraft techniques from long ago that do not need matches or a lighter.
**Survivalist skills training:** Develop essential skills to survive and thrive in the wild.
**Fire kit included:** Every participant gets this kit including a ferro rod and variety of tinders.
**Itinerary**
**10:00** \- Shuttle leaves from near Keele station
**11:00** \- Arrive at course location
**11:00 - 16:00** \- Introduction to fire craft course
**16:00 - 17:00** \- Drive back to Toronto
**Event cost: $104+HST. $20 optional transport also available. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/fire-craft-intro-4)**
**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.
Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.

title: Botanical Drypoint Printmaking
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fun-filled afternoon of drypoint printmaking!
In this hands-on workshop, you’ll be creating an edition of 5 original prints using a printmaking technique called drypoint. This medium is similar to etching, but it’s far safer because no dangerous acids are involved. Rembrandt is a well known Old Master who excelled at both drypoint and etching.
 
For botanical subject matter, please bring sketches and line drawings for inspiration and reference. The image needs to measure 4×6 inches; you’ll learn how to incise the image onto a printing plate using a drypoint needle. If you’re stuck for ideas on what to create, there will be pressed leaves available which make lovely subjects. You’ll also learn how to ink the plate and work with an old-fashioned mechanical printing press.
 
Drypoint gets messy, so please wear old clothes or bring an apron. Also, please bring a pair of dishwashing gloves.
 
Saturday, October 31, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $75, TBG Members $65 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature-focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Additional Program Information

For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.

title: Real Ghosts: A Hallowe'en Exclusive
description:
Putting the ‘boo’ in ‘book’, author Peter Roe (
Haunted Town Halls
,
The Complete Paranormal  Investigation Handbook
) will manifest at the Mimico Centennial Library, for an exclusive Hallowe’en visit Saturday, October 31st, at 2:30 pm sharing
The Searcher Group’
s true-life discoveries from the field of ghost investigation.
Over 30 years before reality TV inspired thousands of thrill-seeking groups worldwide,
The Searcher Group
– Canada’s oldest, most reputable and accomplished paranormal research team – celebrates its 47
th
Anniversary in 2026!
Mixing chills, a deep appreciation of Ontario’s vanishing heritage and thought-provoking discussion with a dash of humour, this popular presentation returns discussing tools-of-the-trade, original theory on life-after-life phenomena and rarely-seen ghost photos!
Skeptics and the curious alike are all welcome to attend this judgment-free Hallowe’en event. Bring your own inquiries and experiences to a Q&A following the hour-long talk!
For early attendees eager to secure a seat, a Pre-Show video will start at 2:00 pm, to set the mood.
Copies of
Haunted Town Halls
($20) and/or
The Complete Paranormal Investigation Handbook
($30) will be available for sale and signing with no obligation to purchase. Cash only, please.
*Please Note: Video recordings of this presentation are not permitted, thank you.
About the Presenter
As Assistant Director of The Searcher Group (TSG), Peter Roe also serves as Director of TSG subdivision, Mortal Coil Paranormal (MCP), serving the Greater Toronto Area and southwestern Ontario.
When he is not spearheading investigations and conducting research, he is actively promoting TSG’s pro bono services, publicly presenting field discoveries and advocating against Ontario’s rapidly vanishing heritage.
Peter has appeared in a testimonial capacity over two seasons of the Travel Channel’s Fear the Woods (aka Evil Encounters on T+E Channel), been interviewed by CBC Radio and the Paranormal UK Network, and has earned worldwide notoriety with the release of his first nonfiction publication, Haunted Town Halls (Quagmire Press), in 2018.
Peter is co-author of
The Complete Paranormal Investigation Handbook
with Searcher Group founder Richard Palmisano – released August 18, 2025 through Llewellyn Worldwide.
About The Searcher Group
Founded in 1979 by Richard Palmisano, The Searcher Group (TSG) is Canada’s leading team of investigators, researchers and theorists. The Searcher Group’s mission includes investigating alleged paranormal activity, developing and conducting experiments for the advancement of parapsychology, and researching and developing new technologies and theoretic models.
Boasting an ironclad reputation for safety, confidentiality and credibility over the course of 47 years, TSG has had the privilege of working with government officials and operators of recognized, historic public sites alike, in its ongoing quest to discover and contribute answers to humankind’s most enduring questions pertaining to life-after-life and ghost phenomena.
Applying his 37-year career in law enforcement, security and surveillance in the field, Richard is also the author of five nonfiction publications documenting the team’s most harrowing and informative cases, including
Overshadows
(2003),
Journeys into the Unknown
(2006),
Ghosts
(2009),
Ghosts of the Canadian National Exhibition
(2011) and
Meeting Place of the Dead
(2014), all available through Dundurn Press. He has co-authored an advanced paranormal investigation manual with TSG Assistant Director Peter Roe, titled The Complete Paranormal Investigation Handbook released August 18, 2025 through Llewellyn Worldwide.
Richard and his books have been featured on television, radio and internet podcasts worldwide, including A Haunting (Season 1, Discovery Channel), Northern Mysteries, Portal into the Unknown, CBC Radio, Breakfast Television, Darkness Radio, and Crash Course in Awesome, among many others.
The Searcher Group featured as the cover story of the United Church Observer (now
Broadview
) in October 2016* and soon after appeared in Reader’s Digest (April 2017)

title: 🇨🇦Japanese and English Language Exchange  (Page for everyone)
description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)
～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は＄2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は＄5を先払いにて頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

予約受付締切：土曜日15:00PM(当日)

スケジュール

5.15 PM - 5:30PM - チェックイン、グループ分け

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントにお申し込みをされる際、皆様一度ウェイティングリストへ自動的に移動されます。当日のオーガナイザーが人数調整を行い、基本は先着順にてお一人ずつへE-transfer先を記載したメッセージを送ります。こちらでお支払いを確認した後、オーガナイザーが参加者リストへ移動します。一度お支払いされますと、払い戻しや振替は出来ませんのでご了承ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events

Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate

RSVP:
RSVP open: 5:00 PM

RSVP cancel deadline: Saturday, 2:00 PM (day of the event)

RSVP close: Saturday, 3:00 PM (day of the event)

Day of Event:
5:15 PM - 5:30 PM - Check-in and Group placement

5:30 PM - 6:15 PM - Japanese conversation

6:15 PM - 7:00 PM - English conversation

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.
However, Dinner is only for Participants that joined on the day of the event.

Event Location:
Atrium Food Court

The food court is directly connected to the Dundas subway station. Leave the subway station and walk west along Dundas Street.

At the intersection of Bay Street and Dundas Street, you will find an entrance. Proceed down the escalator.

The food court is on the basement floor. Please talk to the organizer with the signboard showing TJEX. (If you can’t find them, please send a message to the organizer.)

⚠️RSVP & Late Policy:
If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List and Fee transfer:
Once you enter the "Waiting-list", we will message you for the payment via e-transfer. After your payment is confirmed, you will be moved to the "Going-list"

There are no Refunds or Carryovers.

Going List:
Only Members on the going-list can participate on the day of the event.

title: THE FAMILY CROW: A Murder Mystery
location: Factory Theatre,125 Bathurst St, Toronto, ON M5V 2R2, Canada
description:
The Family Crow: A Murder Mystery


A MURDER murder mystery - and the 100th performance of an acclaimed Canadian puppet show


Internationally acclaimed puppeteer Adam Francis Proulx returns to Toronto this Halloween for the 100th performance of THE FAMILY CROW: A Murder Mystery at Factory Theatre.


A group of crows is called a murder. So what happens when there is an actual murder amongst a group of crows?


You get a MURDER murder mystery!


Enter Horatio P. Corvus, an increasingly exasperated detective with one hour, five crows, and zero patience. When a murder is committed within a family of crows, Horatio must sort through the evidence, interrogate the suspects and uncover the truth before the killer gets away.


Performed by a singular actor but bringing six characters to life (and death?), The Family Crow is a puppet-fuelled, pun-filled theatrical mystery packed with atmosphere, absurdity and twists. It's a show for anyone who loves a good story, a good pun, and a good old-fashioned whodunit—with a distinctly avian sense of humour.


This special Toronto engagement marks the 100th performance of the show, making Halloween night an especially appropriate time to return to the scene of the crime.


Critics have embraced the show's peculiar combination of puppetry, comedy and mystery. Liz Nicolls of Edmonton called it “weird, cuckoo brilliance” and “a bona fide theatrical caws célèbre,” while Glenn Sumi of NOW Magazine described it as “delightfully atmospheric.” The Saskatoon StarPhoenix declared that audiences would be “crowing about it to all your friends,” while CJSF called it “definitely a must-see.”


The production is directed by Byron Laviolette, a director and dramaturg who has worked with interactive art forms for more than twenty-five years. His work spans clown, puppetry, immersive theatre, audio storytelling and interactive performance. He was the founding Artistic Director of What The Festival, a founding member of Morro and Jasp, and is Resident Director of Pucking Fuppet Co.


About Adam Francis Proulx


Adam Francis Proulx is a Dora-nominated Canadian theatre artist and one of Canada's most sought-after puppeteers. He is best known for his solo shows, including The Family Crow: A Murder Mystery and Baker's Dozen: 12 Angry Puppets, as well as the family musical Emilio's A Million Chameleons, which recently celebrated an Off-Broadway run.


Beyond his own creations, Proulx has appeared in the first Canadian companies of Avenue Q and Disney's Frozen, and has worked across North America. He performs as Fuzz the hamster on the Canadian Screen Award-winning The Fabulous Show with Fay & Fluffy on Family Jr., where he also writes for the series. In 2025, he was a Protégé recipient of the Johanna Metcalf Awards for the Performing Arts.


Event Details

Created by and featuring Adam Francis Proulx

Directed by Byron Laviolette

Factory Theatre Mainstage

125 Bathurst Street, Toronto


Tickets: $31 Early Bird until October 26 · $40 General Admission

Running time: 70 minutes · No intermission

Age recommendation: 14+

Warnings: Flashing lights and loud sounds

JUNO & GRAMMY nominated jazz/hip-hop trumpet playing iconoclast BROWNMAN ALI (Jay-z, Missy Elliot, Kanye West, Guru's Jazzmatazz) will once again lead an all-star quartet through his popular annual HALLOWEEN THRILLER concert, this year travelling up from Brooklyn, NY to various venues (and schools) across Southern Ontario. The much lauded BROWNMAN ELECTRYC TRIO + 1 will perform the entire Michael Jackson "Thriller" recording, interpreted and re-worked in the Miles Davis-esque fashion this multiple National Jazz Award winning improviser has become known for. In addition to the quartet performing Thriller from top to bottom, other MJ classics will be featured through the night for this unique Halloween Series jazz party. Costumes and Thriller video dance moves encouraged!

"Delving so deeply into that record always leaves us speechless", states Ali. Using that brilliant material every year on Halloween, as jump-offs for what we do makes for a party that's both danceable, but still rooted in exploratory improvising and deep reaching solos. We approach it the way Miles might have."

The BROWNMAN ELECTRYC TRIO has won a National Jazz Award, 3 Toronto Independent Music Awards, a SOCAN music award, a CBC Galaxie Rising Star Award, and an International Independent Music Award for "Jazz-Funk album of the year" for their latest release "Gravitation", which hit number 4 on the iTunes USA jazz charts upon it's release.

Heralded as “Canada’s preeminent Jazz trumpeter” by NYC’s Village Voice, Brownman Ali - born on the small Caribbean island of Trinidad, & schooled in NYC - is a multiple award-winning NYC-schooled protégé to his teacher, Grammy-winning trumpet legend, Randy Brecker. Splitting his time between Toronto and New York, he tirelessly leads 8 unique ensembles of his own including the internationally acclaimed Miles Davis influenced BROWNMAN ELECTRYC TRIO, and the award-winning CRUZAO latin-jazz quintet. All these ensembles record under Brownman's own much lauded BROWNTASAURAS RECORDS label, established in 2009. In high demand in the studio world with over 300 CD appearances to date, Brownman delivers stylistically authentic horn playing over a wide range of styles from bebop to hiphop having worked with the likes of Guru's Jazzmatazz (replacing Donald Byrd in that primordial ensemble), Mos Def, KRS-1, Quincy Jones, Paul Simon, Jay-z, Missy Elliot, Mingus Dynasty Big Band, Gary Bartz, Chucho Valdes & far too many more to name here. He is considered to be one of the most unique and provocative improvising trumpet players in the nation today and is widely regarded as a vanguard for the evolution of Jazz in Canada.

"One of the next great voices in the new generation of jazz improvisers”
-- Randy Brecker
