title: Exploring Mount Nemo
description:
Wilderness Union Toronto - Outdoor Adventure and Hiking Club
**Please note the only way to register for this adventure is on [our website.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/mt-nemo-fall-26)**
**Mount Nemo is one of the best parts of the Niagara Escarpment and it's only a short drive from the city!**
We'll follow the Bruce Trail for about 7 km along the top of the ridge, through old forest that grows right up to the cliff’s edge. Within a few minutes, while immersed in this UNESCO biosphere reserve, Toronto feels a lot further away than it is.
This isn't a simple stroll but it is accessible for anybody wanting to get into hiking. The ground is broken up in the best way, with rock, roots and the odd scramble, and the route keeps changing character as we go.
November is a good month to do it. The trail is quieter than in peak fall colour season, and depending on the year some leaves may still be hanging on. Most people arrive not knowing anyone, and by the time we're back at the cars you'll likely have a few new trail friends.
**Accessibility**
Wilderness Union is committed to making our adventures as accessible as possible. If you wish to make an accommodation request relating to a disability or provide feedback, please do so by sending an email to info@wildernessunion.com
**Highlights**
**Close to the City:** It's an hour drive from Toronto, which makes this one of the easiest ways to get onto the escarpment.
**Views:** Whatever colour is left in the forest, set against the dark green of the cedars. Bare branches also mean longer sightlines across the valley.
**Meet Your Crew:** A day on the trail with fellow members of the WU crew, and a few new people to plan the next hike with.
**Itinerary**
**10:00** \- Shuttle leaves from near Keele Station
**10:00 - 11:00** \- Drive to trail head
**11:00 - 15:30** \- Hike the trail with a stop for lunch along the way
**15:30 - 16:30** \- Drive back to Toronto
**Event cost: $55+HST. $40 optional transport also available. Please register [here.](https://www.wildernessunion.com/adventures/mt-nemo-fall-26)**
**About Wilderness Union**
Wilderness Union is deliberate about building an outdoors community that connects you to the life-changing magic of the outdoors and helps you find your people.
Members range from 20-40 years old. The group is a mix of GTA locals and newcomers to Toronto from within Canada and abroad.
Attendance numbers on Meetup don't reflect our actual event attendance - we typically have 15-20 community members at each event. Large enough that there's someone new to meet but small enough that it's not overwhelming!
***Learn more at our website [www.wildernessunion.com](https://www.wildernessunion.com/)***

title: Fall Hiking - Hockley Valley - 13km
description: PLEASE NOTE THE CLOCKS FALL BACK AT MIDNIGHT NOVEMBER 1ST PLEASE MAKE SURE YOU TAKE THIS INTO ACCOUNT WHEN DECIDING WHEN TO LEAVE. This hike takes you through three loops in the Hockley Valley Nature Reserve. Hockley Valley is very hilly with some rolling sections. A good cardio workout Free parking in Bruce Trail lot located on Hockley Road east of the trailhead. Distance: 13 km Pace: Moderate (~4 km/hr) Terrain: Moderate - some hills and/or poor footing. title: Jon is taking you on a 18km hike! Be Prepared!
description:
These Boots Are Made for Hiking
**Meetup Point: 1401 Brock Rd, Uxbridge, ON L0C 1A0**

While we have done this area before, this is a new trail and a long one. It will be a full 18km hike at a reasonable pace so come prepared for a good days hike. The trail is really pretty and peaceful so it makes for a great full day hike outdoors. There are some hills but its the perfect way to get you ready for winter hiking as we hike all year, rains, shine, sleet or snow like the postman!

This is not a beginner hike. Its not that difficult but you do need stamina to go the distance. Come with good shoes, plenty of water and snacks!
source: Meetup: These Boots Are Made for Hiking

title: English Spanish Language Conversation
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** here **»** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
**Héctor Fuentes**

title: Toronto East Weekend Gaming @ Face-to-Face Games
description:
Toronto Heavy Boardgamers
Welcome to the Sunday meetup for Toronto Heavy Boardgamers @ Face-to-Face Games!

The purpose of this event is to meet up to play heavier / longer board games, and have fun while doing it! We will start off small and if there is sufficient interest we will add capacity for future events.

**Scheduling details:**

\- If you have a specific game that you would like to post for\, feel free to do so in comments\. In your post\, include the name of the game\, number of players needed for the game\, whether you are offering a teach or not\, and the start time \(please try to start before noon if possible\)\.

\- If you would like to join a specific game that has already been posted\, feel free to comment on it confirming your participation\. Make sure you have noted the details posted by the host\.

\- You are of course also welcome to organize / join games onsite on the day itself\, assuming sufficient players / tables are available

**Rules around COVID:**

\- Given this is a public event\, we respectfully ask that only i\) fully vaccinated individuals\, and ii\) those not exhibiting any COVID symptoms\, participate\. This requirement may change in the future based on provincial guidelines and group requirements

**Admission Fee:**

\- There are no table fees for this event

title: Branch Art Exhibit: My Red Is Not Your Red by Francesco Leka
description:
Throughout the month of November, the works of artist Francesco Leka are on display at Northern District library.
Francesco Leka is a self-taught Canadian artist from Toronto who balances his artistic practice with his studies in Health Sciences at the University of Ottawa. While pursuing a future career in medicine, he continues to develop his art independently and with dedication.
"In my work, I find in witnessing viewers interpret the densely packed symbolic elements into their own narratives. Conceptually, my works explore the illusions people cling to—nostalgia, order, wealth—and the harsher truths underlying them. Visually, scenes in my oil paintings draw inspiration from the awe of nature, aesthetic qualities of myths, and my own visual interpretations of music."
This exhibit is part of TPL's
Art Exhibit Space
program. Toronto Public Library provides space for local artists to exhibit their work at locations across the city. These exhibits aim to reflect the diverse cultural interests of the city and its neighborhoods.
The exhibit can be viewed during Northern District library's opening hours.
Free. All are welcome.

title: Electrical Engineering (EE) Program Showcase
location: 125 Bergeron Centre for Engineering Excellence @ 11 Arboretum Ln, North York, ON M3J 2S5, Canada
description:
Electrical Engineering Program Showcase 2026
Discover | Explore | Connect
The Department of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS) at York University’s Lassonde School of Engineering is pleased to present the Electrical Engineering (EE) Program Showcase 2026, an engaging event designed to introduce students to the exciting opportunities, emerging technologies, and real-world applications of electrical engineering.
Date: Monday, November 2, 2026Time: 10:00 a.m. – 3:00 p.m.Location: BRG 125, York University
Organized by Professor Ebrahim Ghafar-Zadeh, Undergraduate Program Director in Engineering, the showcase will feature 10 faculty presentations, live demonstrations, laboratory tours, and interactive discussions highlighting research and innovation across electrical engineering.
Participants will explore a wide range of topics, including communications, control systems, optoelectronics, analog and digital electronics, artificial intelligence on chips, power electronics, electric vehicles, wearable and implantable devices, and biomedical engineering.
The event will provide a valuable opportunity for students, particularly first-year engineering students, to discover the breadth of electrical engineering, learn about research and career pathways, interact with faculty members and graduate students, and experience cutting-edge technologies through demonstrations and laboratory visits.
Complimentary lunch and networking opportunities will be provided, allowing attendees to connect with faculty, graduate students, and peers in an informal and welcoming environment.
All first-year engineering students are especially encouraged to attend. Students from other years who are interested in electrical engineering are also welcome.
Registration: Scan the QR code on the event flyer to reserve your spot.
Join us to discover how electrical engineering is shaping a smarter, healthier, and more sustainable future!
Be Inspired. Discover Opportunities. Shape the Future.

title: Python Essentials 1 Learning Circle
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.
Python Essentials 1
In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x).

title: Inside Engineering Minds: A conversation with Som Seif
location: Faculty Club, 41 Willcocks Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5S 3G3, Canada
description:
Register now!
					
	
	Where can an engineering degree take you? 
Join Dean Chris Yip for an exclusive conversation with Som Seif (IndE 9T9), founder and CEO of Purpose Investments Inc. and co-founder of Wealthsimple, one of Canada’s most influential entrepreneurs and business leaders. 
Som will reflect on his journey from U of T Engineering student to successful entrepreneur, sharing lessons on leadership, innovation, risk-taking and building a career beyond traditional engineering pathways. 
You’ll have the opportunity to ask your own questions during a live Q&A and connect with fellow students and alumni at a networking reception following the discussion. 
Have questions for Som? Ask them on the registration form! 
	Event details: 
Date: Monday, November 2, 2026
Time: 6:00 p.m. – 8:00 p.m. EST
Location: Faculty Club,41 Willcocks St,Toronto, ON M5S 3G3
Cost: Free, limited tickets available
Refreshments will be available
Register now! Limited tickets available 
	About the speaker 

					
	
	Som Seif,
CEO Purpose Investments Inc.
Som attended the University of Toronto for Engineering. Although he took a more unconventional route to finance, it taught him the core skills of not only how to learn, but more importantly, how to fail yet keep moving forward!
After that, he started a career at RBC Investment Banking. It was a crash course in effort and learning and accelerated his career meaningfully at a very young age – and helped him figure out what he really wanted in his life and career. 
He loves building unique products that people love and that change their lives for the better. But he’s most proud of the people he’s inspired to join him along the way, and the daily effort and constant challenges that come with building a great business. He skips to work every day because he doesn’t see it as work. 
His goal for the future of Purpose has always been to set a high standard that inspires his industry peers and helps move the industry forward. He starts with the mindset that if his customers win, his team wins. He believes leading this industry through innovation can drive systemic change. While it takes time, the ripple effect is profound. 
“My personal definition of success is: happy customers and happy employees.”

title: It Takes Time: producing theatre with The Howland Company
location: Joe G. Green Theatre, Centre for Film and Theatre @ York University, 4700 Keele Street, Toronto, ON
description:
Join us for wide ranging conversation with The Howland Company ( https://howlandcompanytheatre.com/ ) Founding Members Ruth Goodwin, Cam Laurie and Courtney Ch’ng Lancaster, as they discuss the production history of Casimir and Caroline and the gifts and challenges of running a theatre company with your friends.
Date: Monday November 2, 2026
Time: 6:30 pm
Location: Joseph G. Green Theatre
Free Admission
The Howland Company was founded 13 years ago as a vehicle for ten emerging theatre artists to create work for themselves. Since its inception, the company has produced nearly 20 shows at various sizes and scales included the world premiere of Casimir and Caroline, first collectively workshopped in 2015 before premiering in January 2020.
Most recently The Howland Company co-produced Lucy Kirkwood’s The Welkin with Soulpepper and Crows’ Theatre (nominated for 5 2026 Dora Awards), produced Susanna Fournier’s take rimbaud, a new work first commissioned in 2013 (nominated for 5 2026 Dora Awards), and were selected for the 2026 Best of Fringe with YOU CHOOSE: An Improvised Murder Mystery.
We will also share a special sneak peek screening of THAT WHICH IS HEARD, an intimate documentary short that follows actress Shruti Kothari, whose Dora Award–winning performance in Howland’s Casimir and Caroline captivated audiences in January 2020. Just weeks after the show closed — and only days before the pandemic shut down theatres worldwide — Shruti’s life changed dramatically when she suffered a stroke at the age of 30. Her road to recovery and a return to the stage is chronicled in this documentary short directed by Ken Pham and produced by Ruth Goodwin, Kirthiga Rajanayagam and Shruti Kothari.
PARTICIPATING ARTISTS
Ruth Goodwin is a Toronto-based actor, writer, producer and director. She is best known for her roles on Global TV’s Private Eyes and Netflix’s Wedding Season, alongside appearances on Baroness Von Sketch, Workin’ Moms and Murdoch Mysteries and more. She also recently starred opposite Academy Award Winner Adrien Brody in a Super Bowl commercial ranked among the year’s Top 10 by The New York Times.
Ruth is a founding artist of Toronto’s critically acclaimed Howland Company, where her work has earned her numerous Dora Mavor Moore Award nominations, Best of Fringe Awards and a Toronto Theatre Critics Award. She also received a Canadian Comedy Award nomination for her improvised stage show Entrances and Exits, alongside Colin Mochrie, Andrew Phung and Elizabeth Johnston. She has been named a “Top Artist to Watch” by the Toronto Star and NOW Magazine.
Beyond acting, Ruth spent six years as a Segment Producer for CTV’s Canada AM before producing the short film Stuck, which has amassed over 50 million views on Amazon Prime. She made her film directorial debut with The Strangers’ Case, currently streaming on CBC Gem.
Cameron Laurie is a Toronto based actor and theatre producer. He is a Founder and Artistic Leader of The Howland Company, where he has performed in a number of shows including The Welkin, Heroes of the Fourth Turning, Prodigal, Three Sisters, Punk Rock and Casimir & Caroline, for which he won a Dora Mavor Moore Award for Outstanding Ensemble. Other theatre credits include Saving Graceland, The Trials of Maggie Pollock, The Donnelly’s Trilogy, The Drawer Boy, Our Beautiful Sons (Blyth Festival), A Little Closer (The Vault Creation Lab), The Merchant of Venice (Shakespeare Bash’d).

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: Botanical Leaf Painting Workshop: 4-sessions
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a four-week introduction course and learn the basics of botanical leaf painting!
Learn how to paint a realistic oak leaf using watercolour paint and colour pencil. Participants will learn how to mix and layer colour washes in order to create an image that has depth and feels true to life. Our instructor will guide each stage of the process through group demonstrations and provide individual attention. Attendees will observe and paint from actual pressed oak leaves (we will not be copying photos).
 
Beginners welcome. All art materials will be provided.
 
Tuesdays, November 3 through 24, 1 to 3 p.m. (four sessions)
Public $125, TBG Members $110 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Alan Li
Artist and conservationist Alan Li uses pencils, ink and paint to document the wonders of the natural world. Alan’s mission is to build connections to nature through arts-based education. Since 2015, he has been partnering with non-profit environmental organizations to teach nature focused art programs and workshops.
 
Alan was responsible for the successful launch of the Toronto Nature Sketch program in 2018, teaching all of the art lessons during that inaugural year. Nature Sketch is an initiative of Canadian artist Robert Bateman and the Bateman Foundation.
 
In 2019, Alan was a speaker at the annual Ravine Symposium at Toronto Botanical Garden. In his presentation, he shared stories behind ravine-inspired artwork created by himself and a small brigade of volunteer artists. Funds raised through the sale of the artwork were donated to ravine conservation initiatives at the garden.
 
Alan currently teaches Field Sketching, Nature Drawing, and Linocut Printmaking at Toronto Botanical Garden and the High Park Nature Centre.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
 
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: Adult Afternoon Movie - The Choral (2025)
description:
1916. As war rages on the Western Front, the choral society of Ramsden, Yorkshire has lost most of its men to the army. The Choral's ambitious committee, determined to press ahead, decides to recruit local young males to swell their ranks. They must also engage a new chorus master, and despite their suspicions that he has something to hide, their best bet seems to be Dr. Henry Guthrie (Ralph Fiennes) driven, uncompromising, and recently returned from a career in Germany. title: Author Kath Jonathan Presents "The Resistance Painter"
description:
Author, Kath Jonathan presents and discusses the characters, conflicts and family theme of her bestselling novel, “
The Resistance Painter
”. This dual timeline World War II story is set in 1940's Warsaw, Poland and 2010 Toronto, Canada.
The presentation begins with a short reading, then a description of her WWII, dual timeline novel, The Resistance Painter, its main characters, conflicts, themes and questions. More specifically these include the question which haunts the main female characters: How do you live with integrity and compassion in the middle of a war? It’s a question the audience is asked to personally hold in place during the presentation for discussion later. The 1940’s Warsaw narrative centers the young painter, Irena, who joins the Polish resistance army and makes art as a record of war, and later, after a terrible wartime betrayal, continues making art in Toronto as a means of survival.
Drop-In.

title: Let's Make a Graphic Novel! Workshop with Tory Woollcott
description:
Led by the professional cartoonist, Tory Woollcott, this workshop teaches the fundamentals of story outlining and narrative structure as it applies to comics & graphic novels, prose, or even video games! Drop in, limited spots.
Tory Woollcott is a Toronto-based author, illustrator, designer, and educator whose work spans graphic novels, science comics, audio dramas, podcasts, and kids' books. She is the author of Science Comics: The Brain: The Ultimate Thinking Machine (First Second Books), a vibrant and accessible exploration of neuroscience, illustrated by Alex Graudins. Her debut graphic novel, Mirror Mind, is a celebrated autobiography that recounts her experiences growing up with dyslexia. Other notable works include the audio drama Awake with Sparklermonthly, the travel diary Toronto to Tuscany (created in collaboration with Kean Soo), and two successful Kickstarter campaigns: the Tessera Oracle and its follow-up, the Trine Oracle.

title: Protecting Sobriety Through Loss
description: Queer Death Salon is a virtual community space for all 2SLGBTQIA+ people to come together to discuss death, dying and grief. In her life Jackie Clark has seen the overlapping power of queer and recovery communities. Getting sober after a devastating loss and staying sober through another was one of the hardest things She's ever experienced, and it is only through deep connections with other people and a lot of truth telling that She managed. This session is for 2SLGBTQIA+ people in recovery (however they may define it), struggling with substance use, or supporting friends and family through the same, to connect about how death and grief intersect with addiction and recovery. Participants can expect some framing, a grounding meditation, and some prompts for peer-sharing. Participate as much as you’re comfortable (just listening is okay too)! *A note about language and perspective: I, Jackie, will facilitate with deep care and a concerted effort to use language as inclusively as possible. I also understand that everyone’s experiences with both addiction/substance use disorders and with grief are extremely individual. I am not an expert, but a peer with lived experience. * Please feel free to bring your own experience to the table, and also leave behind any perspectives that do not resonate with or serve you. Jackie Clark (she/they) is a queer person from Battersea, Ontario celebrating six years of sobriety. In her professional life she works for a non-profit and on a farm –part of that work is advocating for and building community among queer and trans farmers. Outside of work she fills her days with fostering animals, running in the woods, and spending time with friends. After the loss of her best friend in 2019, she worked towards harm reduction and then addiction recovery, eventually spending a year facilitating meetings for folks recovering from all types of substance use and behavioral addictions. She believes firmly in the wisdom and power of queer community to hold each other safely as we navigate grief. ‍

description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

description: Inside you there are two wolves." Maybe they're both gay. US / International Attendees: This event is priced in CAD. At checkout, you will see the CAD price, but your bank will automatically convert it to your local currency. See tickets for estimated USD conversions! Canadian Locals: If you are based in Canada and experiencing financial barriers, enter promo code CANADALOCAL at checkout to unlock our $20 CAD support tier. --- Live on Zoom. Recording available to ticketholders for 14 days after class! Get the Total Desire Pass to save on all 5 classes in the Psychology & Instinct Winter Electives Series! --- Animal Role Play can be a vehicle for stress relief, structure, silliness, and more - but it can also be a powerful means of exploring and validating the diverse, often-fluid fabrics of gender and sexuality. In this class, we'll take a deep dive into how animal role play can relate to gender and sexuality: Finding your animal headspace/s and how they relate to this lens Solo play self-connection techniques Centering validation (whether that looks loving or humiliating) in our scenes and dynamics Negotiation tips specific to navigating gender Exploration and validation for Handlers, and more. This is a discussion-encouraged class to welcome a tapestry of unique experiences into our content, but can also be enjoyed by just listening in. There will also be a worksheet to help you apply the ideas to your own headspace. Let's discover all the ways to help all animal role players feel empowered and seen. --- Get the Total Desire Pass to save on all 5 classes in the Psychology & Instinct Series! This also includes a FREE month of the new Wolfe Academy of Desire Patreon + 15% off a one-on-one coaching session. If you missed one of the live class date, you'll still get a whole month's access to the class via your free Patreon month! --- About the Instructor Wiley Wolfe (they/them) is a Primal Handler, kink educator, coach, and community organizer based in Toronto, Canada, and the founder of the online kink education platform the Wolfe Academy of Desire. They bring 9+ years of experience as a Pro Dominant and kink professional, over a decade of professional experience screenwriting and developing content for Hollywood film and television, and a BA in Film with a minor in Literature. Their kink workshops have been sought after across the U.S. and Canada, including at Dark Odyssey, Kinkfest, and Westcoast Bound, with their online classes reaching kinksters worldwide. They have worked with hundreds of clients, organized 70+ community events, led support groups, created erotic immersive theatre productions, and more. They are currently pursuing a master’s-equivalent certification in sex coaching, and their personal relationships all center power exchange, queerness, polyamory, and risk-informed consent. Primal and pet play are two of their deepest passions, and they actively use both their Handler and primal headspaces as a way to explore, affirm, and fuck with their own gender alongside those of their playmates'. Their approach is a concoction of creativity, real-life animal research, and our internalized symbolic templates. They delight in guiding both new and experienced players on their journeys, with a particular focus on self-exploration, deepening intention, and personal growth. Access: This class is offered live and online through Zoom. You may need to download the free, basic version of the Zoom app to join. The class will be recorded with the recording available to ticketholders for 14 days. After that time, the recording will be available on Patreon for all tiers that have access to the archive. Recordings will not include any open group shares at the end of class. The handout accompanying this class will be downloadable for ticketholders to keep. In this week’s session of YU & Balance, we will focus on helping students feel more comfortable meeting new people, strengthening the relationships they already have and recognizing what makes a connection healthy and supportive.

Manage social anxiety
Build confidence in social settings
Think intentionally about who they can turn to for support.

title: The spectre of the crowd: Liberal democracy and the fear of the masses
location: HNES 142 @ 4700 Keele St, Toronto, ON M3J 1P3, Canada
description:
EUC Seminar: The spectre of the crowd: Liberal democracy and the fear of the masses with Dr. Hannah Richter
This talk will present key arguments and first findings from ongoing research into the way crowd psychology’s idea of ‘the masses’ has shaped the political imaginary of liberal democracy. At the end of the 19th century, crowd psychologists like Hippolyte Taine, Gabriel Tarde and Gustave Le Bon sought to deduce laws of collective behaviour from the political upheavals of their time. The crowd they presented as the result of their pseudo-scientific investigations was irrational, primitive and readily susceptible to the whisperings of political strongmen. In the following decades, and despite their obvious biases, the political ideas of crowd psychology came to resonate with a diverse group of scholars grappling with fast-paced technological, political and social changes. Amongst them were Joseph Schumpeter, Hannah Arendt and Sigmund Freud. Regardless of whether mass participation is rejected or endorsed, I argue that all three endow the masses with a constitutive, dangerous irrationality that the political community must keep at bay. I will further show how, filtered through the work of José Ortega y Gasset, crowd psychological ideas of mass behaviour shaped the demophobic discourse of the early Mont Pelerin Society meetings, and influenced the economic writings of Friedrich Hayek and Ludwig von Mises. To conclude, I will reflect on the relevance of interrogating the intellectual legacy of crowd psychology’s political ideas in the context of what Cas Mudde has termed the ‘populist zeitgeist,’ in which evaluations of collective political behaviour are ever-present.
Speaker Bio
Hannah Richter is Assistant Professor in Politics at the University of Sussex, UK, where she researches and teaches critical political thought, and Editor-in-Chief of Distinktion: Journal of Social Theory. She is the author of The Politics of Orientation. Deleuze meets Luhmann (SUNY Press, 2023) and Challenging Anthropocene Ontology. Modernity, Ecology and Indigenous Complexities (Bloomsbury, 2024; with E. Randazzo). Her work has been published in academic outlets including the European Journal of Political Theory, the European Journal of Social Theory, Globalizations, International Political Sociology and Political Geography. At the moment, she is working on a project that develops a critical genealogy of how 20th century democratic thinking imagines ‘the masses’.

title: RJC Career Information Session – Interested in structural engineering and building science?
description:
Interested in structural engineering and building science?
Wednesday, November 4, 2026  5-7 p.m.
in BA2155, Bahen Centre
Register: RJC Career Information Session
PIZZA PROVIDED 
Join us on for an industry talk with RJC, one of North America’s premier engineering firms. Since 1948, RJC has expanded from a small structural engineering practice into a multidisciplinary organization delivering innovative solutions across Canada and the United States. 
Come to hear from Duncan Rowe and James Cooper, both U of T alumni and industry professionals, to learn about exciting projects, and explore potential career opportunities. 
Bios
Duncan Rowe (CivE 0T4, MEng 0T9) is a Principal at Read Jones Christoffersen with over 20 years of experience in building envelope design, assessment, and rehabilitation. He holds a Bachelor of Applied Science and a Certificate in Preventative Engineering from the University of Toronto (2004), and a Master’s in Building Science (2010). Since joining RJC in 2007, Duncan has led numerous new construction projects, with a focus on Building Enclosure Commissioning and Durability. Promoted to Project Engineer in 2010, Associate in 2015, and Principal in 2020, Duncan brings deep technical expertise in various building envelope systems. He also serves on the national code commission for Part 5 of the National Building Code. 
James Cooper (CivE 0T5) is a Principal at Read Jones Christoffersen and a Licensed Professional Engineer in Ontario. He graduated with honours from the University of Toronto in 2005 and joined RJC the same year. He became a Project Engineer in 2010, Associate in 2016, and Principal in 2021. James has played a key role in many of RJC’s major rehabilitation and retrofit projects. He is a LEED® Accredited Professional with a specialty in Operations and Maintenance of existing buildings and is currently pursuing certification as a Construction Contract Administrator. He manages projects through all phases—from pre-design to close-out—with a focus on sustainable and effective building performance.

title: Bring Your Problem: Can AI Help?
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
Do you have a recurring problem you think AI might help with? A thing you keep doing by hand that feels like it should be easier? Bring it. If you don't have one, come help your neighbours with theirs.
In this interactive class with our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll learn a simple seven-step way to think about problems: what's annoying you, what you've tried, what AI could actually do, and where it would fail. We'll gather real problems from the room, sort them into groups, and map out what's worth solving with AI, and what's better solved without it. We'll also talk honestly about what an AI fix costs: your money, your time, and sometimes your private information. The problems AI could help with most are often the most personal, and the most personal ones are worth the most care.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.

title: Floral Design Program: Designing with Natural Materials
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Learn how to create stunning arrangements using natural materials!
Each week a different natural material – wood, branches, foliage, and fruit and vegetables – will take centre stage. These elements have always been included in arrangements, but here we will make them the stars of the show! We will study their forms and shapes, textures, sizes, colouring and characteristics to discover the new and exciting ways they can be used. Join us on this journey of discovery.
 
Course fees do not include flowers or supplies. Students are encouraged to find a local flower shop or grocery store to purchase their flowers. A materials list will be e-mailed prior to the start of each class.
 
Prerequisites: Fundamentals I and Fundamentals II.
 
Learn more about our Certificate in Floral Design
Wednesdays November 4, 11, 18, & 25, 6 to 9 p.m.
Public $240, Members $190 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Margaret Taylor
For more than 15 years, Margaret’s passion for flowers has led her to exhibit, judge, demonstrate and teach floral design in Canada and abroad. A recipient of many awards, Margaret’s accolades include two Canada Blooms’ Founder’s Gold Cups for Best in Show. Margaret has also won Best in Show on three occasions at the provincial triennial show and as a result, has been chosen to represent Canada in two world shows. It was her greatest honour to exhibit for Canada both in Boston and in India.
 
Margaret is currently a floral design judge accredited by the Garden Clubs of Ontario, a horticultural judge accredited by the Royal Botanical Gardens and a rose judge accredited by the Canadian Rose Society. Margaret is also a Sogetsu Ikebana teacher and exhibitor. Much lauded for her design acumen by the horticultural community, she is a past president of the Garden Club of Toronto and is a coordinator of floral design studies at Toronto Botanical Garden.

A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

Kensington Market
Stuart Clarfield's feature documentary explores Kensington Market's 160-year history, from it origins as a Victorian suburb of Toronto, to its roots as a Jewish immigrant marketplace to its evolution as a cultural hub for almost every community that calls Toronto home. The film highlights the neighbourhood's vibrant identity and its ongoing struggle against gentrification and development, attempting to preserve the rich bohemian spirit of Kensington, as modern Toronto grows around it. 104 minutes (2024).

title: The Gravity Grand Prix
location: Malvern, Inside the Digital Innovation Hub
description:
Get ready to design, build, and race! This high-speed engineering challenge invites young adults (competing in teams of 2 ages 18-24) to design the ultimate gravity-powered race car. Using professional 3D modeling software and cutting-edge 3D printing technology, your team will compete to see who can conquer the downhill track the fastest. The core of this challenge is physics: maximizing kinetic energy while minimizing friction. How will you transform potential energy into pure speed?🛠️ The Challenge Rules
The Software: All cars must be fully designed from scratch using OnShape. A brief Introduction to the software will be provided.
The Material Limit: To keep the playing field level, your final race car is strictly limited to a maximum of 30 grams of 3D printed filament and 2 tooth picks.
Free Prototyping: Failure is part of engineering! Teams are encouraged to print, test, and redesign. Prototype prints are completely free throughout the design phase.
The Track: A straight, downhill gravity track built for maximum acceleration.
📅 Timeline & Important Dates
Design & Prototyping Week: Nov 4 to Nov 11— Access the DIH, collaborate with your partner, and test your prototypes.
Race Day: Nov 11 (Exactly one week after design week) — Family and friends are welcome to watch the final showdown!
💡 Key Engineering Focus Areas to take home the trophy, your team will need to think critically about:
Aerodynamics & Friction: How will you reduce air resistance and wheel friction to keep your car gliding?
Weight Distribution: How can you strategically place your 30-gram limit to maximize downward momentum?

title: The World Outside these Walls: Toronto's Asylum at 999 Queen Street West*
description:
​Fifty years after its demolition, the shadow of 999 Queen Street West still looms large in Toronto. This presentation explores the asylum's origins as a temporary facility within one of Toronto's first gaols, as well as the personalities and politics that brought such a mammoth building to life. It will also look at its unique architecture, its treatment of patients and its presence as a Victorian tourist attraction.
Presented by Andrew Nablo, historical interpreter at two Toronto History Museums: Colborne Lodge and For York.
Previously advertised as "The Shadow of 999 Queen Street West: Toronto's Lunatic Asylum"

description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

title: Conversation in Spanish & English Practice Online
description:
Language Exchange Toronto - Se Habla English & Spanish
**Spanish Language Conversation Toronto** is part of ***Se Habla.***

“Se Habla” is a leading online community for cultural and linguistic exchange where you can participate in enriching sessions, make new friends, and connect with a growing global network. With 9 Meetup groups across 9 cities in 6 countries, Se Habla is truly open to everyone from Alaska to Patagonia, and from Europe and Asia to Australia. Join us and don’t miss the opportunity to practice with native speakers.

**We have been meeting since June 2020 on the following days:**

* Monday
* Wednesday
* Sunday

With a one-time donation, you can join the meetings as many times as you like and stay as long as you wish.

**Format**
**Conversation Rooms (Everyday and All levels)**
Depending on attendance and nationality, small groups are formed with 4-6 people:

* 2 native English speakers
* 2 native Spanish speakers
* 1 native speaker of another language

The meetings last for 2 hours and are divided into 4 periods:

* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish
* 30 minutes speaking in English
* 30 minutes speaking in Spanish

**Beginner Room (Optional and only Mondays)**
Welcome, English and Spanish beginners.
**Check the English and Spanish lessons** **here »** [https://myspanishclass.xyz/](https://myspanishclass.xyz/)

**Debate Room (Optional and only Wednesday)**
New topic each week.
**Check the discussion topics here »** [https://se-habla.com/category/article/](https://se-habla.com/category/article/)

Please note that **we speak half of the time in English and half in Spanish.** We help each other learn both languages.

**After two hours**, everyone returns to the main room to meet all participants and take a group screenshot. If you have time, you’re welcome to stay and continue the conversation for as long as you like.

**Community**
**We have 9 MeetUp groups meeting at the same time** (Mexico City, Calgary, Vancouver, Toronto, New York, London, Los Angeles, Medellín, and Santiago de Chile). However, during the exchange, you will meet people not only from these cities but also from all over the world.

You can get the link to our 9 MeetUp groups by visiting any of the following pages:
[https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/spanish-meetup/)
[[https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/](https://se-habla.com/english-meetup/)

**One-Time Donation**
For over four years, the meetings were free, but currently I am requesting a **ONE-TIME DONATION** to access the meetings and help to cover the costs of the 9 MeetUp Groups and Zoom.

You can make the one-time donation at the link below. Afterward, PayPal will redirect you to a page where you'll find the Zoom link to join the meeting.
[https://se-habla.com/language-exchange](https://se-habla.com/language-exchange/)

If you have already donated and don't have the Zoom link, please contact me.

**Please don’t hesitate to reach out if you have any further questions.**

See you soon,
Héctor Fuentes

title: A Matter of Feeling: Chinese Ceramics Through the Senses
location: Gardiner Museum, 111 Queen's Park, Toronto, ON, M5S 2C7, Canada
description:
A Matter of Feeling: Chinese Ceramics Through the Senses            
                                    
                                
                        
                                                
                                                        Get Tickets                        
                                            
                
                    
    



	

    
         
    




	


			

    
        
             
                
                    Thursday November 5, 2026
12:00 pm – 1:00 pm ET
Online via Zoom 
Part of the Gardiner Signature Lecture Series
The Ann Walker Bell Lecture 
Speaker: Dr. Laura Vigo, Curator of Asian Art and Archaeology, Montreal Museum of Fine Arts 

                
                    
    



    
         
    




    
        
             
                
                    The Duran Duran song “A Matter of Feeling” seemed to define an era. Strangely enough, it offers an unexpectedly bittersweet point of departure for a talk that, in its own way, circles back in time. In this online lecture, Dr. Laura Vigo will turn to the origins of the Chinese ceramic collection at the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts (MMFA) and the enduring feelings these objects have inspired in those who handled them—potters, users, collectors, and curators alike. She will also consider how attending to these sensory encounters might shift the way we engage with them today. The objects’ appeal has never been simply about beauty or romance. Rather, there is a profound sensuality to ceramics: the sensation of touch, the scent of fired clay, the sound of porcelain when gently struck, and, above all, the pleasure of looking closely. 
These perceptual connotations shaped the collecting practices of figures such as Sir William Van Horne and the museum’s remarkably charismatic first volunteer curator, Cleveland Morgan. Their tales, and the objects they left behind, remind us that collecting ceramics has always been about more than acquiring beautiful commodities. It was, and still is, about cultivating the senses and the imagination, and about bridging past and present through the intimate experience of handling and looking.

                    About the Speaker
                    
                
                
                    Laura Vigo
                    
                
                
                    Laura Vigo is Curator of Asian Art and Archaeology at the Montreal Museum of Fine Arts (MMFA) and an invited curator at the Museum of Asian Art in Turin (MAO), where she co-curated several recent exhibitions and is currently preparing the new galleries dedicated to Chinese material culture. 
At the MMFA, she has developed major exhibitions and collection displays, including the N. Kapany Gallery for Sikh Art, the Asian collections in the Arts of One World wing, and the recent exhibition Tōkaidō: Dreamscapes by Andō Hiroshige. Her previous projects include Egyptian Mummies, Pompeii, and The Warrior Emperor and China’s Terracotta Army, as well as exhibitions exploring Japanese ceramics, artistic diversity, and the museum’s collections. 
Vigo holds a PhD in Chinese Archaeology from SOAS, University of London, and has worked across museums, galleries, and auction houses in Italy, the UK, and Canada. Her interests span from the histories of collecting, the Western construction of Asian art, transcultural narratives, to sensory studies, and digital mediation. She also teaches at the Université de Montréal. 
Her work often brings together museum collections, contemporary artistic practices, and questions about how we encounter objects—and how museums can create new ways of seeing, sensing, and understanding them.

title: Nov 5 - Visual AI Agriculture Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics at the intersection of agriculture and AI.

**Date, Time and Location**

Nov 05, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/visual-ai-agriculture-meetup-november-5-2026)**

Talks will include:

**U-Net Framework for Micro-Scale Surface Damage Segmentation in High-Resolution Soybean Seed Imagery**

Accurate detection of surface-level seed damage is critical for soybean seed quality assurance, yet automated micro-scale damage detection in high-resolution imagery remains an open challenge due to extreme spatial variability in damage scale, severe class imbalance across damage types, and the computational demands of processing ultra-high resolution agricultural imagery at scale. This research addresses the semantic segmentation of fine-grained soybean seed surface defects, such as wrinkles, dark spots, and general surface damage, in 6048 × 4024 pixel images where target damages can be as small as 18 × 18 pixels, using an augmented dataset of 77,000 individual seed images.

To overcome the difficulties of micro-scale detection, spatial sparsity, and class confusion, we propose a two-stage training and dual model inference framework built on an optimized U-Net architecture with a ResNet34 encoder. In the first stage, a damage specialist model is trained using weighted loss functions and a class-balanced approach that prioritizes damage classes.

In the second stage, transfer learning is applied to initialize a healthy seed specialist model from Stage 1 weights, with rebalanced class weights and tile probabilities that identify healthy seeds. During inference, a confidence-gated damage filter suppresses low-confidence predictions, and healthy seed labels are assigned only when the specialist model's confidence exceeds that of the damage model.

The two specialist models achieve validation accuracies of 94% and 98.53%, respectively, and the combined inference system successfully detects and localizes all three damage categories across unseen test images under conditions of extreme spatial variability and class imbalance. Qualitative evaluation confirms close alignment of predicted boundaries with ground truth annotations across all damage types, including dark spots.

These results demonstrate that confidence-gated dual model inference can reduce class confusion in imbalanced micro-scale segmentation, advancing the feasibility of fine-grained automated seed quality inspection at the scale.

*About the Speaker*

[Saurav Upadhyaya](https://www.linkedin.com/in/sauravupadhyaya/) is an AI/ML researcher with a Master's degree in Computer Science, whose work spans agricultural AI, conversational systems, and public health, consistently translating advanced technology into tangible real-world impact.

**From camera to drone: wildfire detection and integration at the edge**

Wildfires are getting larger and more expensive every year. But caught early, a fire is a small job for a small team; caught late, nothing stops it. The cameras to catch them are already installed, so the work is not necessary more sensors but making the ones we have act.

This talk walks the whole chain: a small vision model running on the camera that flags smoke, an integration layer that scores the alert against terrain, weather and history to decide whether it matters, and a drone dispatched to confirm before anyone commits a crew. We will cover what has to run at the edge and why, how small the model can get before it stops seeing smoke, and what it takes to trust a detection nobody has looked at yet.

*About the Speaker*

[Maxime Carriere](https://voxel51.com/events/www.linkedin.com/in/maxime-carriere-871756161) is co-founder of Kernwerk in Berlin, where he works on compressing AI models to run on cheap embedded hardware.

**5,000 Flights to Answer One Question: Can a Drone Sample as Well as a Human?**

Environmental testing still begins with a person walking onto a site with a shovel. We built a system that turns a plain-language brief into a sampling campaign, flies it, and returns soil, water and vegetation samples with GPS, timestamps and chain of custody intact: 5,000 flights, roughly 9,000 miles and 570 flight hours over a 185-acre site in Roatan, much of it under canopy where GPS degrades and clearances are tight.

I will walk through the vision and planning stack, including multispectral and thermal canopy sensing, terrain and land-cover mapping, and the constraint solver that clears a route against airspace and battery budget before anything leaves the ground. Then the harder problem: evidentiary comparability.

A drone-collected result means nothing to a regulator unless it agrees with a hand-collected split under the same method, so I will show the dual-collection protocol we designed to test exactly that. I will close on why calibrated uncertainty and knowing when a model should refuse to answer matter more than raw accuracy once the output lands in a regulatory filing.

*About the Speaker*

[Rohan Talwadia](https://www.linkedin.com/in/rohantalwadia/) is co-founder and CTO of LabGPT, which automates environmental field sampling using drones and edge analysis, with results returned through ISO/IEC 17025-accredited partner laboratories.

title: CRS/Tubman Book Launch: Unwelcome Shores: Black Refugees in America
description:
November 5, 2026
1:00 – 2:30pm (ET/Toronto)
This is a virtual event
Zoom link: https://yorku.zoom.us/meeting/register/B8h3NDjKS16QhZnv-BRSHA ( https://yorku.zoom.us/meeting/register/B8h3NDjKS16QhZnv-BRSHA )
Guest speaker: Bernadette Ludwig, Assistant Dean, Macricostas School of Arts and Sciences, Western Connecticut State University


Unwelcome Shores. Black Refugees in America (Rutgers University Press) ( https://www.rutgersuniversitypress.org/unwelcome-shores/9781978843073 ), Unwelcome Shores is an ethnographic study of the Liberian refugee community in Staten Island, New York, home to the largest per capita concentration of Liberians in the U.S., that sheds light on the racialization of Black refugees and the racism they have experienced at every step of their migration journey. In this pioneering study, sociologist Bernadette Ludwig explores how Liberians have responded to such racist exclusions, noting how members of this community reject the informal refugee label once they are resettled in the United States. Liberian migrants often view the label as a liability since the larger general public, the media, and the U.S. government tend to regard Black refugees as an economic and social burden unworthy of assistance. Indeed, Black refugees’ humanity is often ignored, Ludwig contends, in favor of overemphasizing presumed barbaric violence, endemic wars, cultural backwardness, and diseases. By detailing the lack of aid and support for Black refugees and describing how Liberian refugees in particular have had to overcome various struggles and barriers in coming to the U.S. and while living here, Unwelcome Shores highlights the overarching role of race and anti-Black racism in American society.


Biography



Bernadette Ludwig, PhD is a Sociologist and the Assistant Dean of the Macricostas School of Arts and Sciences at Western Connecticut State University (WCSU). Prior to joining WCSU, she was a tenured Professor of Sociology and the Director of Civic Engagement at a college in New York.
Her primary research focuses on the intersection of immigration, race, and gender and analyzes how seemingly racially neutral refugee and immigration policies indeed are inherently racist. In addition to her book, Unwelcome Shores: Black Refugees in America  ( https://www.rutgersuniversitypress.org/unwelcome-shores/9781978843073/ )(Rutgers University Press, 2025) she had published widely in journals such as International Migration, African and Black Diaspora: An International Journal, and International Journal of Migration, Health and Social Care, and in edited books.
In another research project, she investigates the significance and meaning of community-engaged learning opportunities for students, in particular those from historically excluded groups which have been published in Michigan Journal of Community Service, Learning Science Education & Civic Engagement, and others. Her co-edited book How to Facilitate Community-Engaged Learning (Edward Elgar Publishing) was published in August 2026.
Before pursuing a PhD in Sociology, Dr. Ludwig worked with refugee and immigrant communities in Atlanta GA. During that time, she was the executive director of two non-profit organizations, including Culture Connect, Inc., which she co-founded. Her years of working in the field with refugees and immigrants continue to inform her research and her teaching.  As a first-generation college graduate and immigrant, she is committed to mentoring students, in particular those from historically excluded groups. Dr. Ludwig also serves as a pro-bono country conditions expert for asylum and deportation claims/hearings.

title: Uplifted by the Sea: The Efik of Calabar in the Atlantic Slave Trade
description:
Date: Thursday, November 5, 2026
Time: 2:00-3:30pm EST
Location: Tubman Resource Room (314 York Lanes)
4700 Keele Street 
Toronto, ON | M3J 1P3 
In-Person Registration: https://research.apps01.yorku.ca/machform/view.php?id=322950
Zoom Registration: https://yorku.zoom.us/meeting/register/fDGGCUPYQHu66fmEakVbUg





Title: Uplifted by the Sea: The Efik of Calabar in the Atlantic Slave Trade
 
Abstract:
The history of the Efik of Calabar illustrates how geography, commerce, and human exploitation shaped an African society’s fortunes and its place in the Atlantic world. From the seventeenth century, the Efik leveraged their strategic maritime location to establish Calabar as a major slave-trading port in the Bight of Biafra, linking British merchants with hinterland communities whose people were sold into Atlantic slavery. This paper examines how maritime access, commercial monopolies, credit networks, and indigenous institutions such as the Ekpe society enabled Efik commercial dominance. It explores the paradox of Efik resistance to the enslavement of their own people alongside their participation in the enslavement of neighbouring communities. It also considers how Atlantic commerce transformed Efik society through European goods, literacy, education, and new expressions of wealth and prestige. Finally, it interrogates the selective remembrance of slavery in contemporary Calabar, particularly the tendency to emphasize European culpability while obscuring indigenous participation. Drawing on primary and secondary sources, the paper argues that Efik prosperity and regional prominence were inseparable from the Atlantic slave economy. Ultimately, the sea uplifted the Efik into extraordinary commercial and political prominence, but their ascent was entangled with the exploitation and suffering of others. Confronting this history offers a more nuanced understanding of African agency, complicity, and responsibility in the Atlantic slave trade.
 
Bio:
David L. Imbua is a Professor of Atlantic History and Diaspora Studies at the University of Calabar, Nigeria, where he serves as Head of the Department of History and International Studies and Deputy Director of the Institute for African and Asian Studies. A distinguished historian of the Atlantic world, slavery, the Cross River region, and Nigerian historiography, he has authored over 100 scholarly publications. His award-winning book, Intercourse and Crosscurrents in the Atlantic World: Calabar-British Experience, 17th–20th Centuries, received the 2015 Lapai Book Prize for Outstanding Historical Text in International History. He has contributed to UNESCO’s General History of Africa and collaborated with Professors Paul E. Lovejoy, Nicholas Radburn, and Randy J. Sparks on the landmark book, The Notorious Massacre at Calabar in 1767. A former valedictorian and overall best graduating student of the University of Calabar’s 2002 graduating class, Professor Imbua currently serves as President of the Historical Society of Nigeria, the country’s first professional association, founded in 1955.
Moderator: Dr. Damilola Adebayo, Department of History, York University.




Damilola Adebayo is an Associate Professor of History and a faculty member in the Graduate Program in Science and Technology Studies (STS). He serves as Vice President of the Canadian Association of African Studies and Associate Editor of History and Technology. An award-winning historian of Anglophone West Africa, particularly Nigeria, his research and teaching lie at the intersection of the history of technology, socioeconomic life, and the role of international organizations in Africa. His work examines the socioeconomic life of Western technologies in African cities since the mid-nineteenth century, with particular attention to the varied contexts in which energy, communication, and transportation technologies were introduced, adopted, appropriated, hybridised, reinvented, or discarded by both elite and everyday users, and to how these technologies have been both a cause and an effect of economic, social, and political change in African societies. His work has earned international recognition, including the Maurice Daumas Prize, awarded by the International Committee for the History of Technology (ICOHTEC) for the best article in the history of technology, and the Bernard S. Finn IEEE History Prize, awarded by the Society for the History of Technology (SHOT) for the best article on the history of electrotechnology. His prize-winning scholarship has appeared in leading historical journals, including Past & Present. He earned a BA in History from the University of Ibadan, an MA in International History from the Geneva Graduate Institute, and a PhD in History from the University of Cambridge, where he was a Cambridge-Africa Scholar and recipient of the IEEE Life Members’ Fellowship in the History of Electrical and Computing Technology. His book project, Power and the People: Electricity and Urban Life in Nineteenth- and Twentieth-Century Nigeria, contributes to broader debates on infrastructure, urbanization, development, state power, modernity, and energy inequality.

description:
DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse
DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit  teaches principles of air pressure and pneumatics to kids Ages 6 and up. Each child will get to take home one kit they build.
DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit
Engages children in practical activities
Teaches principles of air pressure and pneumatics
Includes all components for easy assembly
Age: 5+
The
DIY Wooden Pneumatic Horse Kit
is an engaging and educational assembly kit designed specifically for children between the ages of 5 to 12. This kit offers children the opportunity to participate in practical activities, while simultaneously observing the movement of a wooden horse, propelled by the simple push and pull of a syringe. This action illustrates the principles of air pressure and pneumatic systems in a fun and interactive way.
The kit includes all necessary components for the assembly of a pneumatic horse, such as pre-cut wooden pieces for the horse structure, a pair of syringes of different sizes, orange rubber rings that function as grippers, self-tapping screws, metal shafts of varying lengths, a small screwdriver, and a plastic tube. The assembly process does not require any soldering.

location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

title: WORLD PREMIERE – “The Art of Lockdown”
location: Fox Theatre,2236 Queen St E, Toronto, ON M4E 1G2, Canada
description:
The year is 2020. The world as we know it has changed forever. Artists whose lives and livelihoods depended on bringing people together were faced with a terrifying question:

“What do we do now?”

Introducing The Art of Lockdown, a five-episode documentary series exploring the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the arts and entertainment industry.

Each episode delves into the life and journey of a different artist, revealing how they navigated the uncertainty, challenges, and unprecedented changes brought on by the pandemic. From a one-woman clown show to a black and white murder mystery, every artist has a story to tell!

Join us at Fox Theatre on November 5th at 7:30pm for the world premiere of this compelling new series.

Stick around after the screening to connect with fellow Toronto artists, meet the filmmakers, and take part in a Q&A Session for a behind-the-scenes look at the making of the series.


Tickets: www.tickettailor.com/events/blackalloyproductions/2340506 https://www.tickettailor.com/events/blackalloyproductions/2340506


‘The Art of Lockdown’ is a timely exploration about artistic resilience, creativity, and perseverance in the face of overwhelming odds. It shines a light on the people who create the stories we love and highlights the determination it takes to keep creating, even when the world came to a standstill.

Across five episodes, The Art of Lockdown explores the creativity, resilience, and reinvention of artists navigating an unprecedented moment in history. From experimental filmmaking to personal accounts of an industry in crisis, each episode offers a unique perspective on the pandemic’s impact on the arts.

Episode 1: The Clown

When the Toronto Fringe Festival is cancelled, Katherine transforms her one-woman

show into a short film about a clown navigating the early days of lockdown.

Featuring: Katherine Cappellacci and Laura Cappellacci


Episode 2: Hartley & Sheel

“Have you ever seen Clue?” A sketch comedy duo takes a crack at solving a crime in a

black-and-white murder mystery filmed during lockdown.

Featuring: Hartley Fanson, Sheel Radia, Chris Black, and Anthony Gullace


Episode 3: Respect for Actors

“Our industry was the first to shut down… We lost everything.” As COVID-19 brings

theatre and film productions to a standstill, five actors share their experiences of

navigating uncertainty, reinventing their craft, and adapting to a rapidly changing

industry.

Featuring: Chase Jeffels, Felix Beauchamp, Noor Alimran, Karen Scobie, and Chelsea

Muirhead


Episode 4: Phoenix Rising

Faced with unprecedented challenges, one theatre company refuses to stand still. Discover how its team adapts, innovates, and finds new ways to bring creativity to life.

Featuring: Brandon Nicoletti and Jordan Kenny


Episode 5: The Making Of

Go behind the scenes of The Art of Lockdown for an inside look at the creative process, collaboration, and work that brought this documentary series to life.

Featuring: Can Yüksel, Felipe Gonzalez, Brandon Nicoletti, and Jordan Kenny

title: Computers for Beginners
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: Forest Bathing at the Garden
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Connect with nature and join us for a guided forest therapy walk!
Rekindle your relationship with nature this fall through a guided outdoor forest bathing walk with certified forest therapy guide Laura Bincik. At a slow pace and in community with other participants and the environment, you will be guided by a series of invitations throughout the experience to awaken your senses and intentionally connect with nature in the present moment.
 
We will gather briefly indoors to prepare for the walk and consider the origin of forest bathing, as well as some of the benefits of the practice. When we venture into the Toronto Botanical Gardens and surrounding ravine, we will cover a loop of approximately 1.5 km on paved pathways, lawns and bare ground, at times encountering uneven terrain, inclines and declines. We will be strolling, standing and sitting (if you wish to). Your comfort and safety are most important!
 
As this program occurs rain or shine, please dress for the weather and wear sturdy, closed-toed footwear. Long pants and shirt sleeves will help to protect against insect bites. You may wish to bring a water bottle, sunhat/glasses, walking poles and/or a folding stool or sitting/kneeling pad.
 
As the walk ends, we will gather and partake in a seasonal tea, snacks and taste honey harvested at Toronto Botanical Garden.
 
In the event of severe weather or environmental conditions, TBG staff will make alternative arrangements to the program.
 
Washrooms are available onsite.
 
The program is suited for adults 18+. All participants must sign a liability waiver at the start of the program.
 
Service pets welcome but we ask that you leave your pets at home during this program.
 
Friday, November 6, 1 to 3 p.m.
Public $35, TBG Members $30 (plus applicable taxes and fees)
 
About Laura Bincik
Laura Bincik is a certified forest therapy guide with the Association of Nature and Forest Therapy. Following a career that straddled health care and education, Laura discovered that her lifelong sense of awe for the natural world could be enriched and shared with others to enhance wellbeing. Laura feels a connection to the land and the wonder of being in nature from countless hours spent exploring Toronto ravines in all seasons. An active member of Nature and Forest Therapy Canada, Laura follows the growing research on the mental and physical health benefits of forest bathing and is expanding her practice by connecting with local, national and international leaders in the field.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
