title: Robotics Institute Seminar: Leslie Kaelbling, “The Role of Rationality in Modern Robotics”
location: Schwartz Reisman Innovation Campus, 108 College Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5G0G6, Canada
description:
This seminar is co-hosted with the Department of Computer Science 
Schwartz Reisman Innovation Campus, West Winter Garden (10th Floor) 
Register for the seminar 



The Role of Rationality in Modern Robotics
Abstract
The classical approach to AI designed systems that were rational at run-time: they had explicit representations of beliefs, goals, and plans and ran inference algorithms, online, to select actions. The rational approach was criticized (by the behaviorists) and modified (by the probabilists) but persisted in some form. More recently, relatively unstructured data-driven end-to-end approaches have demonstrated great success in a wide variety of domains, and began to seem like a plausible route to general-purpose intelligent robots. However, most recently, we have begun to see the limits of pure behavior learning and many practitioners are re-integrating forms of search and explicit reasoning into their approaches. 
Professor Kaelbling will revisit the rational-agent approach to the design of intelligent robots, from the perspectives of engineering effort, computational efficiency, cognitive modeling and understandability. They will present some current research focused on understanding the roles of learning in runtime-rational agents with the ultimate aim of constructing general-purpose human-level intelligent robots. 
Register for the seminar 
About Leslie Kaelbling
Leslie Pack Kaelbling is a Professor at MIT. She has an undergraduate degree in Philosophy and a PhD in Computer Science from Stanford, and was previously on the faculty at Brown University. She was the founding editor-in-chief of the Journal of Machine Learning Research. Her research agenda is to make intelligent robots using methods including learning, planning, and reasoning about uncertainty. She was doing agentic AI way before it was cool.

title: Nov 19 - Visualizing and Debugging Hugging Face's LeRobot Data
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
This workshop is a hands-on tour of what actually breaks when you load real LeRobot datasets, and how Voxel51's native LeRobot support in FiftyOne catches it.

**Date, Time and Location**

Nov 19, 2026
9:00 AM - 10:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/lerobot-workshop-november-19-2026)**

Robot learning data doesn't look like the data that trains most vision-language models. It's temporal, low-dimensional in the parts that matter most, embodiment-specific, and expensive to collect, and increasingly, it's shipped in Hugging Face's LeRobot format. But packaging robot data consistently isn't the same as being able to see it: episodes hide broken metadata, silently dropped sensor modalities, and mismatched schemas between robots that look identical on paper.

Starting from the core differences that make robot data hard (temporal structure, proprioception, action grounding, embodiment heterogeneity, data scarcity), we'll move into live debugging: a metadata bug that broke multiple dataset imports, sensor streams that vanish without an error, and two robots running an identical benchmark whose data is structurally incompatible. By the end, you'll know what to check before you trust a LeRobot dataset, and how to actually look inside one.

Curious about artificial intelligence or want to learn practical AI skills for work and personal use? Join our staff-facilitated learning circle to complete the self-paced Google AI Essentials specialization.
This 10-hour introductory-level specialization, offered through Coursera, is available for free to learning circle participants. It is made up of five courses, each containing four units that consist of short videos, articles, assignments and a short multiple-choice quiz.
By completing the specialization,
you will learn:
How AI works
How to write effective prompts
How to use generative AI tools responsibly
How to identify AI's potential biases and avoid harm
How to stay up to date with AI news
After you complete the course, you earn a Google certificate and a badge to share with others
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google AI Essentials specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four learning circle sessions.
No AI experience is required.

title: UNESCO World Philosophy Day (Laurie Paul, Yale University)
description:
This year, we welcome as 2026 UNESCO World Philosophy Day lecture speaker Laurie Paul, the Millstone Family Professor of Philosophy and Cognitive Science Yale University. She explores relationships between the nature of the self, transformative experience, preference change, subjective value, temporal experience, causation, time, and perception. 
Talk Title
The paradox of transformation 
Talk Abstract
Transformative changes happen. They can be chosen or unchosen, wanted or unwanted, good or bad. They can occur as part of ordinary life transitions, as when one graduates from college, becomes a parent, marries, emigrates, or divorces, and they can occur in extraordinary circumstances, such as when one experiences a war, a serious physical accident, an invasive neurosurgical procedure, or cognitive change due to Alzheimer’s. I will develop a conceptual framework that characterizes the profound and paradoxical nature of the epistemic and personal transformation that transformative experience can bring, and explore some of the formal implications for models of decision and change.

title: Learning Things You Love with AI
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
Always wanted to learn to cook, draw, knit, fix a bike, or speak another language, but have trouble sticking to it? What if you had a personal AI tutor?
In this class with our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, learn how AI can become your personal tutor for something you love, or something new you want to fall in love with. A tutor explains things in the way you understand, asks you questions, and helps you choose what to learn next. Learn how to turn your goal into a specific, doable learning experiment: options not answers, with a practice that survives a bad day. Decide ahead of time how you'll know it's working: revise, or stop without guilt. You'll leave with a plan you actually want to try, and a sense for what AI should never decide for you.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.
If you wish to save your work from this hands-on program, please bring your own USB stick.

title: Nuclear Industry Panel Night - OPTIONS Program
description:
Thursday, November 19 | 5:00 – 7:00 PM | GB202 (Galbraith Building, 35 St. George St., Room 202) | Register in Advance* 
*PLEASE NOTE THAT THIS EVENT IS AVAILABLE EXCLUSIVELY TO UOFT ENGINEERING GRADUATE STUDENTS. 
Explore the cutting edge of nuclear innovation and the need for talent in this rapidly evolving field. This special evening brings together industry leaders and academic voices to spotlight opportunities, challenges, and the future of the nuclear workforce development.  
ISTEP is proud to bring you this event with the support of our departmental co-sponsors: 

Department of Chemical Engineering & Applied Chemistry
Department of Civil & Mineral Engineering
The Edward S. Rogers Sr. Department of Electrical & Computer Engineering
Department of Mechanical & Industrial Engineering

Featured Speakers:  
Sean Granville, Board of Directors, NWMO | Former COO and Chief Nuclear Officer, OPG | President of BNKA Consulting Inc. 
As former Chief Operations Officer and Chief Nuclear Officer of Ontario Power Generation (OPG), Sean Granville was responsible for all of OPG’s generating fleet, with a capacity of over 15,400 megawatts of electricity. This consisted of 10 nuclear units, 66 hydro stations, two thermal stations, one solar facility, as well as oversight of OPG subsidiaries Atura Power and Eagle Creek Renewable Energy. Mr. Granville’s nuclear career spans 39 years including three years at Point Lepreau Nuclear Generating Station in New Brunswick. Mr. Granville’s energy industry experience includes a World Association of Nuclear Operators secondment, as well as membership in the Canadian Nuclear Association and the CANDU Owners Group. Mr. Granville is also a board member of Women in Nuclear and past chair of the Canadian Chief Nuclear Officer Forum, as well as a past member of the Institute of Nuclear Power Operations Executive Advisory Group. Mr. Granville is currently providing executive consulting services to the energy industry. Mr. Granville is a graduate of the University of Waterloo with a Bachelor of Applied Science in Mechanical Engineering.  
Laurie Swami, President and CEO of Nuclear Waste Management Organization  
Ms. Laurie Swami is the President and CEO of the Nuclear Waste Management Organization (NWMO). She was appointed to the role in 2016 and is responsible for implementing Canada’s plan for the long- term management of used nuclear fuel.   
Prior to joining the NWMO, Ms. Swami spent 30 years, primarily in nuclear operations, at Ontario Power Generation. She served as Senior Vice-President of Decommissioning and Nuclear Waste Management, overseeing the operation of nuclear waste management facilities and planning for the decommissioning of a nuclear generating facility.   
Ms. Swami has extensive experience leading Environmental Assessment projects, including nuclear refurbishments. She has appeared before Joint Panel Reviews (CEA and CNSC) for the Darlington New Nuclear Project and OPG’s Deep Geologic Repository Project. She holds a Bachelor of Science in Engineering Chemistry from Queen’s University and a Master of Business Administration from the Schulich School of Business. She is an ardent supporter of and advocate for the advancement of women to leadership positions. In recognition of this contribution, she received the Women in Nuclear Canada Leadership Award in 2016.  
Peter Keech, Associate Professor, Department of Chemical Engineering & Applied Chemistry  
Peter Keech is an Associate Professor, Nuclear Engineering within the Department of Chemical Engineering and Applied Chemistry. For 15 years, he worked at the Nuclear Waste Management Organization where he led research programs around the world to advance the understanding of the container and sealing system that will be used in the deep geological repository for used nuclear fuel in Canada.    
Through work with universities, national laboratories and international partner organizations, he has over one hundred and twenty publications, including more than ninety peer-reviewed journal articles and three book chapters related to chemistry, nuclear waste, corrosion, microbiology and clay.    
Dr. Keech regularly presents both technical and non-technical information directly to scientists, non-scientists, partners and other stakeholders in the nuclear waste program. He provides support and technical review for several organizations, including Nagra of Switzerland, Posiva Oy of Finland, SKB of Sweden and NWS of the United Kingdom and herecently served as a member of the Technical Advisory Committee for NUMO of Japan.    
While at the NWMO and on behalf of its partner academic research community, Dr. Keech co-chaired the committee on Indigenous Knowledge and Western Science within NWMO’s Strategic Initiatives group. He has organized and co-chaired workshops for a wide range of participants, including professors and graduate students, and Indigenous Youth and Elders, to broaden perspectives and meaningfully contribute to Reconciliation. Dr. Keech was born in Orillia, Canada.   
Christina Dimitrov, Senior Manager of Strategic Initiatives at OPG  
Christina is a seasoned leader with over two decades of experience at Ontario Power Generation (OPG), where she has held diverse roles across business development, enterprise strategy, treasury and risk management. Currently Christina is a Senior Manager supporting New Growth at OPG, pursuing strategic partnerships in support of the company’s growth portfolio. Christina’s career highlights include contributing to OPG’s corporate strategy development, driving business optimization initiatives, and financing large-scale hydroelectric projects.   
Christina has achieved certifications in risk management, treasury, and project management, complemented by an Honours Bachelor of Commerce. She is a supportive mentor, and advocate for the advancement of women in nuclear and across the energy transition more broadly.  
Moderated by:  Maggie von Vaight, Lecturer, Institute for Studies in Transdisciplinary Engineering Education & Practice   
Maggie von Vaight is a nuclear professional supporting the $13-billion Major Component Replacement (MCR) Program at Bruce Power, one of Canada’s largest clean energy infrastructure investments. The program involves the refurbishment of six nuclear units and is helping secure Ontario’s supply of reliable, carbon-free electricity.  
With more than a decade of experience in the nuclear industry, Maggie has established expertise in procedural governance, project controls, and organizational learning, driving performance and continuous improvement across complex, highly regulated environments. She has served as a lecturer with the University of Toronto, Faculty of Engineering and as a guest lecturer at the University of Guelph, Lang School of Business where her teaching and industry engagement have focused on innovation, commercialization, and entrepreneurship, connecting emerging ideas with industry application.  
An alumna of both the University of Toronto and the University of Guelph, Maggie is a passionate advocate for education, workforce development, and collaboration between academia and industry. Through her leadership and mentorship, she champions opportunities for young professionals, fostering meaningful industry partnerships, and developing the next generation of leaders who will build a stronger, more innovative, and sustainable future.

title: The Ishizue Award Dinner 2026
description:
The JCCC Board of Directors is pleased to announce that the 8th Ishizue Award and accompanying dinner will be held on Thursday November 19, 2026. The Ishizue Award acknowledges and expresses our appreciation and respect to members or friends who have made exceptional contributions to the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. The name Ishizue, meaning cornerstone or foundation, pays tribute to the 75 families who, at significant personal financial risk, guaranteed the original mortgage on the JCCC at 123 Wynford Drive in the early 1960’s. These families provided the foundation upon which the JCCC was built, and their support for the JCCC will forever be recognized as the cornerstone for who we are as a community. The recipients of this annual award are a very distinguished group of people who have each made significant life contributions to the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. They are: Ken Fukushima Harry Kawabe Akiko Maruoka David Ohashi (Post humous) Connie Sugiyama David Tsubouchi We cordially invite you to honour these distinguished award recipients at an intimate and elegant dinner on Thursday November 19th at 6:30pm at the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre. Black tie optional. Tickets are $180 each (plus HST) . Maximum of 10 guests per table. To purchase tickets please order through the button below or in person at the JCCC, starting September 21, 2026, and ending November 9, 2026. Please contact Sharon Marubashi for any further information by email or phone (647-291-4751). On behalf of all of the directors of the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre, we look forward to spending a special evening of recognition and celebration together. Purchase Ticket

description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

title: Qawwali Flamenco
location: Massey Hall, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
From Pakistan to Andalusia, musical traditions have crossed paths, met, nourished one another, and blended so thoroughly that between the volcanic power and virtuosity of qawwali singing and the hypnotic lyricism of flamenco, distances fade and similarities naturally emerge.

Qawwali Flamenco marks the long-awaited return of the celebrated collaboration between Pakistani qawwali master Faiz Ali Faiz and flamenco guitar virtuoso Juan Gómez “Chicuelo.”

Following their acclaimed first collaboration a decade ago, Faiz and Gómez reunite to deepen a remarkable artistic dialogue. The first chapter of their Qawwali Flamenco journey explored the relationship between human beings and their beloved; this new creation turns toward the connection between humanity and the divine.

title: Google Prompting Essentials: Online Learning Circle
description:
Ready to develop the skills to use generative AI (GenAI) tools effectively and responsibly for work and daily life? Join our staff-facilitated Learning Circle to complete the self-paced Google Prompting specialization. By completing this Learning Circle program, you will earn a Google Prompting Essentials certificate to share on your resume, LinkedIn and social media profiles!
What You'll Learn
This program is designed for those with some experience with using GenAI. Through short videos, articles, assignments and quizzes, you will discover:
Essential
Prompting Skills
: How to use a prompting framework to create a desired output with GenAI; how to evaluate and refine your results.
Everyday Work Tasks:
Strategies to draft content, brainstorm ideas, create tables, timelines, and more.
Data & Presentations:
How to explore data visualization and use GenAI responsibly when working with data.
Advanced Techniques:
How to use prompt chaining for complex tasks and prompt versioning to save and reuse your best prompts over time.
Learning Circles are study groups guided by
library staff for people who want to complete the Google Prompting specialization together in a welcoming space:
Learners meet weekly and work together through course materials.
Participants are expected to commit to attending all four Learning Circle sessions.

title: Computers for Beginners
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

As the result of a life changing 14-year dementia care experience, Karen founded the Long Term Care Planning Network, Canada’s leading resource centre for ageing, eldercare and long term care planning and education. Her seminar series, web site and print/electronic tools are recognized as key long term care educational resources for Canadian families.
Karen is a Certified Professional Consultant on Aging (CPCA).

Become a page-turner by joining the Between the Lines Book Club! Here, we embark on a new chapter with every read, diving into a world of endless possibilities. Friday November 16: A Gentleman in Moscow by Amor Towles
Set in Moscow in 1922,
A Gentleman in Moscow
by Amor Towles follows Count Alexander Rostov, a refined Russian aristocrat sentenced by a Bolshevik tribunal to house arrest in the grand Metropol Hotel, where he must spend the rest of his life confined within its walls. As the world outside undergoes dramatic political and social change, the Count gradually transforms his restricted circumstances into a life rich with unexpected friendships, meaningful encounters, and quiet adventures. From navigating the hotel's intricate social world to forming a particularly meaningful bond with a young girl named Nina, Rostov discovers new perspectives on love, loyalty, personal growth, and the passage of time. Elegant, witty, and deeply moving, the novel explores the nature of freedom, the importance of human connection, and the possibility of finding purpose and beauty even when life takes an unexpected turn.

title: CANCELLED: Orhan Pamuk's The Museum of Innocence: Novel and Museum
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
IMPORTANT UPDATE:
Due to unforeseen circumstances, this event has been cancelled. We apologize for any inconvenience and look forward to welcoming you to another event soon.
Nobel Prize-winner Orhan Pamuk speaks about the creation of Istanbul's Museum of Innocence.
Renowned Turkish novelist and Nobel Prize-winner Orhan Pamuk joins celebrated museum and cultural planning leader, Gail Lord, for an extraordinary conversation about one of the most singular acts of imagination in contemporary literature and museology: the creation of Istanbul's Museum of Innocence.
Conceived in tandem with his acclaimed novel of the same name, Pamuk's museum houses the fictional world of his characters Kemal and Füsun in a real, physical space — a small house in Istanbul filled with everyday objects, each one tied to a moment in the novel. The result is a haunting blur between fiction and reality, where a love story lives on not only on the page, but in glass display cases, drawers, and rooms visitors can walk through.
How does one curate a museum for people who never existed? What does it mean to give physical form to memory, longing, and melancholy — the very textures of a novel? And what challenges arise when an author becomes a museum-maker, translating narrative into space, object, and atmosphere?
Orhan Pamuk sits down with Gail Lord, co-founder of Lord Cultural Resources and one of the world's leading museum planners, to discuss the twin creation of the novel and the museum, the ethereal act of turning fiction into physical experience, and what he hoped visitors would feel wandering through the rooms of a story. The conversation will also turn to Pamuk's evolving philosophy of museums — the ideas first laid out in his "Modest Manifesto for Museums" — exploring his belief in small, intimate institutions that honor individual and everyday stories over the grand, monumental narratives so often privileged by national museums.
The discussion will also look ahead to Pamuk's second museum project, currently in development, in which he continues to explore the relationship between storytelling, memory, and collected objects. Building on the foundations laid by the Museum of Innocence, this new endeavor promises to further test the boundaries between literature and lived space, offering fresh insight into how narrative can be translated into an immersive, tangible experience.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

title: Koerner Hall:  Naghash Ensemble, Karen Ouzounian, and the Amadeus Choir
description:
TORONTO ARTS & CULTURE
**A magical evening of Armenian music direct from Yerevan, and the Canadian premiere of *Dear Mountains*,** a recent work for chorus, solo cello, oud, and percussion, co-composed by the RCM alumna and Silk Road Ensemble member Karen Ouzounian and Lembit Beecher.

Please **use our 15% off promo code** for this concert. Details/Ticket link is below. (Excellent pricing and seats on this concert)

**The Naghash Ensemble** combines the earthy spirituality of Armenian folk songs, new classical music, and contemporary post-minimalism with the energy of rock and jazz. Three brilliant female vocalists and some of Armenia’s finest instrumentalists on duduk, oud, dhol, and piano play captivating new music based on sacred texts by the medieval Armenian mystic poet and priest Mkrtich Naghash.

Written by Armenian-American composer John Hodian, The Naghash Ensemble’s *Songs of Exile* is a profound meditation on man's relationship to God from the perspective of a monk forced to live in exile for many years. Part folk music, part classical, and profoundly moving.

Sought after for her “radiant” (*The New York Times*) performances full of “tremendous heart, bringing joy and a captivating sound to the stage” (*The Strad*), Karen Ouzounian is a Grammy Award nominated cellist and composer who creates music from a deeply personal place. An omnivorous musical spirit who “powerfully shatters pigeonholes with her artistic partners” (*Ravinia Magazine*), she has premiered numerous works and collaborated with some of the most singular musicians of our time, including Yo-Yo Ma, Rhiannon Giddens, and Augustin Hadelich. She will present *Dear Mountains*, a major work composed by her and Lembit Beecher in 2024 that juxtaposes stories told and retold in Ouzounian’s family with scenes of music-making across the Armenian diaspora over the last 100 years, as seen through archival recordings and writings. *Dear Mountains* features Ouzounian on cello, Ara Dinkjian on oud, Philip Mayer on percussion, **and the Amadeus Choir led by Kathleen Allan.**
Led by Artistic Director Kathleen Allan, the Amadeus Choir champions the best of choral music and premieres works of Canadian and international composers through a self-produced Toronto concert series, guest performances, and special events. The Choir regularly commissions work from high-profile and emerging Canadian composers and recently established the Choral Creation Lab, a residency for composers and poets to co-create original works.

title: Blackbird: In the Footsteps of Ziryab
location: Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Blackbird: In the Footsteps of Ziryab makes its world premiere as a bold new multidisciplinary performance celebrating the enduring connections between cultures through oral and artistic traditions. Led by Artistic Director Amir Amiri, the Amir Amiri Ensemble, featuring Óscar de los Reyes and Esperanza Soria, the performance brings together Canadian and Spanish Andalusian artists in a powerful artistic dialogue. Connected through centuries of migration, poetry, rhythm, and memory, the performance explores a shared cultural legacy while embracing new creative expression. The essentials of flamenco are all present: voice, complex rhythm, and dance.

This presentation ultimately asks how music travels through history, how cultures reshape one another, and how artists continue to carry ancient knowledge into contemporary life. The project seeks to illuminate the enduring connections between Persian and Andalusian artistic worlds, while creating a contemporary performance grounded in research, artistic integrity, and shared humanity.

title: Kashikari-Inspired Tile Glazing Workshop | Misbah Ahmed & Tigerbaby Coffee & Clay
location: Tigerbaby Coffee & Clay,977 College St, Toronto, ON M6H 1A6, Canada
description:
Join sukoon space, ceramic artist Misbah Ahmed https://misbahahmed.com/?utm_source=luma and Tigerbaby Coffee and Clay https://tigerbabycc.com/?utm_source=luma for an afternoon of tile glazing inspired by Kashikari.

Taking the colours and patterns of Kashikari tilework as a starting point, you’ll explore your own design on a handmade ceramic tile. Misbah will guide you through the glazing process, working on an approximately 7 × 7-inch tile that has been prepared and fired ahead of the workshop.

Spend an afternoon making, experimenting with pattern and connecting with others, while creating a piece of your own. All glazing materials, guided instruction and final kiln firing are included.

About Kashikari

Kashikari is the art of glazed ceramic tilework, with roots in Persian ceramic traditions and a distinctive heritage in Multan, Pakistan. Multani tilework is known for its cobalt blues, turquoise and white, combining intricate floral motifs and geometric patterns to decorate shrines and historic buildings.

In this workshop, we’ll take inspiration from that tradition as you glaze your own handmade, pre-fired ceramic tile. Misbah will guide you through exploring colour and pattern, with room to interpret the designs in your own way.

Artist Bio

Misbah Ahmed is a Toronto-based artist and educator working across ceramics, painting and printmaking. Born in Islamabad and raised in Canada, she draws on Pakistani and South Asian stories, family histories and archival research to explore belonging, cultural change and our relationship with the environment.

Her work brings an interest in traditional crafts into conversation with themes of memory, resilience and the climate crisis. She graduated from OCAD University’s Illustration program in 2018, receiving its program medal, and has taught there since 2020. She also teaches ceramics at the Gardiner Museum and founded Sehn Studio in 2024, a Toronto space for art-making, classes and guest workshops. Her solo exhibitions include Dry Thunder at the Art Gallery of Burlington in 2025.

Georgian, Gothic Revival, Bay and Gable, the list goes on and on. Toronto has many styles, and one can explore the history of Toronto simply by learning the different time periods involved.

This tour explores the **architecture** of the Annex District, **Casa Loma** and its grand competitor Spadina House. These legendary landmarks on the hill overlooking the city have been focal points of Toronto history for well over a century in an area that has a vast story to tell.

Just a reminder that we will be walking up to the Case Loma site and exploring the grounds and the history, we are not going inside any of the buildings.

We begin this walk in front of the main doors to the Toronto Public Library Spadina Branch at 10 Spadina Road. We end at St. Clair Avenue West at the Loblaws Superstore at the St. Clair West Subway Station. Hope to see you soon.

This walk is for most walking levels; however, there are steps and stairs near Casa Loma, north of Davenport. Please dress for the weather and see you there.

title: Go-Between Girl: Author Andrea Gunraj on Identity, Memory, and the Indo-Caribbean Woman Experience in Canada
description:
Meet
Andrea Gunraj
, acclaimed essayist and author of
Go-between Girl: My Indentured Roots as Reclaimed Present
, The Lost Sister and The Sudden Disappearance of Seetha. Based out of Toronto, Gunraj writes about underseen stories and connections. She will discuss her latest work, Go-Between Girl, through storytelling and personal reflection, exploring themes of family, migration, belonging, and the complex intersections of Caribbean, Indian, and Canadian identities.
Gunraj will be in conversation with
Victoria Kuketz
, a public policy leader and journalist (IG @victoriakuketz). The discussion will be followed by an audience Q&A and book signing.
Presented by the
Caribbean Canadian Indian Cultural Collective (CCICC)
and
Indo Caribbean Educators Network (ICEN)
, this event offers a unique opportunity to engage with one of the most compelling voices in contemporary Indo-Caribbean literature. Attendees will gain insight into Gunraj's personal journey as a professional civic leader and Indo-Caribbean woman, and how historical and cultural experiences have shaped Indo-Caribbean people. Discover the power of storytelling as memory, community building, and cross-cultural understanding.
Whether you are familiar with Andrea's work or discovering it for the first time, this event promises an inspiring and thought-provoking evening celebrating literature, heritage, and the diverse narratives that enrich Canada's multicultural landscape.
Free program. Please register. Doors open at 12:45 pm. At 1:00 pm, seating becomes first-come, first-served until capacity is reached.
Organization Info:
The
Canadian Caribbean Indian Cultural Collective (CCICC)
is a community organization representing Indians (currently referred to as South Asians) of various ethnicities, regions, and faiths, who are the descendants of the indentured labourers taken by the British to their colonies in the Caribbean and around the world. Their mission is to share their stories of struggle, resilience and contributions across the Caribbean and here in Canada.

title: Introduction to Chainmail Workshop
location: Lillian H. Smith, Bagshaw Room, 1st floor.
description:
Chainmail, the ancient art of linking metal rings together in a chain or mesh weave, has a long history within cultural practices from all over the world. These days you might not need a piece of armour to protect yourself during a swordfight, but you still might want to know how to make some - whether for yourself or to deck out a favourite toy! Or, maybe you want to make some unique jewelry: bracelets, necklaces, or earrings. Why not both?
Registration for both sessions is required:
1st session, Nov 7: Basics! Opening and closing rings, Japanese 1-in-1, 2-in-2, or 3-in-3 chain weave, attaching clasps. Make a bracelet or a short necklace.
2nd session, Nov 21: Pick 1 option - barrel or box chain weave, or 4-1 European mesh weave. Make a bracelet, a short necklace, or a base for a larger piece.
Please note that chainmail requires repetitive hand motions, gripping, and close visual attention to detail.
These sessions are oriented towards beginners but more advanced learners are also welcome.

title: Who Should Own AI? Building Public AI
description:
If AI becomes as important as roads, electricity, or libraries, who should own it? Who decides what it's used for? Who gets access and to say no?
This panel discussion, as part of our Innovator-in-Residence program with
Ryan Kelln
, will include speakers building public-interest AI, working in civic tech, and organizing communities affected by AI decisions. We'll explore what's already being built, from open models and public compute to community-owned data, and what's being privatized. You'll get to draft your own "public AI requirements" and see what others think should be guaranteed to everyone. The future of AI is being decided now; this is a chance to have a say in it.
Featuring:
Alex Olson
, Director of University of Toronto’s Centre for Analytics & AI Engineering
Khasir Hean
, Founder of Technologists for Democracy, Machine Learning engineer
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.

location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

title: Flamenco: Made in Canada presents Duende Al Nur
location: Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
Duende al Nur , meaning “Duende toward the light,” is an immersive flamenco work where light, shadow and fire transform the dancing body.

Performed on a luminous plexiglass platform, the piece explores light as a sacred, living force rising from beneath the dancer. From darkness, the body is awakened by illumination. Breath becomes pulse, pulse becomes rhythm, and rhythm becomes flamenco. Through footwork, castanets, zills, breath and silence, Carmen Romero moves through a ritual journey of awakening and renewal. Rooted in the emotional power of duende and the Arabic resonance of nur, the work becomes a passage through memory, prayer, rhythm and transformation.

The work draws from flamenco’s emotional intensity, rhythmic complexity and theatrical power while opening the performance space to Arabic resonance, sacred illumination and immersive sound. Rather than presenting cultural influence literally, Duende al Nur approaches these elements as echoes, atmospheres and poetic points of connection.

description: FALL/WINTER HIKING The Forks of the Credit is a part of the Bruce Trail and also the Niagara Escarpment Biosphere. The hike starts at the junction of Mississauga Road and the Elora Cataract Rail Trail. There had been a mill in the Cataract area since 1820 and in 1885 John Deagle bought the mill and converted it into a hydro generating station which was later purchased by Ontario Hydro and eventually shut down in 1947. The area was also the source of Credit Valley sandstone which was used in the construction of various large buildings like Queen's Park and the Old City Hall. title: Look to Windward - Ian M. Banks
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi all,

So glad to have our Iain M. Banks selection finalized for November. As we’ve discussed previously, the books in the Culture series are connected, but don’t necessarily need to be read in order. The Club really enjoyed Book 2, *The Player of Games*, and I’m curious to see where in the universe we land with Book 7, 2000’s *Look to Windward*.

[sophyanempire](https://sophyanempire.wordpress.com/2012/03/08/look-to-windward-iain-m-banks-orbit-2000/) has a solid review of this entry in the Culture series, calling *Look to Windward* “exciting, tense, sad and heroic.” She notes that from there, “the book grows in scope, showing multiple perspectives, almost all of them from a non-human alien point of view.”

[The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/books/2000/sep/02/sciencefictionfantasyandhorror.iainbanks) also has a great review from when the book was first published. Phil Daoust writes that “Banks has tremendous fun with his giant canvas” in *Windward*.

To join a Book Club meeting, all you will need is YOURSELF. If you haven’t had a chance to finish the book, we still would love for you to join us in the discussion.

Not able to join us in person for events? [The Sci Fi Book Club is on Discord](https://discord.gg/B9NMnC2F). Join us and keep the conversation going.

A reminder that Book Club takes a break each October, so while Look to Windward has a fairly large page count, we’ll essentially have two months to read our pick.

Cheers,

Jon

description: This listing is for a two session Beginner Crochet Course. The classes will be held in person at Bistitchual on Sunday November 22nd and 29th from 2:30pm-4:00pm Learn the fundamentals of crochet in this two part class. We will be covering chaining and single crochet, as well as double and half-double crochets. Don’t know what any of that means? Great, you’re in the right place! We’ll provide all the materials, including a simple pattern that teaches you common terms and instructions you’ll encounter in most crochet projects. We will also discuss how to choose the appropriate yarn and hook for a project as well as where you can take your crafting after you master these basic techniques. There’s a lot to learn, and we’re excited to accompany your beginning in the wonderful craft of crochet! Materials are included! - 50g ball of worsted weight cotton in your choice of colour - 6mm crochet hook Our class size is capped at 4 people, so everyone can receive the attention they need. Mike will share lots of tips and techniques to get you well on your way. About the instructor: Tired of disposing of clothes that were still perfectly wearable, Mike (he/him) started crafting mainly as a means of mending and repair. This led him to knitting (and later crochet), which pretty much immediately became one of his favourite tools of self-expression. Please note that classes will only proceed if we have a minimum of two attendees . If the minimum is not met, there will be the option for a refund or to reschedule. title: Sound and Sense: Jewish Music @York presents Pursue Peace
location: Tribute Communities Recital Hall @ Accolade East Building 83 York Boulevard, Toronto
description:
Contemporary Chamber Music by Canadian Jewish Composers
Album Release Celebration Concert
York University’s Koschitzky Centre for Jewish Studies ( https://www.yorku.ca/cjs/ ) and the Department of Music ( https://ampd.yorku.ca/department-of-music/ ) in the School of the Arts, Media, Performance and Design ( https://ampd.yorku.ca/ ) invite you to the opening of the fifth season of Sound and Sense: Jewish Music at York, with a special release concert celebrating Pursue Peace, the initiative’s debut album. The program brings together the work of three distinguished Canadian composers and leading performers in an evening of music shaped by memory, identity, history, and the many ways music gives voice to human experience.
Released by New Focus Recordings, the New York-based independent label devoted to contemporary and creative music, Pursue Peace features composers Noam Lemish ( https://www.noamlemish.com/bio ) (ON), Sid Robinovitch ( https://www.sidrobinovitch.ca/ ) (AB), and James Rolfe ( https://www.jamesrolfe.ca/bio/ ) (ON), whose music spans intimate works for violin and piano, string quartet and clarinet, and a larger work for choir, soprano and ensemble.
More than three years in the making, the album is the culmination of an ongoing artistic collaboration at York, bringing the work of Sound and Sense: Jewish Music at York to a wider audience. We invite you to join the ongoing conversation through music and celebrate this milestone with us.

title: Los Magníficos
location: Nanji Family Foundation Auditorium, Aga Khan Museum, 77 Wynford Drive, Toronto, ON M3C 1K1
description:
“Los Magníficos” is a once-in-a-lifetime encounter with the greatness of contemporary flamenco. Five outstanding artists come together in a unique performance where singing, dance, guitar, and piano reach their highest expression.

Sandra Carrasco, one of the most important voices of the moment, takes us to the very heart of flamenco. David de Arahal captivates audiences with his mastery of the guitar, while Andrés Barrios transforms the piano into pure emotion. Dancer “El Yiyo” embodies the power and intensity of flamenco, joined by Carmen “La Talegona,” whose artistry and magnetic stage presence bring elegance, strength, and depth to this extraordinary encounter.

Prepare for an intense and magnetic journey, where energy and sensitivity intertwine in an explosion of talent. “ Los Magníficos” is not just a performance; it’s a unique opportunity to witness the union of some of the finest artists of our time in a moment destined to remain forever in the memory of flamenco art.

title: Get Things Done with AI: Build Your Own Productivity System
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if your to-do list could check in on you, notice what's been stuck for weeks, and offer to help instead of just sitting there?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll explore a personal productivity system built around an AI agent and a weekly-review practice. See how the agent loads goals, counts what actually got done, flags the items that keep slipping, and drafts next week's plan. It can support without cheerleading, asking "Why has this been stuck for three weeks? Here are your options." You'll try it yourself with a practice set of goals, and leave with the plain-text templates and a clearer map of how an AI might support you, ready to build your own system at home.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.

title: Bee-ing a Pollinator Protector: Plan Now for a Buzzing Spring Garden
description:
Saving the bees is an environmental cause that resonates deeply with Canadians.  While most of us might not be thinking about bees this time of year, our actions during the colder months can still support these pollinators, particularly native bees, which are crucial and threatened by climate change, habitat loss, and other pressures.
In honour of the late bee scientist Sheila Colla, this presentation will offer practical tips on planting and maintaining gardens that provide beautifully blooming habitat for pollinators, with a particular focus on how native plants support wild bees.
Presented by
Lorraine Johnson
, who co-authored
A Garden for the Rusty-Patched Bumblebee
with Sheila Colla, as part of TPL's environmental program series,
Our Fragile Planet
, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​

title: Toronto Star Live at Soulpepper: In Conversation with Jennifer Shahade The Next Move
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
Jennifer Shahade on strategy, power and seeing the board differently.

Chess master Jennifer Shahade, author of Thinking Sideways and Chess Queens, joins Star Opinion Editor Jordan Himelfarb, author of his own book on chess, for an interactive conversation about strategy, decision-making and how to see the board differently when the obvious move fails. Drawing on chess, poker, gender and power, this event will invite audiences to think in moves, countermoves and possibilities — and to ask what changes when we stop looking for the right answer and start looking for the better move.

In this interactive session, participants will explore the concept of Resilient Flow and how our beliefs, habits, and ways of making sense of the world influence how we respond under pressure.
Sangeetha Dikshit
, one of TPL's four Career Coaches in Residence. Sangeetha is a Career and Leadership Coach empowering individuals to navigate career transitions, develop in-demand skills, and achieve professional success.
Abirambika Ravivarman
is a Human-Centric Leadership and Systems Coach and the founder of Human Systems at Work. Her work goes beyond individual behaviour to focus on the deeper relational dynamics that shape team performance and culture. In today’s AI-augmented workplace, she emphasizes the importance of strengthening the Human Edge—the presence-based and relational capabilities that enable leaders and teams to thrive in complexity.

title: National Housing Day: A Film Screening and Panel Discussion of Seeking Shelter
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall (1st floor)
description:
On November 24
th
, join Homeless Connect Toronto at the Toronto Reference Library for a special premiere screening and community conversation celebrating the launch of Seeking Shelter, a documentary series by filmmaker Nadine Valcin.
As Canada continues to grapple with a growing housing crisis, Seeking Shelter shines a light on the people, organizations, and grassroots movements creating innovative and inclusive solutions to housing instability. Through stories of resilience, collaboration, and community action, the series explores what becomes possible when people come together to reimagine housing.
This special event will feature premiere screenings of:
Episode 2: Communal Land for the Common Good :
Toronto’s Parkdale Neighbourhood Land Trust is sowing the seeds for innovative housing and communal growth.
And
Episode 3: Co-ops and the Power of Community:
Since the 1970s, a Toronto co-operative has modelled a collaborative and people-first approach to housing.
Following the screenings, filmmaker Nadine Valcin will moderate a panel discussion with housing subject-matter experts, exploring the themes raised in the films and the future of community-driven housing solutions. Audience members will also have an opportunity to participate in a Q&A and contribute reflections to a collaborative poll.
Doors open: 6pm
The episodes are provided courtesy of the National Film Board of Canada.

title: Your Health Matters: Breast Cancer Screening and Early Detection
description:
Breast cancer is one of the most common cancers affecting women, but early detection can significantly improve outcomes. Understanding your risk, knowing when to get screened, and recognizing potential warning signs are important steps in protecting your health.

Understanding Breast Cancer:

Screening and Early Detection:
Understand who should be screened, why early detection matters, and what to expect during the screening process.
Recognizing Warning Signs:
Learn about potential signs and symptoms of breast cancer and the role of breast self-examination and assessment.
Accessing Care and Support:
Learn about the Ontario Breast Screening Program and resources available to support people living with breast cancer.
This session will be led by staff from LAMP Community Health Centre, who will provide practical information and guidance to help you better understand breast cancer screening and the resources available to support your health.

description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads ***Yesteryear*** by Caro Claire Burke.
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/4849281772290048) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"A traditional American woman, a beautiful wife and mother who sells her pioneer lifestyle of raw milk and farm-fresh eggs to her millions of social media followers, suddenly awakens cold, filthy, and terrified in the brutal reality of 1855—where she must unravel whether this living nightmare is an elaborate hoax, a twisted reality show, or something far more sinister." (from [BookMarks](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/yesteryear/))

"The chasm between social media and reality runs deep and dark in Caro Claire Burke’s debut novel, “Yesteryear,” which crawls into the psyche of a tradwife influencer so maddening and mesmerizing that Anne Hathaway has already signed on to play her in the movie adaptation.
“Sometimes it actually made me sick,” Natalie Heller Mills narrates, “how perfect my life was, and how good I was at living it.” Note her use of the past tense." (from [New York Times Book Review](https://archive.ph/WHSQ6#selection-753.0-764.0))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Jeff Chang: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL presents award-winning author Jeff Chang in conversation with Vinh Nguyen at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon, celebrating what would have been Bruce Lee's birthday.
More than half a century after his death, Bruce Lee remains as towering a figure as ever, the man who popularized martial arts in the West, became a bridge between Eastern and Western culture, and was poised to conquer Hollywood when he died suddenly at age thirty-two. But in the decades since, his legend has eclipsed the man. Forgotten is the immigrant, the fighter, the seeker, the teacher, the father grappling with exile and belonging in a country that questioned his right to simply exist.
In his epic new cultural biography
Water Mirror Echo: Bruce Lee and the Making of Asian America
, acclaimed author Jeff Chang recovers the man behind the icon. Drawing on in-depth interviews with Lee's closest intimates, thousands of newly available personal documents, and dozens of rare photographs from the family archive, Chang traces Lee's remarkable journey: a charismatic child star turned delinquent teen fighter in Hong Kong, exiled alone to America, who transformed personal struggle into a philosophy of movement and being. Chang reveals how Lee's rise didn't just create a Hollywood legend, it helped birth something even more enduring: the very concept of Asian America.
Join Jeff Chang for a special evening honouring Bruce Lee's birthday, offering a stirringly human portrait of the icon, the immigrant, and the movement he unknowingly ignited.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.

description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Research rarely progresses in a straight line. title: Wednesday Afternoon @ the Movies: One False Move
description:
Join us on Wednesday afternoon at the library for a screening of One False Move movie.
A small-town police chief conceals an explosive secret. A pair of ruthless drug dealers leave a bloody trail in their wake as they make their way from Los Angeles to Arkansas. And an enigmatic woman is caught in the middle. The way these desperate lives converge becomes a masterclass in slow-burn tension thanks to the nuanced direction of Carl Franklin, whose haunting debut feature travels a crooked road across America’s most fraught divisions—urban and rural, Black and white—while imbuing noir conventions with a wrenching emotional depth.

title: CRA Personal Finance
description:
Make the Most of Your Tax Return & Protect Yourself from Financial Scams
A representative from the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) will explain how filing your taxes can help you access benefits and credits you may be eligible to receive. The representative will also discuss how to recognize scams and fraud, the different methods used by scammers, how to protect your personal and financial information, and what steps to take if you believe you have been targeted.  Learn about available programs, eligibility requirements, and how to apply. Topics may include:
Canada Groceries and Essentials Benefit (CGEB)
Canada Child Benefit (CCB)
Canada Workers Benefit (CWB)
Disability Tax Credit (DTC)
Child Disability Benefit
Canada Caregiver Credit
Eligibility for benefits and credits
Registraion is required.

title: Vibe Coding: Make Your Own Interactive Story with AI
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
What if you could write a story where the reader chooses what happens, like a branching adventure, a mystery, or a game, and have AI build it with you?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll learn "vibe-coding": using an AI coding assistant to build your own interactive story or simple game. You'll design the branches, describe the rules in plain language, test for the tricky edge cases (what if the player picks the weird option?), and end up with a single file you can share with anyone. Just a story you want to tell. This is the playful sibling of the practical vibe-coding workshop.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.
If you wish to save your work from this hands-on program, please bring your own USB stick.

This program includes activities that use agentic AI tools (listed below) on library laptops.
You do not need to create your own account for this program.
Participants are encouraged to follow the Resident’s guidance throughout sessions, which include best practices on using AI.

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

At checkout, you will see the CAD price, but your bank will automatically convert it to your local currency. See tickets for estimated USD conversions! Canadian Locals: If you are based in Canada and experiencing financial barriers, enter promo code CANADALOCAL at checkout to unlock our $20 CAD support tier. --- Live on Zoom. Recording available to ticketholders for 14 days after class! Get the Total Desire Pass to save on all 5 classes in the Psychology & Instinct Series! --- Have you ever wondered why you think so differently as a pet? Maybe you start to see your inner pet come out in your everyday life? You may be surprised to learn how much of pet play and headspace can be explained by surprisingly common psychological concepts that fit into your daily life (or the daily lives of your average vanilla friend). Join Pup Ryder, to learn about how various aspects of psychology play a role in your headspace, pet-self, and dynamics, while also learning about some psychological tips and tricks that you may be able to add in to really play with your pet’s head. --- Get the Total Desire Pass to save on all 5 classes in the Psychology & Instinct Series! This also includes a FREE month of the new Wolfe Academy of Desire Patreon + 15% off a one-on-one coaching session. NOTE: This class will not be uploaded onto the Patreon. --- About the Instructor Pup Ryder (he/him) is a member of the Toronto pet play community, previously holding a role as an event organizer. He is currently pursuing a PhD in psychology examining the formation of boundaries in power exchange relationships. His past research, as well as several ongoing research projects also revolve around pet play experiences, headspace, and different roles within pet play communities. Access: This class is offered live and online through Zoom. You may need to download the free, basic version of the Zoom app to join. The class will be recorded with the recording available to ticketholders for 14 days. Zoom now provides closed captioning which will be available for this event. ‍

location: Fred Thury Studio Theatre, 258 Vanier College
description:
An Original Version of Miss Braddon’s popular Novel, In Two Acts by C. H. Hazelwood Adapted from the 1862 novel of the same name, Lady Audley’s Secret is a classic example of Victorian melodrama. Concerning the ambitious, unscrupulous Lady Audley who, in order to preserve her present situation is prepared, when an unwanted husband returns, to attempt to get rid of him in the garden well. But she is observed – and struggle and twist as she may, neither bribery nor attempted arson avail her. Nemesis overtakes her and tragedy ensues. Find out what she is hiding and the lengths to which she will go to in order to protect Lady Audley’s Secret.

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Disruptors & Dilemmas — Surviving the smoke: The new reality of wildfires
description:
Register now!   
Wildfires are no longer distant events unfolding deep in remote forests. As fires grow more frequent and intense, their impacts are increasingly felt in our cities, communities and the air we breathe. How do wildfires reshape the future of our forests, cities and climate? 
Join University of Toronto experts for an engaging discussion on the science, technology and human realities of wildfires. Explore how robotics and aerial monitoring are changing the way fires are tracked, why wildfire smoke poses growing challenges for urban centres and how communities can adapt in a world where fire is both a natural part of the landscape and an escalating public concern. 
From public health and environmental justice to urban planning and climate resilience, discover how the decisions we make today will shape our ability to live with fire tomorrow. 
This is a Disruptors and Dilemmas speaker series event.This event is co-hosted by: University of Toronto Faculty of Applied Science and Engineering, Temerty Faculty of Medicine and University of Toronto Mississauga.

title: Recovery College- Balance & Build Week 6: Managing Academic Stress & Exam Anxiety
description:

title: Recovery College: YU & Balance Week 6 | Managing academic stress and exam anxiety
description:
This session will be offered in person at York University’s Markham Campus and is open to students from all York University campuses.
Sometimes, a single grade can get inside your head and make you question your ability to succeed in your program. The pressure to earn high marks, often called “academic perfectionism”, is something many post-secondary students experience.
In this week’s session of YU & Balance, participants will explore how stress affects academic performance and learn practical strategies to manage it as you prepare for exam season. By the end of the session, participants will have tools to recognize stress, respond to it effectively, and protect your confidence during exams.
This session is part of a 6-week Recovery College series. For each session attended, participants will receive $5 on their YU-card. To receive the gift card, you must attend the full session (approximately 45–60 minutes). Unfortunately, we’re not able to provide gift cards for partial attendance. Gift cards will be emailed after the session to the same email address used to register and join the session.
Space is limited, and registration is offered on a first-come, first-served basis. If the session is full and you’d like to be added to the waitlist, please email hstacey@yorku.ca ( mailto:hstacey@yorku.ca ). We’ll reach out if a spot becomes available. If you’re registered but can no longer attend, please let us know as soon as you can so we can offer your spot to another student.

title: How Pleasant to Know Mr. Lear
description:
Dennis Duffy, Professor Emeritus, Department of English, University of Toronto, discusses the genius of Edward Lear as a painter and poet, the great joiner of oil painting and printed nonsense.
Lear was a singular eccentric in his bespoke but loosely-fitting suits and his runcible hat, he created work placing him among the finest of graphic cartoonists and satirists. This presentation explores that jagged world that he made up for himself, in order to preserve his own complex selfhood.

title: Low Income Retirement Planning
description:
November is Financial Literacy Month
Learn about government benefits, tax credits, and strategies to help protect your retirement income. Presented by John Stapleton from Open Policy Ontario.
These sessions are designed for seniors with low income and those who advise them.
Registration not required. Drop-in welcome.
Thursday Oct 1: What Do Seniors Get?
Learn about benefits for older adults living in Ontario, including Canada Pension Plan (CPP), Old Age Security (OAS), Guaranteed Income Supplement (GIS), and Guaranteed Annual Income Supplement (GAINS).
Thursday Oct 15: Understanding the Personal Income Tax System.
What is a taxable income and how can tax credits, deductions, entitlements and exemptions help to reduce taxable income.
Thursday Oct 29: Protecting Your Retirement Income.
Learn how to reduce claw backs to GIS and GAINS payments if receiving additional income from employment, a private pension, or a Registered Retirement Savings Plan (RRSP).
Thursday Nov 12: Coming to Canada and Leaving Canada.
Learn about eligible benefits for those that resided in Canada for fewer than 40 years between the ages of 18 and 65, or for those planning on emigrating from Canada after retiring.
Thursday Nov 26: Tax Credits and Benefits for Seniors and People with Disabilities.
Learn about other tax credits and benefits for seniors, people with disabilities, and caregivers, including the disability tax credit, the Canada caregiver credit, and the home accessibility tax credit.
One-on-one support is available at select branches. Meet with Financial Empowerment staff for free financial counselling. Book your free appointment today. Speak with branch staff or visit

title: Coding with Python II
description:
Python is an open source programming language that is used for creating web applications, web content, mathematics and system scripting. In this second Python session we will leverage everything we learned about loops and blocks in part one to create our very own functions. We'll take a look at how to approach function design, how to allow users to enter data into functions through arguments, and how to get our functions to return results. title: Alderwood Book Club: Clara at the Door With a Revolver
description:
In November we will be discussing the non-fiction book
Clara at the Door With a Revolver
by Carolyn Whitzman.
“In the autumnal darkness of October 6, 1894, an unseen figure rang the doorbell at the Parkdale home of a well-to-do Toronto family and then shot eighteen-year-old Frank Westwood in his doorway, murdering him in cold blood.
Six weeks later, Clara Ford, a Black tailor and single mother, was arrested. Known for her impeccable work ethic and her resolute personality - and for her predilection for wearing men’s attire – she confessed to the murder.
But as the details of her arrest and her complex connection to the Westwood family emerged, Clara recanted, testifying that she had been coerced by police into a false confession.”

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

title: Computers for Beginners
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: Journée pédagogique: Explorum - Bombes à bain
description:
L’expérience des bombes à bain est une expérience simple qui illustre une des réactions chimiques les plus communes : la neutralisation acidobasique qui forme un sel et de l'eau. Cette activité relaxante permet aux enfants de faire leur propre bombe à bain et de comprendre que cette réaction produit du gaz (des bulles) ; ils apprennent que l’acide contient du cations H+ et que la base contient des anions OH- qui réagissent ensemble pour former du sel et de l'eau. Chaque participant combine ses ingrédients et confectionne sa propre bombe à bain qu’il emporte avec lui emballée dans un petit sac en cellophane.
The bath bomb experience is a simple activity that illustrates one of the most common chemical reactions: acid-base neutralization, which forms a salt and water. This relaxing activity allows children to create their own bath bomb and understand that this reaction produces gas (bubbles). They learn that the acid contains H+ ions and the base contains OH- ions, which react together to form salt and water. Each participant combines their ingredients and crafts their own bath bomb to take home, packaged in a small cellophane bag.

title: Internet Horror Classics on Film: We're All Going to the World's Fair
description:
In this third instalment of Toronto Public Library's virtual series Internet Horror Classics on Film, crime writer Kathleen Hale and film critic Willow Maclay discuss Jane Schoenbrun's coming-of-age psychological horror film, We're All Going to the World's Fair alongside host Adam Nayman.
About this event's guests:
Kathleen Hale
is a crime writer based in Los Angeles. Her reporting has been featured in Vanity Fair, among other outlets. Slenderman is her first true crime book.
Willow Maclay
is a freelance film critic stationed in St. John's, Newfoundland. She has written for outlets such as The Village Voice, Ebert Voices, Cinemascope Magazine, and more. She is also the co-author of Corpses, Fools and Monsters: An Examination of Transgender Cinema.
Adam Nayman
is a critic, teacher, and author, whose books include critical surveys of the Coen Brothers, Paul Thomas Anderson, and most recently, in Mind Games, the filmmaker David Fincher. He is a regular contributor to The Ringer, a lecturer at the University of Toronto's Cinema Studies Institute, and he has written on film for The New Yorker and The New York Times.
Read more:
Corpses, Fools and Monsters
