title: Robotics Institute Seminar: Steven Waslander, “TankerVision: Turning Firefighting Flights into a Wildfire Behaviour Dataset”
location: Bahen Centre for Information Technology, Room 1190, or on Zoom, 40 St George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5S 2E4, Canada
description:
Join in-person (BA1190) or online (Zoom) 
TankerVision: Turning Firefighting Flights into a Wildfire Behaviour Dataset
Abstract
Models of wildfire rate of spread, intensity and spotting still rely mostly on small experimental burns from decades ago. Fires are hardest to observe exactly when it matters most, during rapid, intense spread. Satellites are too coarse in space and time, and drones and research aircraft are kept out of fire airspace. The only platforms reliably overhead during a major run are the aircraft fighting the fire. 
TankerVision turns these operational flights into a continuous, automated source of fire behaviour data. Working with Conair Aerial Firefighting, the BC Wildfire Service and Alberta Wildfire, we developed a self-contained imaging unit for the bird-dog aircraft that direct airtanker operations. It records georeferenced colour and thermal infrared imagery whenever the aircraft is near a fire, with no action required from the crew. A prototype flew roughly 50 missions over 30 fires from Kamloops in 2025. 
With support from DRDC and NRCan, three upgraded aircraft flew fires across five provinces and territories in 2026. An automated pipeline segments fire and smoke, reconstructs georeferenced 3D fire fronts and derives rate-of-spread observations from successive passes. The result is the first large multi-pass, multi-fire dataset of active wildfire behaviour, a foundation for data-driven fire prediction models, with an initial public release planned for December 2026. 
About Steven Waslander
Prof. Steven Waslander is a leading authority on autonomous vehicles, including multirotor drones and autonomous driving vehicles.  He received his B.Sc.E.in 1998 from Queen’s University, his M.S. in 2002 and his Ph.D. in 2007, both from Stanford University in Aeronautics and Astronautics, where as a graduate student he created the Stanford Testbed of Autonomous Rotorcraft for Multi-Agent Control (STARMAC), the world’s most capable outdoor multi-vehicle quadrotor platform at the time. He was recruited to Waterloo from Stanford in 2008, where he founded and directed the Waterloo Autonomous Vehicle Laboratory (WAVELab), extending the state of the art in autonomous drones and autonomous driving through advances in localization and mapping, object detection and tracking, integrated planning and control methods and multi-robot coordination. His work on autonomous vehicles has resulted in the Autonomoose, the first autonomous vehicle created at a Canadian University to drive on public roads. In 2018, he joined the University of Toronto Institute for Aerospace Studies (UTIAS), and founded the Toronto Robotics and Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (TRAILab). Starting in July of 2026, he became the director of the University of Toronto Robotics Institute. 
Join in-person (BA1190) or online (Zoom)

title: The Myth of “Samshu”: Smell, Race, and the Making of Chinatown in North America, 1880s–1920s
description:
What did Chinatown smell like to outsiders a century ago? How could an unfamiliar distilled drink
become a symbol of racial and cultural difference? Between the 1880s and the 1920s, Chinese
immigrant communities in North America encountered growing scrutiny of their businesses,
customs, and everyday lives. Among the objects attracting attention was “samshu,” a term found in
English-language descriptions of Chinese distilled spirits. Its reputation became entangled with
accounts of Chinatown, unfamiliar odours, drinking practices, illicit alcohol, and anxieties about
immigration.
This lecture investigates how descriptions of samshu circulated within the cultural imagination of
North American society. Moving among sensory impressions, racialized representations, and the
history of bootlegging and alcohol regulation, it asks how ordinary experiences of smell and taste
could become markers of inclusion and exclusion. The lecture also asks audiences to distinguish
claims made about Chinese communities from the more complicated realities of their lives. In doing
so, it explores how historical encounters produce durable ideas about “us” and “them.”
Presenter: Dr. Jackson Yue Bin Guo | Sessional Lecturer II, Global Asia Studies / History,
University of Toronto Scarborough | Founder, Aprilum Lyceum
Jackson Yue Bin Guo received his Ph.D. in History from the University of Toronto in 2023. He
researches food and drink, law, sensory experience, material culture, and everyday life in late
imperial and modern China. His current book manuscript, Governing Intoxication: Alcohol and the
Convergence of Sensory Life in Late Imperial and Modern China, explores the social, cultural, and
regulatory histories of distilled alcohol. His scholarship has appeared in Global Food History and

title: De Profundis: Oscar Wilde in Jail
location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

description:
Since 2021, the Fusion Festival has brought together writers, directors and actors to workshop and develop new works by Canadian playwrights & screenwriters. The program will provide opportunities for artists to develop their work, with selected scripts showcase at our annual Fusion Festival!

SPOTTER

Featuring: Patrick S. McEwen & Blake Pyne

When Kai nearly injures himself during a bench press, Tyler steps in and offers to be his spotter. The two men form an unlikely connection that sparks conversations about body image, modern dating, and the way gay men see each other.

KILL TEST

Featuring: Marisa Roggeveen, Andy Kalirai, & Scott Clark

A rookie operative must extract information from a captive while her mentor tests her resolve.

Join us at Naturlandia on November 27 th at 8:30pm for an evening of new Canadian theatre.

Come experience original storytelling, support emerging Canadian artists, and help us continue our tradition of bringing bold new orks to the stage and screen!

title: Holiday Succulent Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us this holiday season and create a one-of-a-kind succulent!
Celebrate the festive season with a delightful holiday-inspired succulent arranging workshop! In this creative and relaxing session, you’ll design a beautiful succulent arrangement in a charming birch-lined tin planter—perfect for adding a touch of natural elegance to your holiday décor or gifting to someone special.
 
Guided by a succulent expert, you’ll learn tips and tricks for arranging succulents with a seasonal flair, including techniques for layering textures, balancing colours, and incorporating winter-inspired accents.
 
All materials are provided, including a birch-lined tin planter, premium succulents, specialty soil, and care instruction cards to ensure your arrangement stays vibrant through the holiday season and beyond.
 
Join us for this festive workshop and leave with a stunning centrepiece that captures the warmth and beauty of the holidays!
 
Saturday, November 28, 10 to 11 a.m.
Public $55, TBG Members $50 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Canadian Succulents
Molly is the owner and operator of the small business Canadian Succulents. Canadian Succulents creates floral arrangements using entirely succulents and cacti plants. They not only arrange and design all of the creations, but also grow all the plants that can be found in them as well. They operate out of a greenhouse just northeast of the city, where they grow over 300 varieties of succulents and cacti. They grow and create these designs for wedding centrepieces and favours, corporate events and gifting, and hotel and office greenery.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!
 
Additional Program Information



Please review our Refund Policy and Terms of Agreement.
For more information on accessibility at the garden please review our Accessibility Features webpage. If you have any accessibility requirements during your program please email programsupport@torontobotanicalgarden.ca.
To learn more about the Toronto Botanical Garden and our programs, please review our list of Frequently Asked Questions.

title: Pressed Flower Candle Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a morning of hands-on pressed flower candle making!
Discover the simple, satisfying craft of flower pressing and transform a plain pillar candle into a one-of-a-kind keepsake. Using warm palette knives to gently melt pressed flowers directly into the wax, you’ll learn a technique that’s part botanical art, part patience. Choose from a variety of pressed flowers to design your own arrangement. Beginners welcome.
 
Each attendee will receive one 6″ white pillar candle, a full selection of pressed flowers to choose from, and step-by-step guidance on using heated palette knives safely to melt your design into the wax.
 
Saturday, November 28, 10 to 11:30 a.m.
Public $65, TBG Members $60 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Epiphanie Belanger
Epiphanie Belanger is the founder of HobbyHub, a community-driven platform designed to help people try new hobbies in a relaxed environment. What started as a personal curiosity for creative pursuits quickly turned into a mission to make hobbies more accessible, social, and fun for beginners.
 
Through curated workshops and experiences, Epiphanie brings people together to explore hands-on creative skills in a welcoming, low-pressure environment. title: Christmas in Old York! 1833 (RETURN FOR 2026)
description:
Toronto History Walks
\*\***The Toronto History Walks Yearly Pass is available. Get it now for $125.00 for 1 year of unlimited tours, email**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**
**for more information or for signing up!\*\***

\*\* **Please note: Please e-transfer the ticket amount when booking your space for this tour! You can e-transfer to the following email at:**
**torontohistorywalks@gmail.com**

**If you plan on attending, please get your tickets for this event early as this tour has run for the last 3 years, and does sell out rather quickly.**

So what was it like in York in 1833 at Christmas time?

The prices of various food items and gifts on display, the gas lights creating a glow as the snow begins, places to gather, places to get a drink, like the Steamboat Hotel on Front Street, or maybe one might decide to take their best girl or guy on a stagecoach trip to High Park to watch kids speed down the hills on their skids.

What were the traditions in old York? Maybe the residents went down to the lake and watched the nighttime fishermen spear fish for Christmas dinner. Let's take a trip around old York and see what it was like back in 1833, three months before we changed our name to Toronto in 1834.

Or take a holiday trip to Kingston or Montreal to buy gifts directly from New York or London stores, fancy hats for the ladies and cigars for the men. Books and wooden toys for the kids. What about that goose in the little grocery store on King Street West of Jarvis? Candies from Britain, real home made gingerbread in the store windows.

On Christmas Eve everyone walked to St. James Cathedral for the ringing of the bells, singing, and skating over the frozen Toronto Bay to the Peninsula.

This tour explores old York. This walking tour is for all walking levels. The tour begins and ends at St. James Cathedral on King Street East at Church Street. A great way to kick off the season.

This tour has a ticketed price of $15.00.

title: Painting Botanical Cast Ornaments from Garden Blooms
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Learn how to create your own plant-based pigments and paint one-of-a-kind botanical cast ornaments!
Want to give a holiday gift that is not mass produced in a factory? Looking for a calming experience that beats the hustle and bustle? Join botanical artist Rebecca Fortin for an afternoon of natural paint-making and ornament painting.
 
Under Rebecca’s guidance, you’ll explore how to create colour pigments from local botanicals, such as goldenrod, nettle, berries, and more.
 
Test your plant-based pigments on watercolour paper, including creating a holiday card. Participants will choose two plaster miniature botanical casts to paint and take home or gift for the holiday season. These ornaments are created by Rebecca, each made using impressions of live botanicals. This workshop features botanical casts made with flowers directly from Toronto Botanical Garden, capturing the garden’s beauty in artwork that lasts long after the blossoms fade.
 
All materials will be provided. No prior experience required.
 
This workshop is intended for ages 16+. Mature youth aged 12+ are welcome, but must be accompanied and supervised by an adult.
 
Please note: Please wear practical clothes and footwear that you don’t mind getting a little messy. As with all handmade processes using real plants: results will vary, pigments may shift in colour over time, and each piece will have perfect imperfections that contribute to its unique character.
 
Saturday, November 28, 1 to 4 p.m.
Public $115, TBG Members $110 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Rebecca Fortin
Rebecca Fortin is a visual artist based in rural Whitby, Ontario, where she creates botanical artwork rooted in the textures, colours, and quiet beauty of the plants around her. After a 20-year career in public health administration, Rebecca pivoted to focus on her art practice, completing the Drawing and Painting program at the Haliburton School of Art + Design in 2022. She now works full-time as an artist, bringing together her background in community health promotion with her passion for connecting people to nature through art.
 
Rebecca’s work has been shown across Ontario and is held in private and corporate collections in Canada and internationally. Her hands-on workshops invite participants to explore botanicals and natural art materials — offering memorable, calming experiences and the opportunity to create beautiful, one-of-a-kind pieces to take home.
 
Follow Rebecca on Instagram.

description:
Toronto Japanese English Exchange (TJEX.ca)
～English description below～

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は＄2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は＄5を先払いにて頂いております。

皆さんから頂いたお金は、こちらのサイトの維持費や将来のランゲージエクスチェンジ施設利用料やソーシャルイベント等のために使われます。ご理解の程、よろしくお願いいたします。

予約受付開始：土曜日5:00PM

予約取消締切：土曜日14:00PM(当日)

予約受付締切：土曜日15:00PM(当日)

スケジュール

5.15 PM - 5:30PM - チェックイン、グループ分け

5:30 PM - 6:15PM - 日本語の時間［または英語の時間］

6:15PM - 7:00 PM - 英語の時間［または日本語の時間］

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

開催場所：Atrium フードコート

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントにお申し込みをされる際、皆様一度ウェイティングリストへ自動的に移動されます。当日のオーガナイザーが人数調整を行い、基本は先着順にてお一人ずつへE-transfer先を記載したメッセージを送ります。こちらでお支払いを確認した後、オーガナイザーが参加者リストへ移動します。一度お支払いされますと、払い戻しや振替は出来ませんのでご了承ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

※ご注意※

・空席ができた際は、自動的に”キャンセル待ち”より”参加予定”へ変更されます。この時にMeetupよりお知らせがあるかはわかりません。

・システムにより自動的に”参加予定”とされ、それに気づかずに参加しなかった場合でも、不参加とみなされますのでご了承ください。

Instagramアカウント @tjex.ca

最新情報やミートアップの様子を掲載しています。

ぜひこちらもフォローお願いします！

Although our group is a non-profit organization, we collect $ 5 per English Speaker for every event. All the proceeds are used to run this website and for social events

Canadian English speakers must be Native or Fluent in English in order to participate

RSVP:
RSVP open: 5:00 PM

RSVP cancel deadline: Saturday, 2:00 PM (day of the event)

RSVP close: Saturday, 3:00 PM (day of the event)

Day of Event:
5:15 PM - 5:30 PM - Check-in and Group placement

5:30 PM - 6:15 PM - Japanese conversation

6:15 PM - 7:00 PM - English conversation

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

Optional Dinner :
After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.
However, Dinner is only for Participants that joined on the day of the event.

Event Location:
Atrium Food Court

The food court is directly connected to the Dundas subway station. Leave the subway station and walk west along Dundas Street.

At the intersection of Bay Street and Dundas Street, you will find an entrance. Proceed down the escalator.

The food court is on the basement floor. Please talk to the organizer with the signboard showing TJEX. (If you can’t find them, please send a message to the organizer.)

⚠️RSVP & Late Policy:
If you are unable to join on the day of the event, please change your status from 'going-list' to 'not going-list'. Failure to Not show up will result in 1 No -Show. Also, in case of arriving 15 mins late to the event will result in 1 No-Show.

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List and Fee transfer:
Once you enter the "Waiting-list", we will message you for the payment via e-transfer. After your payment is confirmed, you will be moved to the "Going-list"

There are no Refunds or Carryovers.

Going List:
Only Members on the going-list can participate on the day of the event.

Find yourself on the frontier of Carson McHone's imagination with The Pentimento Performance Project. Created in collaboration with dramaturge Deana Jones and choreographer Allie Blumas, this multidisciplinary project weaves light, shadow, and dance into a live performance of McHone's newest album, Pentimento.


Community collaboration brings the project to life, with McHone’s live performance including artists in the forefront of Canada’s folk rock and guitar scene: Daniel Romano and Tommy Major (Daniel Romano’s Outfit), Steven Lambke (Constantines), and composer Michael Cloud Duguay.


The evening starts with Toronto’s Potions, a freak-folk quartet with involved and concerned lyrical stylings. Potions crafts a perfect mix for lovers of the archival and the new, the online and the analogue.


Wavelength’s final monthly show of 2026 promises a tactile approach to music and movement. We invite you to come take part in this ever-forming memory!


Poster by Julia Araïche and Carson McHone

location: Soulpepper Theatre,50 Tank House Lane, Toronto, ON M5A 3C4, Canada
description:
“There is no prison in any world into which love cannot force an entrance.”

This November, Soulpepper Theatre is thrilled to bring back their award-winning musical adaptation of DE PROFUNDIS: OSCAR WILDE IN JAIL

The musical begins with Oscar Wilde languishing in a prison cell, cut off from the world that once adored him. As he writes a letter to the man he loved—memory, regret, and desire crowd the silence—turning confinement into confession.

In this intimate, 90-minute musical fantasy, Robbie Ross and Bosie emerge through Wilde’s fractured memories as as the plot thickens and audience are carried away by the original, genre-spanning score that moves from Irish ballads to Broadway and electro-pop.

Weaving together Wilde’s trial testimonies, letters and epigrams, De Profundis reveals Wilde unmasked: lover, icon and exile—insisting that even in the darkest places, love can still reach us.

Onstage at Soulpepper Theatre for a limited run from November 3rd- November 29th

title: Python Essentials 1 Learning Circle
description:
Learn Python and build your programming skills in a supportive group. This learning circle will meet on Monday evenings from November 2 to December 7, 4-6pm. Learning circles are study groups guided by staff for people who want to take a free online course together in a welcoming space. Learners meet weekly and work together through the course materials. Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.
Python Essentials 1
In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x).
For more information about the Python learning circle, please contact
networkingacademy@tpl.ca

title: AI for Small Business and Entrepreneurs
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
You've got the business idea. Now come the thousand questions: who's my customer, what's the market, how do I pitch this?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll use AI as a research and planning partner for small business. We'll practice together on a sample business, turning rough ideas into business plans, digging into markets, drafting customer-discovery questions, and building useful low-maintenance automation. The most valuable thing you'll get is usually a better question to be tested in the real world. Whether you're starting or growing, you'll leave with an experiment you can run on your own business this week.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start October 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Fourth Annual National DIVERT Meeting
description:

The program brings together researchers, clinicians, trainees and community partners to explore youth mental health, including eating disorders, screen use, digital mental health and 2SLGBTQ+ youth, and equity in mental health research and policy.

Registration: $25 for in-person attendance or $15 for virtual attendance.

location: Online Zoom Webinar @ Online Zoom Webinar
description:
The Faculty of Graduate Studies is hosting a session entitled From Research to Real-World Impact: An Introduction to Knowledge Mobilization for Graduate Student Scholars. Join us!
Research creates knowledge, but impact happens when knowledge is shared, understood, and used. This interactive session introduces graduate students to the fundamentals of Knowledge Mobilization (KMb) and explores how to move research beyond traditional academic audiences. Topics will include how to identify key audiences, develop effective knowledge-sharing strategies, build meaningful partnerships, and communicate research in ways that support social, community, policy, and professional impact. Whether you are just beginning your research journey or preparing for future careers inside or outside academia, this session will provide practical tools to help amplify the reach and relevance of your work.

title: Data Analytics Essentials Learning Circle
description:
Interested in learning about data analytics? Let's take a free online course together in a welcoming space!
A
learning circle
is a study group, guided by library staff, for people who want to take a free online course together in a supportive and welcoming environment.
Organizations all over the world recognize the value of analytics. Together, we'll learn about the essential tools used in this field.
In this 12-week learning circle, we will work through the Data Analytics Essentials course from Cisco Networking Academy. We will explore the fundamental tools of a data analyst, including how to:
transform, organize and visualize data with spreadsheet tools like Excel
query data from a relational database using SQL
improve data presentations using business intelligence tools like Tableau
We will meet weekly,
in-person,
every Tuesday afternoon, September 15 - December 8, 2-3:30 PM (12 sessions).
Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend sessions on a weekly basis.
Learners who complete the course will be able to:
earn a digital badge
download a certificate of completion

title: A Short History of Library Architecture in Toronto and Beyond
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall, 1st floor
description:
Christopher Hume, the architecture critic and urban issues columnist of the Toronto Star, presents a short history of library architecture. He will be commenting on the structures and social relevance of monumental libraries from Paris, Boston, New York, with a focus on Toronto Public Libraries from around the city.
Hume is the recipient of 2009 The National Newspaper Award for journalism in architecture and urban affairs. His illustrious career at the Toronto Star earned him a President’s Award for Architectural Journalism from the Royal Architectural Institute of Canada. Hume's book, William James’ Toronto Views, won a Toronto Heritage Award in 2000 and in 2004 he received a Landscape Ontario award.

location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Tiny Titans: Insects Up Close | Book Launch & Panel Talk with Author & Photographer Dara Ojo
location: North York Central Library, Room 101 - 1st floor
description:
Discover the hidden world of arthropods through stunning macro photography — a visual journey celebrating their beauty, complexity, and essential role in our ecosystems.
Meet
Dara Ojo
, an award-winning macro photographer and conservation storyteller whose work brings the hidden world of arthropods into vivid relief. Ojo's book,
Tiny Titans : The Silent Keepers of Our Ecosystem
reveals the fascinating lives of insects, spiders, and other small creatures that quietly sustain life on Earth. Captured across Canada, Mexico, Costa Rica, and beyond, Dara Ojo’s photography highlights the intricate details and diversity of these often-overlooked species.
Ojo will be leading the conversation with:
Dr. Sandra Rehan
, professor at York University and principal investigator of the Rehan Lab with a focus on wild bees, pollinator biology and conservation. Rehan's research explores the biology, behaviour and evolution of bees, with a particular interest in understanding and protecting native pollinators.
Dr. Laura Timms
, Senior Specialist of Natural Heritage Management at Credit Valley Conservation and Adjunct Professor with the Daniels Faculty’s Institute of Forestry and Conservation.
Lorraine Johnson
, author and native plant and ecological gardening advocate, bridging the connection between insects, plants, habitat and practical conservation action.
Join in this evening to celebrate macro photography and the intricate beauty and ecological importance of insects and spiders, creatures that quietly anchor global biodiversity, pollination, and climate resilience.
Free. Register for a reminder.
5:30 pm:
Doors open. Mingle and chat with fellow nature and environmental enthusiasts!
6:00 pm:
Presentation begins. Enjoy a highly visual presentation combining photography, science, conservation and storytelling, taking the audience behind the scenes of six years documenting tiny worlds across five continents and exploring why these overlooked species matter. A light, informal conversation with guest speakers will explore why arthropods are so essential to our ecosystems, with a discussion of challenges impacting local species, and how science, photography and art can work together to help people notice, understand and care about the natural world. An audience Q&A follows this discussion.
7:30 pm:
Book signing with books available for purchase.
***
This program is part of TPL's
Our Fragile Planet
program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.​
Questions? Please contact North York Central Library - Business, Science & Technology Department.
***
Place a hold or borrow from Toronto Public Library:
Tiny Titans : The Silent Keepers of Our Ecosystem
(book) - Dara Ojo
A Garden for the Rusty-patched Bumblebee
(book) - Lorraine Johnson
***

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

​(Random House, 2026).
Explore the stories behind twelve iconic dining rooms in homes around the world—from a Japanese samurai house to Claude Monet's brilliant yellow dining room to Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul to Jackie Kennedy’s White House—and travel through time in pursuit of the ultimate design.​
The Dining Room is an englightening and joyous celebration of history, culture and the art of dning. Presenter John Ota's charming observations of the surprising impact of dining rooms on our lives and the cherised moments we share within them will delight armchair travellers, history fanatics and interior design enthusiasts alike.

description:
Develop and exercise the skills you need to be an active participant in everyday democracy in this fun, interactive session. Democracy Fitness expands traditional ideas of what democracy is by exploring how people participate in civic life, build understanding and work together.
In this session, we’ll exercise our Compromise muscles. In a democracy, we find solutions together. When we make room for each other's approaches, more people can accept the decisions. Through a 30-min series of short, interactive exercises, you'll find out how you prefer to make decisions, practice solving a problem with those who think like you, and practice compromising with those who might think differently. This workshop will strengthen your ability to engage in meaningful dialogue.

title: Learning Things You Love with AI
location: North York Central Library, eLearning Lab
description:
Always wanted to learn to cook, draw, knit, fix a bike, or speak another language, but have trouble sticking to it? What if you had a personal AI tutor?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, learn how AI can become your personal tutor for something you love, or something new you want to fall in love with. A tutor explains things in the way you understand, asks you questions, and helps you choose what to learn next. Learn how to turn your goal into a specific, doable learning experiment: options not answers, with a practice that survives a bad day. Decide ahead of time how you'll know it's working: revise, or stop without guilt. You'll leave with a plan you actually want to try, and a sense for what AI should never decide for you.
Prerequisites: Mouse, keyboarding and internet skills. Computers are provided. No coding experience required.
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: Computers for Beginners
description:
Computers for Beginners 1: Use the Mouse
A class on how to use a mouse for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this first session you will:
Observe and practice how to operate a mouse effectively
Understand various mouse pointers and cursors
Review basic keyboard functions
Use the mouse for basic Windows functions
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a computer mouse at a basic level and will be able to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 2: Use the Keyboard
A class on basic keyboard functions for absolute beginners with little or no computer experience.
In this second session you will:
Familiarize yourself through practice with the most essential keyboard functions (alphabet, number and symbol keys)
Practice proper keyboarding posture
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use a keyboard at a beginner level and know how to go online for additional practice.
Computers for Beginners 3: Use the Internet
An introductory class on the Internet for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fourth session you will:
Understand how to read a web site address
Practice using web addresses
Search for information using a search engine
Explore a web site in detail to understand its key components
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use the internet at a beginner level and complete simple searches.
Computers for Beginners 4: Use Google Search and Maps
A class on using Google's filters, tools, and Maps for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this fifth session you will:
Use Google search tools more effectively to find websites, images, and news sites
Explore Google Maps to find addresses and get directions for transit and road travel.
Upon completion of this class students will be able to use more advanced search engine features and use Google Maps at a basic level.
Computers for Beginners 5: Use Windows
A class on essential basic Windows skills for absolute beginners with little computer experience.
In this third session you will:
Become familiar with the Windows (10) operating system
Practice using common Windows features: File Explorer, Desktop, Taskbar, Windows, Applications
Upon completion of this class students will have a basic understanding of how to create and organize files in the Windows environment.

title: Artists in the Library: Origami Lotus Flowers
description:
This is a six-part workshop series that creates a space for exploring belonging and not belonging through conversation and hands-on art-making. Guided by reflective questions, participants engage in practices such as origami with washi, drawing, dyeing, and writing, using the lotus as a shared symbol of transformation and resilience across cultures. The workshops foster an inclusive, supportive environment, particularly for those who feel marginalized or disconnected. The series culminates in a collaborative public floral installation in the library, sharing participants’ work with the wider community.
Led by artists "Being~inbetween"
The workshops are open to youth, ages 13-17, and require no prior artistic experience.

title: Art of Darkness: Edgar Allan Poe's Life & Work
location: Toronto Reference Library, Appel Salon, Second Floor
description:
Professor Emily Ogden shares her intimate inquiry into the shadowy life and compelling work of the definitive author of the macabre.
Since Edgar Allan Poe’s mysterious death in 1849, his stories and poems have captivated millions of readers around the world. Nearly two centuries later, why do we continue to descend into the darkness of his imagination—and of the genres, from horror to crime, that he pioneered?
In Darkness Becomes Bright, Ogden plumbs the darkness within Poe and enters it alongside him. She interweaves stories from his mysterious and tragic life with those of his most famous readers and translators, showing us how Poe’s vision echoes across the generations, allowing us to make peace with our own flawed humanity.
Emily Ogden speaks with author and critic Naben Ruthnum about the brief life and immortal art of Edgar Allan Poe.
Q&A and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this event’s guests:

title: Vietnam & Cambodia with Angkor Wat! Ancient Kingdoms of Southeast Asia!!
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
A Meetup trip in December . . . what can be a better gift for the holidays?! Join our travelers group on a captivating 14-day journey through the heart of Southeast Asia as we explore the vibrant cultures and breathtaking landscapes of Vietnam & Cambodia (Dec 04-18, 2026)

As with all our tailor-made Meetup trips, our expert guides will lead us off the beaten path to uncover the authentic charm of each destination, while comfortable accommodations and delicious local cuisine ensure a truly immersive travel experience. Embark on an unforgettable journey through the vibrant cities and breathtaking landscapes of Vietnam, finishing with the wonders of Cambodia.

We begin in Hanoi, where history and culture come alive, then sail the emerald waters of Halong Bay. Step back in time among the imperial treasures of Hue, wander the lantern-lit streets of charming Hoi An, and feel the dynamic energy of Ho Chi Minh City. We conclude your adventure at the awe-inspiring temples of Siem Reap, home to the legendary Angkor Wat.

TRIP HIGHLIGHTS:

* **Hanoi**; explore Ho Chi Minh sites, Temple of Literature, Old Quarter cyclo ride & water puppet show
* Visit rural **craft villages**: conical hat & incense making, home-hosted lunch, village walk
* **Ha Long Bay cruise**: limestone islands, floating villages, cave visit, Tai Chi & sunset views
* **Hue**: Perfume River boat ride, Thien Mu Pagoda, Khai Dinh’s Tomb & Imperial Citadel
* Scenic **Hai Van Pass train** to Danang; explore Dragon Bridge, Cham Museum, Marble Mountain
* **Hoi An Ancient Town** (UNESCO), visit tailor shops, pottery village & organic farm with cooking class
* **Ho Chi Minh City & Cu Chi Tunnels**; War Remnants Museum, Reunification Palace & Ben Thanh Market
* **Mekong Delta cruise**: coconut workshops, sampan ride, orchards & lunch in riverside village
* **Siem Reap**: dinner with Apsara dance, Angkor temples (Ta Prohm, Bayon, Angkor Wat)
* Cambodian cultural immersion: **monk blessing**, village crafts & cooking, **Tonle Sap Lake sunset cruise**

For a detailed Day By Day itinerary: **[Click Here](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)**[ to fill out our info request form](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

title: AI for Us: Shaping AI in Toronto
description:
Toronto is one of the biggest AI cities in the world. But what do the people here actually think about it and how do we want to shape its development and use?
A panel of experts, alongside our Innovator-in-Residence
Ryan Kelln
, who know AI from very different angles, unite for an open conversation about what AI is doing to this city, and what we want it to do instead. We'll talk about:
The human beings behind the machines: what drives the people who build AI, and what worries them.
Work, money, and meaning: what happens to jobs, creativity, and value when AI lands here.
Who gets to shape it and who's left out (both are our neighbours).
The stories we tell: how art, media, news, and everyday talk shape what we expect, fear, and hope for.
No pitches, no boosterism. Just an honest conversation about the ideas and stories shaping AI in this city, and what we want it to become.
Featuring:
Jerrold McGrath
, Cultural Programmer and Theorist, In the Meantime
Joseph Wilson
, Anthropologist & Author of Humans of AI: Understanding the Humans Behind the Machines
Owais Lightwala
, Assistant Professor, Performance at The Creative School at Toronto Metropolitan University, Director,
Chrysalis
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.

Sarah Zanchetta (she/they) is a queer textile artist and educator whose practice dives into the loss of connection and knowledge of poisonous plants in North America. title: Growing Native Plants From Seed
description:
Growing native plants from seed is an inexpensive and easy way to add plants to your garden – but you need to start early! Many native plants require several months of cold temperatures to sprout in the spring. Join this session with Toronto Master Gardeners to learn where to get your seed and how to sow it over the winter for germination in the spring. At the end of the program, native seeds will be given out to attendees, while supplies last. Suitable for gardeners of any skill level, with any kind of outdoor space.
This program is part of TPL's Our Fragile Planet program series, supported by Friends of Toronto Public Library, South Chapter.
Registration recommended, drop-in welcome space permitting.

title: Paper Quilling: Holiday Gnome Workshop
location: Toronto Botanical Garden, 777 Lawrence Ave E, Toronto, ON, M3C 1P2, Canada
description:
Join us for a fun-filled workshop on paper quilling and learn how to make amazing art with paper strips!
In the spirit of the holidays, join us for a creative and relaxing experience surrounded by the beauty of Toronto Botanical Garden! In this hands-on workshop, you’ll learn the art of paper quilling and create a stunning artwork from paper strips.
 
Perfect for beginners and craft lovers alike, this session will guide you step by step through rolling, shaping, and assembling paper strips into a masterpiece on a 5″x7″ canvas. Whether you’re coming with friends, family, or enjoying some creative “me time,” you’ll leave with a beautiful handmade piece and a new skill to cherish
 
All materials provided. Suitable for adults and children ages 10 and above.
 
Saturday, December 5, 2 to 4 p.m.
Public $50, TBG Members $45 (plus applicable taxes and fees).
 
About Deepa Krishnan
Deepa Krishnan is a self-taught artist specializing in the art of paper quilling, which involves manipulating narrow strips of paper to create exquisite designs. She discovered this art form when she was looking for a creative outlet from her engineering job. She was amazed by the possibilities and beauty of paper quilling, that she decided to pursue it as a full-time career. Since then, she has been passionately mastering this technique and has created many artworks drawing inspiration from nature, music and travel. She cuts the paper strips in different widths to add depth and dimension to her creations. She loves to play with the colours and experiment with the quilling techniques to create her own distinctive style. Deepa believes that anyone can learn this art form, regardless of their age or skill level and she hosts many workshops to spread the joy of quilling. She enjoys seeing her students discover their own creativity and style in paper quilling.
 
Join Toronto Botanical Garden
Join the Toronto Botanical Garden (TBG) as a member to get a discount on this program, upcoming events and classes, and free parking. A TBG membership helps you deepen your knowledge and connection to the natural world, become a part of a dynamic community of plant people, and be inspired! Become a member!

title: Shedding light on the dark side of the Universe
description:
The standard model of cosmology tells us that the Universe is mostly made up of ‘Dark Matter’, with normal matter contributing only about 15% of the total budget. However, direct detections have not yielded any results about the nature of this mysterious dark matter, leaving us with only indirect means of inferring its existence and distribution. I will try to answer tantalizing questions about its nature, and how it may have helped shape the Universe.
This talk will be given by Dr. Pratika Dayal from the Dunlap Institute for Astronomy & Astrophysics at the University of Toronto.
No registration is required, but registering will make sure you receive a reminder.

イベント参加費として、日本人の方(日本で生まれ育ち、現在英語を勉強している方)は＄2、日本人以外の方(日本語を勉強している方)は＄5を先払いにて頂いております。

【イベント内容】

Language Exchangeへようこそ！このグループでは、皆さんのレベルに応じて、3〜4名のグループにわかれ、同じ席になった人たちで各45分間、それぞれ英語と日本語でフリートークを行なっていただきます。決まったディスカッショントピックなどはございませんので、気軽に質問をしながらそれぞれのセッションを楽しんでいただければと思います。

TJEXのサインボードを持ったオーガナイザーにお声がけください。(もしサインがなかったり、わからなければメッセージをお願いします！)

予約規約（⚠️重要）

・当日の不参加、もしくは15分以上の遅刻、また予約取消締切後の変更は原則不参加(No-Show)とみなします。不参加(No-show)が3回になりますと会員登録が抹消され、退会となりますのでご注意ください。

・イベントにお申し込みをされる際、皆様一度ウェイティングリストへ自動的に移動されます。当日のオーガナイザーが人数調整を行い、基本は先着順にてお一人ずつへE-transfer先を記載したメッセージを送ります。こちらでお支払いを確認した後、オーガナイザーが参加者リストへ移動します。一度お支払いされますと、払い戻しや振替は出来ませんのでご了承ください。

・イベントに遅れそうな場合は必ずオーガナイザーまでメッセージをお願いします。イベント開始時間にいるメンバーでグループを組み直すこともあるので、連絡なしで到着された場合はイベントに参加できない可能性もあります。原則、30分以上遅れての参加はご遠慮いただいております。あらかじめご了承ください。

キャンセル待ち

・満席の場合、”キャンセル待ち”リスト(waiting-list)にご登録いただくことが可能です。“参加予定”リスト（going-list)中に空席が発生した場合は、”キャンセル待ち”への登録が早かった方を優先に、オーガナイザーが”参加予定”へ移動しますので、当日の参加状況の変更がないかご自身でご確認ください。

title: WANTON LEE
location: Red Sandcastle Theatre,922 Queen Street East, Toronto, ON M4M 1J5, Canada
description:
WANTON LEE — Black Jazz History Comes Alive On Stage!

Presented by Things Falling Apart Theatre, Wanton Lee is a powerful, semi-fictional, soul-stirring theatrical journey inspired by the life, music and untimely death of legendary jazz trumpeter Lee Morgan.

Through a dynamic solo performance by Drae Walsh, audiences are transported into the world of jazz and the complicated life behind the trumpet. Wanton Lee explores brilliance, struggle, love, addiction, redemption and the price of genius, revealing the humanity behind one of jazz music’s most extraordinary figures.

Following its Toronto engagement in July, Wanton Lee returns November 30–December 6, 2026, at Red Sandcastle Theatre, 922 Queen Street East, Toronto.

Written and Directed by Tien Providence
Performance by Drae Walsh

Whether you're a lifelong jazz lover, a theatre enthusiast, a Black history buff, or simply looking for a compelling Toronto cultural experience, Wanton Lee offers an unforgettable evening of storytelling.

🎺 The music. The struggle. The genius. The man behind the trumpet.

Live Theatre. Live History.

In this beginner’s class you will learn about:

description:

Participants are expected to commit to the duration of the course and attend all learning circle sessions.
Used by startups and tech giants like Google, Facebook, Netflix, and more, Python offers you endless possibilities for creating small and large-scale software projects. User-friendly with easy-to-read code, Python is a great first programming language to learn and requires no prior programming knowledge. Python skills open you up to careers in almost any industry and are required if you want to continue to more advanced, higher paying software development and engineering roles such as software engineer, systems administrator, and security engineer.
Python Essentials 1
In this course, you will learn in-demand skills such as how to design, develop, and improve computer programs, methods for analyzing problems using programming, programming best practices, and more. The course also prepares you for the PCEP – Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer certification (Exam PCEP-30-0x).

title: Our Infinite and Inevitable Ends: Author Talk with A.D. Sui
location: Toronto Reference Library, Beeton Hall (first floor)
description:
In this exciting author talk A.D. Sui will discuss their upcoming novel Our Infinite and Inevitable Ends, a sapphic cli-fi thriller, as well as science fiction's role in today's rapidly politically and technologically changing world. Question and answer period to follow.
This sapphic cli-fi thriller is a love letter to hope in the bleakest of times, combining the multiverse-bending drama of This Is How You Lose the Time War with the cat-and-mouse chase of Killing Eve.
On a near-future Earth devastated by climate change, Dr. Cassandra Barlowe is right where she wants to be: working on an island of floating trash in the middle of the Pacific Ocean, as far away from Dr. Yana Gulsvig as possible. Cas’s research on plastic-dissolving fungi is undervalued and underfunded, thanks to the invention of deleria, a drug that allows glimpses into different timelines. For the average user, it’s a way to view lost loved ones or experience a different life, but it also offers a glimpse into worlds where humanity has solved its many global crises. Now, most science funding is dedicated to trawling these different timelines, searching for a reality with the solution to the climate devastation.
But when Yana — the world’s leading expert on deleria and Cassandra’s ex-lover — is killed in a mysterious explosion in the hub of deleria research, taking the hope of reversing climate change with her, Cas is arrested on charges of domestic terrorism. Cas must delve through timelines to piece together what happened, while watching other versions of herself and Yana live out the life they could have had — happier, more in love. As brutal government agents close in and her addiction to deleria grows, Cas has to make a choice: live in the spiraling branches of reality, seeking closure for Yana’s death until the drug shatters her mind, or live in the now, even if that means embracing her own damaged self and fighting, however hopelessly, for her own future and that of humanity.

Professor Belot’s primary interests are in philosophy of physics, philosophy of science, metaphysics, and epistemology. His most recent book, Accelerating Expansion: Philosophy and Physics with a Positive Cosmological Constant, explores some of the philosophical consequences of modern cosmology, focusing on the significance of the discovery of the accelerating expansion of the universe for our understanding of time, geometry, and physics.

Meet the Resident:
Sarah Zanchetta (she/they) is a queer textile artist and educator whose practice dives into the loss of connection and knowledge of poisonous plants in North America. Zanchetta uses textiles, texts, and hosts community workshops to create intimate works and spaces where we can unfold our curiosities, care and anxieties about what grows beside our feet. She holds a Master of Visual Studies from the University of Toronto (2023) and a BFA from OCAD University (2018).

title: Birds and Our Christmas Traditions
description:
Birds are woven into the fabric of Christmas traditions, serving as powerful symbols of hope, renewal, and warmth during the winter months. Their presence during the holidays, whether through festive ornaments, songs, or sightings at feeders, recalls ancient lore that connects birds with messages of love and positivity. By inviting birds into our lives and honoring them through tradition, we not only support these treasured visitors but also embrace the spirit of Christmas—one of generosity, harmony, and the celebration of nature’s enduring beauty. Jim Mackiewicz is the owner of Wild Birds Unlimited and has been helping customers with backyard bird feeding and connecting to nature for 25 years.

description:

A
learning circle

description:

Python Essentials 1

description:
Karla García is a Chilean-Canadian guitarist, music creator, and educator based in Toronto. Originally from Chiloé, Chile, she has performed as a soloist and collaborator with orchestras and ensembles in Canada and Latin America. title: Instructional Skills Workshop (ISW) (IN-PERSON) – December 9, 10, 11, 2026
description:
This 3-day intensive workshop encourages examination of one’s teaching practices with feedback focused on the learning process rather than on the specific lesson content. The ISW engenders participatory learning and community building that can transfer back into the classroom. Participants work collaboratively in a small group setting of 4-5 participants to further develop their teaching effectiveness as they design and lead three 10-minute lessons. Following each, participants receive reflective verbal, written, and video feedback from the other participants who have been learners.
This certificate is open to all faculty members (research stream, teaching stream, contract).
This certificate is also available for graduate students with at least 3 years of teaching experience. Alternatively, graduate students are invited to complete the Teaching Assistant Certificate in Teaching (TACT) ( https://www.yorku.ca/teachingcommons/certificates/#tact ).
This is a three-day workshop series scheduled for Wednesday December 9, Thursday December 10, and Friday December 11. Each day will run from 9 am to 4:30 pm in DB 1014.
** Please kindly note: this is a 3-day workshop series intended for participants to attend  the entire workshop (all three days from 9am-4:30pm) in-person.
Register using our registration form ( https://teachingcommonsforms.apps01.yorku.ca/forms/view.php?id=1163054 ).

information and connect with the business across all devices.
KEYWORDS: NAVIGATION MENUS · ELEMENTOR PAGE BUILDER · SUB-PAGES · CONTACT FORMS ·

Small Things Like These
by Claire Keegan
Summary: It is 1985 in a small Irish town. During the weeks leading up to Christmas, Bill Furlong, a coal merchant and family man faces into his busiest season. Early one morning, while delivering an order to the local convent, Bill makes a discovery which forces him to confront both his past and the complicit silences of a town controlled by the church. Already a bestseller in France and certain to be read worldwide for generations to come, Small Things Like These is a deeply affecting story of hope, quiet heroism, and empathy from one of our most critically lauded and iconic writers

title: Language Exchange & Social Event @ Madison Ave Pub by Toronto Babel
description:
TorontoBabel: Toronto's International Language Exchange
🌎**Toronto Babel – Language Exchange & Social Night!** 🎉

Looking to meet new people, discover different cultures, and switch up your usual Wednesday night?

Come hang out with Toronto Babel for an evening of languages, music, games, and good company! Whether you’re here to practice English, share your native language, or simply expand your social circle, there’s always someone new to meet and something to talk about. 🫶✨

✨ **What’s Happening:**

💬 **Language Exchange** – Practice English and connect through French, Spanish, Korean, Japanese, Mandarin, and more!

🎲 **Board Games** – Break the ice and challenge someone new

🎨 **Arts & Crafts** – Get creative and try something different

🎧 **Resident DJ** – Enjoy the music while you mingle

🌍 **Meet New People** – Connect with friendly faces from around the world

📍 **Madison Avenue Pub**
14 Madison Ave, Toronto, ON M5R 2S1
🕖 **7:00 PM – 11:00 PM**

Whether you’re rolling in solo or bringing your crew, come ready to meet new people, share a few laughs, and make some unexpected connections. Pull up solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll leave with new connections, good laughs, and even better vibes 💬🫶🌟

💵 **$5 Entry Donation at the Door**
Your contribution helps cover Meetup fees and event essentials like name tags, games, stickers, and other supplies that keep our community going. Thank you for supporting Toronto Babel! ❤️

📩 **CONTACT:** Terry (Organizer)
💸 **E-transfer:** [tmg8@wealthsimple.me](mailto:tmg8@wealthsimple.me)

🔗 **Stay Connected & Join Us:**

📸 Instagram: [https://www.instagram.com/t.o.babel](https://www.instagram.com/t.o.babel)

📅 Meetup: [https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel](https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel)

💬 WhatsApp Group Chat: [https://chat.whatsapp.com/EYMdUw8XaxE5irFSNg5bt7](https://chat.whatsapp.com/EYMdUw8XaxE5irFSNg5bt7)

📘 Facebook: [https://www.facebook.com/groups/torontobabel](https://www.facebook.com/groups/torontobabel)

👉 **See what’s coming up and RSVP on our calendar:**
[https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel/#calendar](https://www.meetup.com/TorontoBabel/#calendar)

Toronto Babel is a welcoming, inclusive, and safe space for everyone. Our events focus on language exchange, cultural sharing, and friendship — **not for dating or matchmaking.** Harassment and inappropriate behavior will not be tolerated. If you experience or witness anything concerning, please let an organizer know so we can help.

Come for the conversations, stay for the community! 🌎💬❤️

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Dec 10 - AI, ML and Computer Vision Meetup
description:
Toronto AI, Machine Learning and Computer Vision Meetup
Join our virtual meetup to hear talks from experts on cutting-edge topics across AI, ML, and computer vision.

**Date, Time and Location**

Dec 10, 2026
9:00 AM - 11:00 AM PST
Online. **[Register for the Zoom!](https://voxel51.com/events/ai-ml-and-computer-vision-meetup-december-10-2026)**

**Your mAP is fine. Your slices are not. Finding the images that actually matter**

A single mAP can look acceptable while one slice is unusable, small objects, occlusion, or a confused class. I will run a pretrained detector on a few hundred public images (COCO-style, not a production crawl), report the headline metric, then break the same run by slice and walk through the worst samples.

The claim is modest: you do not need a million images or a trained-from-scratch model to see what the mean is hiding, and you cannot relabel everything, so the next labeling budget should follow those slices. No employer data and no confidential dashboards.

*About the Speaker*

[Amandeep Jiddewar](https://www.linkedin.com/in/amanfj/) is a Machine Learning Engineer at Pinterest, with prior work in U.S. manufacturing analytics (CertainTeed / Saint-Gobain) and marketplace allocation (QuinStreet). Emory Goizueta MSBA (2019), Kaggle Expert. This talk is in his personal capacity and does not represent his current or prior employers.

**Production AI Agents: Tool Use, Evaluation, Guardrails and Observability**

Building an AI agent is easy. Knowing whether it is behaving reliably in production is much harder. This session explores how to evaluate agents that use tools and external systems, including tool-call validation, tracing, observability, failure analysis, guardrails, permissions, and human review.

Attendees will learn practical patterns for understanding not just what an agent answered, but why it acted and whether the action was safe.

*About the Speaker*

[Akshay Talathi](https://www.linkedin.com/in/akshaytalathi/) is a Vice President at Goldman Sachs with over 10 years of experience building large-scale, cloud-native, and distributed systems across financial services and technology. His current focus is GenAI and agentic AI, including production AI agents, MCP, enterprise integrations, guardrails, observability, and reliable AI-driven workflows.

**From Virtual Worlds to Physical AI: Building Simulation Pipelines That Survive the Real World**

Robots are moving beyond perception systems that only detect and classify objects toward systems that must understand a scene, learn behaviors, and act in the physical world. In this talk, I’ll show a practical Physical AI workflow using OpenUSD, BowerBot, NVIDIA Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab to build a robot’s virtual world, including its body, cameras, sensors, and environment.

We’ll explore how demonstrations and reinforcement learning can teach behaviors in simulation, how vision and sensor data become observations for a robot policy, and what needs to match when transferring that behavior to real hardware. The demo follows a small robot from a simulated environment toward a real-world task, exposing both the power and the limitations of sim-to-real.

The goal is to make the path from pixels to actions concrete for computer vision and machine learning practitioners.

*About the Speaker*

[Arturo Morales Rangel](https://www.linkedin.com/in/arturo-morales-rangel) is the founder of Binary Core LLC, a Physical AI engineering company working across simulation, perception, robot learning, and deployment.

**Prompting Video-Language Models in Production: Lessons from Enterprise Video Tagging and Evaluation**

Video-language models can now describe, tag and answer questions about long-form video, but production results depend heavily on prompt design and evaluation. This talk shares field lessons from deploying such models for media, news, streaming and sports organizations, including how to structure prompts for consistent, schema-bound outputs across hours of footage.

On one sports video-tagging project, consolidating the prompt definitions cut estimated processing cost about 3x, and about 90% of the originally reported issues were later resolved through prompting alone. I'll also walk through building evaluation frameworks for video outputs, including for hard domains like egocentric video, and what changes when migrating between model versions.

Attendees will leave with reusable prompt patterns and an evaluation checklist they can apply to their own video pipelines.

*About the Speaker*

[Yash Gugale](https://www.linkedin.com/in/yashgugale/) is a Senior Forward Deployed Engineer at TwelveLabs in New York, integrating video foundation models (Marengo for embeddings and search, Pegasus for video-language understanding) for media, news, streaming and sports customers. He previously spent about six years in video streaming engineering at Peloton and Samsung TV Plus, and holds an MS in Computer Graphics Technology from Purdue.

title: Aesthetics Reading Group (Alexandra King, Simon Fraser University)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Aesthetics Reading Group is pleased to welcome as guest speaker Alexandra King, associate professor in the Department of Philosophy at Simon Fraser University. Currently, she is thinking through what aesthetic normativity looks like: the shape it takes, its parallels and interactions with other varieties of normativity (like the moral and epistemic), and whether it can be said to exist at all. Within aesthetics, she is also interested in an assortment of issues, including subtlety, high and low art, aesthetic/artistic agency, and applied arts. She also owns, runs, and regularly writes for the aesthetics and philosophy of art blog Aesthetics for Birds, which aims to make concepts and arguments in academic aesthetics accessible to a wide, public audience.

title: Ghost Stories of Toronto: Modern Phantoms
description:
As Toronto has grown into a major metropolis, its ghost stories have grown along with it. Many of our city's most bone-chilling tales were born out of that rapid evolution — and the sense of unease it has often caused. We'll conclude this series of talks with author Adam Bunch by exploring ghost stories from Toronto's more recent past. We'll take the subway with the spectre believed to haunt the TTC, set sail with the ghost ship of Etobicoke Creek, and meet the demon said to have terrorized one of Canada's most famous folk singers.
About this event's guest:
Adam Bunch
Read More:
The Toronto Book of Love
The Toronto Book of the Dead
About this series:
You can learn a lot about Toronto through its ghost stories. Whether you believe in the supernatural or not, the tales we tell about spirits and spectres illuminate the true history of the city. They're often tied to dramatic stories of death and disaster, to fascinating historic sites, and to pivotal moments that helped shape our communities. In this series of talks by author Adam Bunch, we'll explore Toronto's past through tales of ghosts, séances and hauntings. Whether it's phantom horses from the War of 1812, the strange prime minister who believed in the occult, or the ghost who was arrested by the Toronto Police Morality Squad, these supernatural stories have a lot to teach us about the history of the place we call home.

title: Early Modern Philosophy Research Interest Group (Andreea Mihali, Wilfrid Laurier)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Early Modern Philosophy Research Interest Group is pleased to welcome as its guest speaker Andreea Mihali (Wilfrid Laurier University) who is an expert in critical thinking, informal logic and argumentation theory, modern philosophy (Descartes to Kant) and visual and musical arguments. 
Talk Title
Descartes’ Omissions 
Talk Abstract
In the Meditations Descartes insists that readers closely follow the example and meditating steps set out in this text (AT VII, 10; CSM II, 8). Given this emphasis on the right order of reasons, it is at least prima facie surprising to also find the following remarks in the Second Replies: “Moreover there are many truths which although it is vital to be aware of them – this method [analysis] often scarcely mentions since they are transparently clear to anyone who gives them his attention” (AT VII, 156; CSM II, 110 – emphasis added).  
A careful reading of Descartes’ works shows that such remarks regarding things left out of Descartes’ actual text are far from being unique. This paper aims to classify Descartes’ omissions, to inquire into what these omissions tell us about Descartes’ approach and to make some preliminary remarks about the light these omissions shed on his explicit statements and theses. 
After discussing and backing up with textual evidence seven criteria of classification of omissions (content-relatedness, scope, means of identification, deliberateness, motivation, purpose and who is expected to remedy these omissions), I will apply them to Descartes’ published works. This application will show that Descartes’ account of the progression of his published works in the Preface to the French Principles (progression from the Discourse and the three accompanying Essays, through the Meditations, to the Principles – Latin and French), this progression in effect also tracks omissions and corresponding additions.

title: Film Screening: ᑕᐅᑐᒃᑕᕗᒃ / Tautuktavuk / What We See
description:
Join us to watch ᑕᐅᑐᒃᑕᕗᒃ / Tautuktavuk / What We See in Inuktitut with English Subtitles.
The film screening will include an 82 minute film and a 20 minute pre-recorded Q&A (102 minutes total).
Blurring the line between narrative and non-fiction, Uyarak and her eldest sister Saqpinak, embark on a difficult healing journey after a traumatic event that reminds them of the importance of community, culture, and family.
Feel free to drop in, no registration required. Registering will send you a reminder before the event.
SYNOPSIS: After experiencing a traumatic event in Igloolik (an Inuit hamlet in Foxe Basin, Qikiqtaaluk Region in Nunavut), Uyarak leaves her community and family in Nunavut to live in Montréal. When Covid-19 lockdowns close off the Canadian Arctic from the rest of the world, Uyarak is further separated from her closest friend, eldest sister, Saqpinak. This extreme situation blurs the lines of both the fictional lives of the sisters, and the non-fiction lives of the film’s directors, Lucy Tulugarjuk and Carol Kunnuk, who play the sisters. The film becomes a series of vignettes of heartache and healing – both in the dramatic based-on-true-events narrative, and the lived reality of these characters and creators. Uyarak doesn’t remember much about one terrible night of domestic violence, but Saqpinak does. Through Zoom calls, Uyarak talks about healing from years of trauma and abuse, and how the counselling sessions she goes to, and other cultural reconnections, are helping her heal. At the same time, Saqpinak is raising a family and hosting live shows about her community. Things are difficult at home – Saqpinak herself is experiencing domestic abuse at home but is waiting to talk about this to Uyarak when she can get home. When Covid-19 restrictions ease, Uyarak is finally able to travel home to Igloolik. At home, she embarks on a deeper healing journey visiting with family and elders, in town, and out on the land. Uyarak and Saqpinak share more stories and support one another in their short time together before Uyarak must return to Montréal.
ABOUT THE CO-DIRECTORS: Lucy Tulugarjuk is an award-winning actor, creative performer, and the Executive Director of Nunavut Independent Television Network (NITV). NITV created Canada’s first 24/7 Inuit language television station, Uvagut TV. Lucy is the co-writer, director of Tia and Piujuq, and assistant director for Zacharias Kunuk’s, One Day in the Life of Noah Piugattuk. In addition to her work in film and television, Lucy is a skilled Inuktitut translator. Carol Kunnuk is a filmmaker working in independent television and film with Isuma for over 25 years as a writer, camera operator, production supervisor, assistant director, actor, and editor. Her personal work includes the short, Being Prepared (NFB), and creator/director of the documentary, Attagatuluk. Carol currently directs and produces Welcome to my Qammaq, a weekly live television show broadcasting across Canada on Uvagut TV.

description:

The series culminates in a collaborative public floral installation in the library, sharing participants’ work with the wider community.
Led by artists "Being~inbetween"
