title: Nerikomi with Eiko Maeda | Nov 14 & 15 2026 | Dupont
location: 300 Campbell Avenue, Unit 115 Join us for a two-day workshop with ceramic artist Eiko Maeda, exploring the traditional Japanese technique of Nerikomi. Unlike surface decoration, Nerikomi builds pattern directly into the clay body itself, layering, stacking, and folding differently coloured clays until intricate designs run through the material from edge to edge. Over two days, you'll learn to prepare and condition coloured clays, build your own pattern blocks and work through four distinct pattern designs, each resulting in a finished ceramic piece approximately 15 cm in diameter. Eiko will guide you through every stage, from initial slab to shaped, refined form. This workshop is open to makers at all levels. No prior experience with Nerikomi is required, though some familiarity with hand-building is an asset. ABOUT EIKO MAEDA Eiko Maeda trained in Japanese lacquer at Joshibi University of Art and Design in Tokyo before discovering ceramics after relocating to Canada. She has spent over a decade developing and teaching her Nerikomi practice from her studio in Ontario, and has been recognized by the Ontario Arts Council and the Toronto Outdoor Art Fair. In 2026, her work was exhibited in Taipei, Taiwan. PLEASE NOTE Firing is included in the registration fee. Finished works will be available for pick-up approximately 3–4 weeks after the workshop concludes. You will be notified by email when your pieces are ready. All Specialty tools will be available for usage with the option to purchase your tools at the end of the course., Toronto, ON

title: Série Portraits et autoportraits: Portraits et autoportraits supports d’une esthétique radicale
description:
Les expérimentations plastiques radicales du XXe siècles ne signifièrent en rien la fin des portraits et des autoportraits. Loin de devenir de simples prétextes, le genre fut au contraire renouvelé par les nouvelles solutions formelles issues du Fauvisme et du Cubisme, mais aussi par les arts décoratifs. Les réseaux d’ornements imaginés par Gustav Klimt concoururent ainsi à magnifier ses modèles tout en préservant leur sensibilité. Quant aux aplats de couleur avec lesquels Henri Matisse ou André Derain architecturent leurs autoportraits, ils traduisent leur vie intérieure avec plus d’intensité encore. Autant de recherches qui ouvrent la voie à l’art contemporain.
Cette conférence vous est proposée par Gilles Genty, historien de l’art, en partenariat avec l’
Alliance française de Toronto
.
Accessibilité:
Le sous-titrage en direct ou automatique, l’interprétation en langue des signes, les services d’intervenant, ou les services d’accompagnement sont disponibles sur demande. Veuillez soumettre votre demande au moins deux semaines à l’avance à : tpl.ca/accessibility-events

Event Description:
This is an in-person language exchange! Members are placed into groups of three or four based on their language level. Each 45 minute session consists of friendly casual conversation, and/or informal study.

After the Language event, we usually go for Dinner. Dinner is optional, you may or may not join the Dinner, it depends on you.

Atrium Food Court

The food court is directly connected to the Dundas subway station. Leave the subway station and walk west along Dundas Street.

At the intersection of Bay Street and Dundas Street, you will find an entrance. Proceed down the escalator.

The food court is on the basement floor. Please talk to the organizer with the signboard showing TJEX. (If you can’t find them, please send a message to the organizer.)

Members are removed from the group after 3 No-Shows.

Waiting List and Fee transfer:
Once you enter the "Waiting-list", we will message you for the payment via e-transfer. After your payment is confirmed, you will be moved to the "Going-list"

title: Android Apps for Beginners
description:
This class is for beginners who are curious about buying an Android phone or tablet, or who have acquired one and want to install apps. Android phones include those manufactured by Samsung, Google, Motorola, and OnePlus.

In this beginner's class, you will learn about:
- what apps are, and the benefits of using them
- the differences between pre-installed, free, and paid apps
- how to access and use the Google Play Store
- how to evaluate, download and use apps

At the end of the class, you will have a basic understanding of how to install apps on your Android device through the Google Play Store.

Bring your own device: if you have an Android device, feel free to bring it with you and follow along with the exercises.

Prerequisites:  None
Format:  Lecture with hands-on exercises

title: Afternoon Book Club
description:
Join us on the following Monday afternoons to discuss books in a friendly and social atmosphere: September 14th, October 19th, November 9th, and December 14th.
This month we will be reading
The MANIAC
by Benjamin Labatut.
The MANIAC
is a 2023 novel by Chilean author Benjamin Labatut, and his first in English (compared to his usual Spanish). It is a fictionalized biography of polymath John von Neumann interwoven with tripartite narratives exploring the intersection of human genius, rationality, and artificial intelligence.Told via oral-history style from peers, wives, and colleagues, Labatut attempts to decipher core themes of reason and madness, the edge of progress, and the loss of the sacred. While a spiritual sequel to
When We Cease to Understand the World
,
no prior knowledge of science or technology is needed to appreciate Labatut's polymathic portrait of von Neumann.
Participants can borrow a copy of the book from the Woodside Square branch upon registration.

Laboring under a shared loss, a father and son set out on a late-season backpacking trip through the mountains of New Hampshire. They find beauty and solidarity in the outdoors, making friends along the way and falling into the rhythms of an expedition. But when war breaks out during their hike, they are forced to withdraw even further into the backcountry.

From their mountain refuge they must confront the perils of a changed world until they are forced to decide whether--and how--to rejoin society.

title: Peek Inside an AI Assistant: How It Thinks and Works
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
You've asked an AI chatbot questions. But there's another kind of AI that doesn't just answer: it acts.
In this demo-driven talk with our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, we'll look deeply at always-on personal AI assistants. The assistant can read your files, use your apps, and remember what you've told it, growing more useful over time. The same powers that let it help you can hurt you if something goes wrong. We'll also open up what happens inside: the hidden instructions, the tools it uses, what it remembers and forgets.
Then we'll look at the AI assistant that helped develop this workshop, and how we shaped our workflow together, and why.
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.

description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads ***[Exit Party](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4792123)*** by Emily St. John Mandel (author of ***Station Eleven***).
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/5182568441053184) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"From the bestselling author of Station Eleven, Exit Party is Emily St. John Mandel’s epic new story of crimes committed and loves lost across worlds and decades.
2031\. America is at war with itself\, but for the first time in weeks there is some hope: the Republic of California has been declared\, the curfew in Los Angeles is lifted\, and everyone in the city is going to a party\.
Ari, newly released from prison, arrives with her friend Gloria just as a fragile new era begins. But there are people at the party who shouldn’t be there. Something is very wrong...
Years later, living a different life in Paris, Ari remains haunted by that night. Whatever happened at the party fractured her sense of reality – and may hold the key to a very different world.
Freedom and surveillance, art and survival, love and loss in a broken world: Exit Party is the electrifying new novel from Emily St. John Mandel." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/241683548-exit-party?ac=1&from_search=true&qid=8V5Hrtzu0U&rank=1))

"A novel of doubles, shadow worlds, and fractured timelines as a man disappears from a glittering Los Angeles party, and a woman—a gunrunner, an art collector, an operative of the State—searches for answers." (from [BookMarks.reviews](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/exit-party/))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Sven Beckert: A Global History of Capitalism
location: Toronto Reference Library, Bram and Bluma Appel Salon, Toronto Reference Library (789 Yonge Street), 2nd floor
description:
TPL and Toronto Metropolitan University present historian Sven Beckert in conversation with Sanjay Ruparelia at the Toronto Reference Library's Appel Salon.
As the Laird Bell Professor of History at Harvard University and co-chair of the university's Program on the Study of Capitalism, Sven Beckert has spent his career tracing how a single economic system came to structure nearly every aspect of modern life, how we work, how we think about ourselves and others, and how we organize our politics.
In
Capitalism: A Global History
, Beckert reveals that capitalism was born global, corresponding at no point to an idealized dream of free markets; from the outset, state-backed institutions, imperial expansion, and coercion shaped its dynamics as much as innovation and exchange did. Along the way, capitalism has both expanded political voice for some and violently foreclosed it for others, entangled from its origins with slavery, colonialism, and profound inequality.
How do we distinguish between capitalism's capacity to generate genuine prosperity and its tendency to concentrate power in ways that undermine democratic institutions? What can nearly a thousand years of capitalist history teach us about the conditions under which economic systems support, rather than erode, democratic life? And as we confront what many call a crisis of late-stage capitalism, what possibilities remain for reimagining an economic order more compatible with democratic values?
Join one of the world's foremost historians of capitalism for an essential conversation about the deep entanglement of markets and democracy, and what history suggests about the road ahead.
Question and answer session and book signing to follow. Books available for purchase.
About this Event's Guests:
Sven Beckert
Sanjay Ruparelia
Read More:
Capitalism
Empire of Cotton
***
This event is part of our
On Civil Society
series, where we host local and international authors, activists and academics in conversation about the most critical topics of our time. Generously supported by the McConnell Foundation and also by Chris M. Reid.
***
About the series:
On the Frontlines of Democracy
is a public lecture series to analyze the trajectory of democracy in the twenty-first century.
In every region, the prospects of democracy face serious challenges, old and new. Can we protect constitutional rights and renew collective self-rule in an era of popular mistrust, severe partisanship and resurgent nationalism? Can they reduce inequalities of power, wealth and status, defend deep diversity and confront climate change in the new digital age? Can we develop innovative strategies to revitalize civic engagement, empower public institutions and resist autocratic threats? And what can we offer, learn and do to promote the prospects of democracy in our increasingly post-western global order?

description:
What if your AI didn't need the internet at all: no subscription, no one recording what you type?
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, you'll see AI models running entirely on one computer, with no connection and no data leaving the room. We'll compare a small local model against a powerful cloud model and plain search: what each gets right, what each costs, and what the privacy trade-offs really are. You'll leave with a decision sheet for your own hardware, an installation recipe, and an honest look at what "open" really means when it comes to AI.
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.
Note: Your spot will not be guaranteed after 5 minutes of the start of the program.
After this time, remaining seats will be filled on a first come, first serve basis until capacity is reached.

title: Building Your Website with WordPress Session 4
description:
In today's world, having a personal website is essential for many reasons and especially to support careers and small businesses. Learn how to use WordPress to build your own e-commerce or small business website.

In this final, pivotal session, we transform the websites into fully functional online stores. We will cover
the comprehensive setup of WooCommerce, including product listing and category management, with

site review, troubleshooting, and a collaborative Q&A to ensure each participant feels confident
managing and growing their new online store.
KEYWORDS: WOOCOMMERCE SETUP · PRODUCT LISTING · STRIPE PAYMENT INTEGRATION · SITE

title: Sedai Youth Creator Lab Showcase
description:
For the past 2 years, the JCCC has been working on enhancing the accessibility of our Sedai Oral History Collection through long term preservation, outreach workshops on Oral History techniques and through activation of our existing interviews. The capstone project of this Japanese Canadian Legacies Society funded project is our Sedai Youth Creator Lab. Six youth have been working with three mentors and JCCC staff, to collect and edit oral histories in 3 amazing short documentaries. Join us on December 16, 2026 as we screen these documentaries for you for the first time. The evening will include 3 short documentaries and a panel discussion with our Youth and Mentors. A celebratory Reception will be held after the panel discussion. This evening event will be a celebration of both the work of our Sedai Youth Creator Lab and our larger Sedai Project as we wrap up this amazing grant work. We hope that you are able to join us as we celebrate this amazing project. When: December 16, 2026 Doors Open: 6:00pm Screenings will begin promptly at 7:00pm Where: Kobayashi Hall at the Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre Registration is highly recommended. Register

title: The Delicious and Surprising History of The Dining Room: Author Talk with John Ota
description:
John Ota presents​ and discusses his book
The Dining Room
.
Explore the stories behind twelve iconic dining rooms in homes around the world—from a Japanese samurai house to Claude Monet's brilliant yellow dining room to Frida Kahlo's Casa Azul to Jackie Kennedy’s White House—and travel through time in pursuit of the ultimate design.​
The Dining Room is an enlightening and joyous celebration of history, culture and the art of dining. Presenter John Ota's charming observations of the surprising impact of dining rooms on our lives and the cherished moments we share within them will delight armchair travelers, history fanatics and interior design enthusiasts alike.
John Ota has been involved with architecture and design since 1978, with degrees from Columbia University, the University of Toronto and the University of British Columbia. His bestselling book
The Kitchen
was a 2021 Taste Canada Awards finalist and a 2021 Paris Gourmand Cookbook finalist in the book design category. After working in architecture in Toronto, New York, and Vancouver, and as lead on multiple Ontario Ministry of Culture projects, John now loves to travel the world visiting historic houses, cooking regional food, and meeting people of all backgrounds.

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: How Do AIs "Think"? And Why They Get Things Wrong
location: North York Central Library, 2nd Floor eLearning Lab
description:
How does a machine actually "think"? Explore the history and latest developments of machine learning.
In this class led by our Innovator-in-Residence,
Ryan Kelln
, we'll dig into what's really going on inside AI systems: how they decide what matters in your question, where their training data comes from (and who's missing from it), and how hidden instructions can sneak into content and hijack an AI. Develop an intuitive understanding of how AIs "think" without the math. We'll talk about how AIs remember, how they don't and how they are both similar and different to humans. And we'll ask the question underneath it all: is there anyone home inside the machine?
Registration is required and will start November 9, 2026 at 12:30 PM.

description:

s'associent pour créer un club de lecture théâtre. Ce rendez-vous mensuel est l'occasion de discuter et d'explorer des scènes mythiques ayant marqué le monde du théâtre. Avec
Georges Som
, médiateur culturel, nous essayerons de comprendre les enjeux de ces scènes, de découvrir leurs sens et de partager nos sentiments sur leurs auteurs et autrices. Chacun est le bienvenu au club, qu'il soit néophyte ou amateur de théâtre confirmé. Les seuls prérequis pour participer sont la curiosité et le plaisir d'échanger autour du théâtre !
Au mois de décembre, nous allons discuter un extrait de la pièce
En attendant Godot
de Samuel Beckett. Deux vagabonds, Vladimir et Estragon, se retrouvent sur une route de campagne, près d'un arbre, à la tombée de la nuit. Est-ce bien le jour et l'heure pour attendre Godot. Arrivent Pozzo, un homme autoritaire, le propriétaire des lieux, avec un Knouk, un sous homme tenu en laisse.

title: Shannon Kyles: What Our Buildings Say About Us
description:
Shannon Kyles discusses the history of architecture in Ontario and what it says about the people who have built this province. Starting with the Indigenous people, going through the first century of European contact, through the 20th century wars, democratic policies that resulted, and finally onto the 21st century speculative housing practice.
Professor Shannon Kyles is the author of ​

. She has written and published articles on architecture, taught History of Ontario architecture for 42 years at Mohawk College and online for universities, and has served on the board of the Architectural Conservancy of Ontario for 15 years.

title: Internet Horror Classics on Film: Backrooms
description:
In this final instalment of Toronto Public Library's virtual series Internet Horror Classics on Film, actor Erin Mick and critic Michael LaPointe join host Adam Nayman to discuss Kane Parsons' debut film, Backrooms, which bends the liminal spaces that have haunted the internet for years into a mesmerizing horror film.
About this event's guests:
Erin Mick
is an actor and writer based in Toronto. Her doctoral research centers on contemporary horror cinema, with particular interest in emergent modes of fan/viewer engagement, as well as horror's relationship to and mobilization of notions of trauma and collective memory. Erin also works as an actor, and is a writer of horror fiction.
Michael LaPointe
is a novelist, critic, journalist and producer in Toronto, Canada. He has published a novel with Random House Canada, written for The New Yorker, The Atlantic, and The Paris Review, and produced series for BBC Radio 4. He is a regular contributor to the Times Literary Supplement. His second novel, Ruby Red, will be released in spring 2027.
Adam Nayman
is a critic, teacher, and author, whose books include critical surveys of the Coen Brothers, Paul Thomas Anderson, and most recently, in Mind Games, the filmmaker David Fincher. He is a regular contributor to The Ringer, a lecturer at the University of Toronto's Cinema Studies Institute, and he has written on film for The New Yorker and The New York Times.
Read more:
The Creep

Une discussion conviviale en français suivra le film, si le temps le permet. Présenté en version originale avec des sous-titres en anglais.
Ouvert à tous, mais recommandé pour enfants de 8 ans et plus accompagné de leurs familles.
Aucune réservation requise.
Join us for a French-language film screening of
La guerre des tuques
(1984), directed by André Melançon. In this Québecois cult classic, a snowball fight over the winter holidays becomes the pretext for a veritable battle between two gangs of children who take themselves seriously and play at war like adults.
An informal discussion in French to follow the film, time permitting. Film presented with English subtitles.
Open to all, but recommended for kids 8 and up with their families.

location: Sanderson - Closed, Main Floor Program Room
description:
Due to renovations the Bookclub will take place in Scadding Court Community Center in Room 4 (same building), participants will be responsible in sourcing copies of the monthly titles themselves as the branch will not be open to the public during this time. We apologize for the inconvenience!
Become a page-turner by joining the Between the Lines Book Club! Here, we embark on a new chapter with every read, diving into a world of endless possibilities. From gripping thrillers to heartwarming coming-of-age tales, or a sprinkle of fantasy adventures, there's something for everyone. Whether you're a die-hard fan of one genre or love mixing things up, you'll find a place here to discuss, share, and connect with fellow readers. Ready to explore different worlds and discover your next favorite book? Join us and let's turn the page together!
Friday November 16: A Gentleman in Moscow by Amor Towles
Set in Moscow in 1922,
A Gentleman in Moscow
by Amor Towles follows Count Alexander Rostov, a refined Russian aristocrat sentenced by a Bolshevik tribunal to house arrest in the grand Metropol Hotel, where he must spend the rest of his life confined within its walls. As the world outside undergoes dramatic political and social change, the Count gradually transforms his restricted circumstances into a life rich with unexpected friendships, meaningful encounters, and quiet adventures. From navigating the hotel's intricate social world to forming a particularly meaningful bond with a young girl named Nina, Rostov discovers new perspectives on love, loyalty, personal growth, and the passage of time. Elegant, witty, and deeply moving, the novel explores the nature of freedom, the importance of human connection, and the possibility of finding purpose and beauty even when life takes an unexpected turn.

cheese

title: Mission of Gravity - Hal Clement
description:
The Sci Fi Book Club
Hi everybody,

Back for another team investigating an alien planet. This time we have a true classic, Hal Clement's seminal 1954 gritty sci fi novel, *Missions of Gravity*. This one has been on the list for a while and I'm so glad it was on theme enough to get on the survey.

Book of the Month
*Mission of Gravity* \- Hal Clement \(1954\)

From a good review on Skiffy.ca, "Originally serialized in 1953 in the magazine *[Astounding Science Fiction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Analog_Science_Fiction_and_Fact)*, the tale was published in book form the following year. Decades later, it was awarded a [Retro Hugo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hugo_Award#Retro_Hugos), for excellence in SF’s pioneering era.

*Mission of Gravity* is an archetypal example of what the kids call “hard science fiction”, a subgenre in which the characters within the SF story solve physical problems with physical –largely technological– means. The science tends to be solid, even the speculative science, and the rules are intensely consistent within the boundaries of the story."

To join a Book Club meeting, all you will need is YOURSELF. If you haven’t had a chance to finish the book, we still would love for you to join us in the discussion.

Not able to join us in person for events? [The Sci Fi Book Club is on Discord](https://discord.gg/B9NMnC2F). Join us and keep the conversation going.

description:
The
Chess Institute of Canada (CIC)
invites you to join our Chess for Life program - a fun and engaging chess program designed for seniors of all skill levels. Chess Institute of Canada (CIC) is an engaging social chess experience for adults and seniors. Learn the game, build your skills, challenge your thinking and discover new strategies while connecting with fellow players. Whether you're making your first move or planning three moves ahead, there's a place at the board for you!
Whether you’re a seasoned player or interested in learning the game - enjoy friendly matches, sharpen your strategy, and connect with others in a relaxed, supportive environment. Come make your move!
Put your mind in play!
Register for a reminder. Drop-ins are welcome.
The program will take place in the Auditorium located in the basement. Elevator on site. If you have any questions, please call Bendale Branch at 416-396-8910.

🌎**Toronto Babel – Language Exchange & Social Night!** 🎉

Looking to meet new people, discover different cultures, and switch up your usual Wednesday night?

Come hang out with Toronto Babel for an evening of languages, music, games, and good company! Whether you’re here to practice English, share your native language, or simply expand your social circle, there’s always someone new to meet and something to talk about. 🫶✨

💬 **Language Exchange** – Practice English and connect through French, Spanish, Korean, Japanese, Mandarin, and more!

📍 **Madison Avenue Pub**
14 Madison Ave, Toronto, ON M5R 2S1

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Screen Scaries: Black Christmas, Bob Clark (1974)
description:
Get your spook on with this month's scary movie screening of
Black Christmas
(1974), directed by Bob Clark.
A prototype of the American slasher,
Black Christmas
wears its Giallo influences on its sleeve and sets a blueprint for genre films like John Carpenter's
Halloween
(1977). Shot in Toronto, the film follows a group of sorority girls over their winter break as they are harassed by a series of disturbing phone calls.
Black Christmas
has a running time of 1 hour and 37 minutes, and is rated R.
There will be a short introduction to the film followed by the screening, which will be accompanied by closed captions.
The next Screen Scaries will be:
January 25, 2027:
Ring
(1998, Japan) Hideo Nakata. Runtime: 1h35m; Rating: PG

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

*Eat / Drink/ Socialise at a nearby pub afterwards

Please use the map provided on the event page also.

Payment

**11.55 by Debit/Credit card

*Everyone will get cookies/candy for free

- Please do not bring CHIPS AND CRACKERS as they make a mess and are greasy
***ALCOHOL IS PROHIBITED AND WE HAVE A ZERO TOLERANCE POLICY ON THIS - there are no second chances**

title: ABCD Reads American Hagwon by Min Jin Lee
description:
A Book Club, Downtown (ABCD)
ABCD Reads [American Hagwon](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C4792135) by Min Jin Lee (author of [Pachinko](https://tpl.bibliocommons.com/v2/record/S234C3448477))
([RESULTS](https://opavote.com/results/6718256866656256) of the poll for this event.)

**:: ABOUT THE BOOK ::**
"In schools and churches, hotel rooms and nail salons, law firms and fried-fish shops; in cramped, dingy apartments and luxury, gated communities, the men, women, and children in American Hagwon struggle to find satisfaction and meaning in a world that seems to grow less forgiving with each passing year. Once comfortably middle class in Korea, John and Helen Koh and their three children, Bo, DH, and Mido, find their lives upended, first by a shocking betrayal by John's oldest friend, then by the 1997 Asian financial crisis." (from [BookMarks](https://bookmarks.reviews/reviews/american-hagwon/))

"At last, the National Book Award finalist and NYT bestselling author of Pachinko returns with a breathtaking contemporary epic: Min Jin Lee has written a masterpiece by turns sweeping and intimate, one that reckons with ambition and moderation, lust and loyalty, personal dreams and familial duty." (from [Goodreads](https://www.goodreads.com/en/book/show/245886309-american-hagwon))

**:: ABOUT THE EVENT ::**
You are welcome to arrive 30 minutes before the event and stay 30 minutes or longer afterward to connect with other attendees outside the book talk.

Please ensure you have read the book before attending (though finishing any book is not a barrier to participating, as long as you don't mind spoilers).

First-time attendees can join for free. If the event is full, we maintain an unofficial waitlist. Please send [Michael](https://www.meetup.com/members/55295192/) a direct message for more information, in either case.

We request a $3 contribution from regular attendees to help cover our monthly meetup costs.

**:: ABOUT OUR NEXT BOOK ::**
At the end of each event, we will ask for nominees for our next book. If you have a good one in mind, please ensure it is between 200-400 pages long, available from the Toronto Public Library, and counts as contemporary literary fiction (though these are not hard and fast rules). When enough nominees are collected, Michael will send the members a direct message with a link where you can vote.

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Applied Qualitative Research: A Practical Guide for Graduate Student Researchers
description:
Are you interested in gaining an understanding of how to design, conduct, and present applied qualitative research? If so, these online workshops are for you! While this series is particularly intended for graduate students, FGS additionally invites and warmly welcomes graduate faculty including supervisors and committee members, as well as research staff, and postdocs. Feel free to come to one, two or all of them! Workshops will be delivered virtually and will be recorded. Registration is required.
Facilitated by Dr. Karen Campbell, RN, PhD ( https://www.linkedin.com/in/kcamp232/?originalSubdomain=ca ), Assistant Professor, School of Nursing, York University. Dr. Campbell’s program of research focuses on the intersections of women’s health with physical and social geography. She has taught graduate-level courses in qualitative research and designed and conducted multiple applied qualitative research projects using a broad range of study designs and approaches to analysis.
Hosted by Associate Dean, Academic, Dr. Cheryl van Daalen-Smith, RN, PhD
Webinar One: A Guide to Applied Qualitative Research
This webinar provides graduate students, supervisors, and researchers with a practical foundation in applied qualitative research. Participants will explore key qualitative methodologies, research design considerations, data collection strategies, and approaches to generating rigorous and meaningful findings.
When: Tuesday, January 12, 2027 from 11:00 a.m.-12:15 p.m.
Location: Zoom
*Registration is required | RSVP Link
Webinar Two: Coding Qualitative Data
This webinar introduces the principles and practices of qualitative data coding, from developing initial codes to identifying patterns and themes. Through practical examples, participants will learn strategies for organizing, analyzing, and interpreting qualitative data in a systematic and transparent manner.
When: Tuesday, February 9, 2027 from 11:00 a.m.-12:15 p.m.
Location: Zoom
*Registration is required | RSVP Link
Webinar Three: Generative AI in Qualitative Data Analysis 
This webinar examines the emerging role of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in qualitative research and data analysis. Participants will explore opportunities, limitations, ethical considerations, and practical applications of GenAI tools to support coding, theme development, data synthesis, and research productivity while maintaining methodological rigor.
When: Tuesday, March 9, 2027 from 11:00 a.m.-12:15 p.m.
Location: Zoom
*Registration is required | RSVP Link

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Teaching Assistant Certificate in Teaching (TACT) – Winter 2027 Virtual Course
description:
Throughout this course, you will have the opportunity to practice and experience different instructional strategies with peers from across the university. Discussion and reflection will centre around the ways in which your instructional strategies are informed by the teaching and learning literature, and the ways you use the strategies intentionally to align with your teaching beliefs and commitments to Decolonizing, Equity, Diversity, Inclusion, and Accessibility (DEDIA).
By the end of the course, you will
– Connect and learn collaboratively with a community of individuals committed to professional development in teaching and learning
– Investigate the ways in which teaching strategies are used intentionally
– Express and practice different teaching and learning strategies to design and teach a 10-minute BOPPPS lesson giving and receiving feedback based on DEDIA and research evidence
Please note that registration closes on January 4, 2027 at 11:59pm ET.
The course will consist of five 2-hour synchronous sessions spread between January 14 to March 18, 2027 (details below) via Zoom. Online learning and preparation between sessions will be required, for a total time commitment of approximately 20 hours.

title: Learning, Not Shortcuts: Centring Growth in AI-Supported Classrooms Workshop
description:
Online workshop, 15 January 2027, 10-11:30 am ET

title: 藍 ai - A life of creativity in Indigo by Sachiko Watanabe Opening Reception
description:
Artist Talk Sachiko Watanabe will share the story of ai (indigo), from growing plants to making dye material, demonstrating the traditional tools and techniques used to transform indigo plants into dye. Through her artwork and personal experiences, she will discuss the various indigo dyeing methods, her deep connection with nature, her lifestyle and the role that love and care play in her creative practice. The presentation will include: An introduction to the cultivation of indigo, the preparation of natural dye, and the artistic process behind her work. A video presentation showcasing her life, practice and creative journey. A Q&A session with the audience. Exhibition info Artist bio: Sachiko Watanabe (渡辺幸子) was born in 1977 in Ehime Prefecture, Japan. After studying textile design at Musashino Art University in Tokyo, she encountered natural indigo dye at the Iyo Kasuri Centre in Ehime. This encounter marked the beginning of a practice that has continued for more than 20 years. Sachiko later moved to Onomichi, Hiroshima, where she developed her work with indigo. Today, she grows her own indigo plants on Mukaishima, an island off the coast of Onomichi. She combines her harvest with sukumo, traditionally fermented indigo leaves from Tokushima Prefecture, to create her own natural dye. Living in a traditional Japanese house, where she also exhibits and sells her work, Sachiko continues to work closely with indigo each day. Through her textiles, she hopes to share its quiet beauty and to remind us of the natural world that surrounds and embraces us. Her exhibitions include Indigo in Our Daily Lives (2019), Indigo, Simultaneously (2021), Indigo in Winter (2021), Indigo in Darkness (2022), and Intaking Indigo (2024) Photo: © Toshinori Tanaka

title: 藍 ai - A life of creativity in Indigo by Sachiko Watanabe
description:
For over twenty years, Sachiko Watanabe has lived with indigo — growing it, fermenting it, dyeing with it, and shaping her days around its rhythms. Traveling from her home in Japan, she brings this quiet, deeply personal practice to the JCCC for the first time. Rooted in one of Japan's oldest natural dyeing traditions, natural indigo sukumo fermentation, this exhibition invites you to slow down and step into her world — to see, touch, and feel the colour of a life shaped by patience, land, and time. Join us in welcoming her to Toronto. About the Exhibition The exhibition follows the full life cycle of indigo — from seed to sukumo, from vat to fabric, from field to everyday life. Visitors will encounter: The Making of Sukumo — a year-long journey through sowing, transplanting, harvesting, drying, and fermenting indigo leaves Shades of Indigo — a study of the many named hues within the indigo spectrum, from pale aijiro(藍白) to deep kachi-iro(搗色) Textiles & Objects — a curated collection of dyed khadi, cotton, linen, hemp, and wool pieces, shaped by Sachiko's hand Everyday Indigo — an invitation to touch, smell, and wrap yourself in indigo cloth Living with Indigo — a reflection on more than twelve years spent in an old farmhouse, where growing, fermenting, and dyeing indigo have become inseparable from daily life Opening Reception & Artist Talk Please join us on January 16 at 2pm More Info Workshops Details coming soon! Artist bio: Sachiko Watanabe (渡辺幸子) was born in 1977 in Ehime Prefecture, Japan. After studying textile design at Musashino Art University in Tokyo, she encountered natural indigo dye at the Iyo Kasuri Centre in Ehime. This encounter marked the beginning of a practice that has continued for more than 20 years. Sachiko later moved to Onomichi, Hiroshima, where she developed her work with indigo. Today, she grows her own indigo plants on Mukaishima, an island off the coast of Onomichi. She combines her harvest with sukumo, traditionally fermented indigo leaves from Tokushima Prefecture, to create her own natural dye. Living in a traditional Japanese house, where she also exhibits and sells her work, Sachiko continues to work closely with indigo each day. Through her textiles, she hopes to share its quiet beauty and to remind us of the natural world that surrounds and embraces us. title: Ethical Research Decision-Making: Building Professional Judgment Across Career Paths
description:
This workshop is designed for graduate students and postdoctoral scholars who want to strengthen their ability to navigate ethical challenges in research and professional practice. While responsible conduct of research is often presented through policies and regulations, researchers frequently encounter situations where the “right” course of action is not immediately clear. These complex scenarios require thoughtful judgment, critical reflection, and the ability to articulate and defend ethical decisions.
By the end of the workshop, participants will have greater confidence in navigating ethically challenging situations and a stronger foundation for responsible leadership in research and professional environments. The skills developed are relevant across disciplines and career paths, supporting participants in becoming thoughtful, reflective, and ethically grounded professionals.

title: Virtual Drop-In Session: Master of Biotechnology Management (MBM) & Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology (GDB)
description:
The Master of Biotechnology Management  is a course- and experiential learning-based graduate program designed for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides practical interdisciplinary training in biotechnology and management to enhance student competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Graduates from this program are prepared to contribute to the sector in roles that require scientific, technical, and management skills and competencies.  
The Graduate Diploma in Biotechnology is a graduate certification for students who hold a bachelor of science degree in biology, biological sciences, biotechnology, life science, or related discipline, and have little/no work experience in biotechnology. It provides scientific and technical training in biotechnology to enhance graduate competitiveness and employability in the biotechnology sector. Students acquire the skills and competencies required to address labour gaps in the biotechnology sector and strengthen the Canadian economy. 
Drop by one of our virtual sessions on Thursdays from 11:30 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. to meet the graduate program director and graduate program administrator who will be able to answer questions about the programs.

title: Aimi Kobayashi Piano Recital
description:
Experience an unforgettable evening with acclaimed Japanese pianist Aimi Kobayashi, celebrated for her “perfect technique, a light touch, fast and virtuoso” playing. A Fourth Prize winner at the 18th International Chopin Piano Competition, Kobayashi has captivated audiences around the world with her exceptional artistry, expressive depth, and extraordinary musicality. From her early beginnings at the age of three to performances with leading orchestras across Japan and Europe, she has established herself as one of Japan’s most sought-after pianists of her generation. Her distinguished career includes performances with the Orchestra of the Eighteenth Century, Moscow Virtuosi, Yomiuri Nippon Symphony Orchestra, Japan Philharmonic Orchestra, New Japan Philharmonic, Tonhalle-Orchester Zürich, Tokyo Symphony Orchestra, and Münchner Philharmoniker. Her recordings for Warner Classics feature works by Bach, Beethoven, Chopin, Liszt, and her latest album, Schubert (2024). Join us for an inspiring evening of piano artistry as Aimi Kobayashi brings her remarkable talent and passion to the stage. Concert Program: Beethoven: Bagatelles, Op. 126 Chopin: Nocturne in F major, Op. 15, No. 1 Chopin: Mazurka in F minor, Op. 68, No. 4 Chopin: Ballade No. 1 in G minor, Op. 23 Schubert: Piano Sonata No. 20 in A major, D. 959 *Concert program subject to change. Tickets $65 General Admission $50 JCCC Members and Bravo Niagara! Members $30 25 years old and Under Notes: HST not included no refunds/exchanges Tickets co-presented by the JCCC and Bravo Niagara! title: Saturday Movie: The Girl Who Cried Pearls and Higglety Piggley
description:
Due to Hillcrest Library closure on July 27, this event will be postponed until January 2027.
In Montreal, at the dawn of the 20th century, a poor boy falls in love with a girl whose sorrow turns into pearls. He sells them to a ruthless pawnbroker, who hungers for more. Tempted by greed, the boy must choose between love and fortune. The choice could damn his soul.
The 2026 Oscar® Winner for Best Animated Short Film from the acclaimed team of Chris Lavis and Maciek Szczerbowski. This meticulously crafted film is a testament to the magic of stop-motion animation. With handmade puppets, mesmerizing narration by Colm Feore and a haunting score by Patrick Watson,
The Girl Who Cried Pearls
is a timeless parable of desire, deception and the price of innocence. (25 minutes)
Also screening from the same Oscar winning team with be
Higglety Pigglety Pop! or There Must Be More to Life
. This live-action/animated adaptation of Maurice Sendak's book features the voices of Meryl Streep and Forest Whitaker.
The story follows Jennie the terrier's suspenseful and unexpectedly moving journey to gain new experiences and realize her dream of becoming the star of the World Mother Goose Theatre. (23 minutes)
Films courtesy of the National Film Board of Canada (NFB).
Drop-in! No registration required.

title: Thailand Sea Side Discovery: Bangkok, Phuket and Krabi Island
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
Join us for an unforgettable 10-day Meetup adventure through Thailand, blending culture, temples, islands, beaches, and relaxed free time. This trip is a true Meetup - designed for those who want to travel the world and explore exotic destinations like Thailand, but don’t want to do it alone. We are traveling as a group, while still enjoying flexibility and optional experiences.
This journey blends the energy of Bangkok, the tropical beauty of Phuket, and the laid-back charm of Krabi, creating the perfect balance of culture, nature, and downtime. We will explore iconic temples, cruise through stunning islands, relax on white-sand beaches, and enjoy free time to wander, shop, or simply slow down and soak it all in.

**Trip Highlights**
• Bangkok City & Temple Tour
• Optional Ayutthaya Day Trip
• Flight to Phuket included
• Phi Phi Islands Tour
• Big Buddha Visit
• Scenic drive from Phuket to Krabi
• 4 Island Hopping Tour with Picnic

**Who is this trip for**
✔ Solo travelers who don’t want to travel alone
✔ People who want structure without feeling rushed
✔ Travelers who enjoy a mix of sightseeing and free time
✔ Anyone who wants to experience Thailand with a fun, supportive group

This adventure is ideal for solo travelers, friends, couples and even families, who want the comfort of a group while keeping the experience fun and social.

The best way to see what it's like is to check the gallery with past pix from our previous trip: https://photos.app.goo.gl/qXfrs5zQp5rULNvb9

For a detailed Day By Day itinerary [Click Here](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8) to fill out the form and receive information.

**Land Tour cost $2997 per person, double occupancy (we match roommates for those willing to share and save).**
**If you want your own room: Solo occupancy $3867**

**The only way to secure your spot for this meetup is a $325 deposit that is refundable up to 90 days before departure.**
**[Click here for secure deposit link](https://www.paypal.com/instantcommerce/checkout/4K9UHVSFEL8UA)**

When you make a deposit be sure to fill out this [ATTENDEE’S FORM](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLScjUyrsruOGiQWnWgqn-hiNuIpheVNCkYkavtNyYNsAnn0tZA/viewform).
As mentioned, . . . the cost is $2997. This is for the "Land" portion only. **International airfare is not included.** This gives you the flexibility to have a flight with timing that works best for you. Or to use points/miles.
Ekaterina can also help arrange your airfare.
To contact her for more info, [CLICK HERE](https://www.meetup.com/messages/?new_convo=true&member_id=14363992) [to send her a message.](https://secure.meetup.com/messages/?new_convo=true&member_id=14363992)

**What is included in the cost:**
✔ Meet & greet upon arrival at the airport

title: Get the Jump on Spring 2027
description:
Where the Plant People Meet



Shake off the winter blues and start the countdown to spring at Toronto Botanical Garden’s much-loved Get the Jump on Spring one-day garden extravaganza. Whether you’re a seasoned gardener, a curious beginner, or simply dreaming of warmer days, this annual event brings together plant lovers, expert growers, and local makers for a joyful, inspiration-packed kickoff to spring. 



Saturday, February 20, 2027, 10 a.m. to 4 p.m.FREE Admission. $2 suggested minimum donation 







What to Expect













Plant Community Connections 



Meet fellow plant enthusiasts, swap stories, ask questions, and connect with horticultural societies, plant and seed vendors, local makers, and other community groups dedicated to gardening, nature, and sustainable living. 









Over 40 Local Makers & Eco-Vendors



Discover unique houseplants, organic seed vendors, botanical-inspired products, garden accessories, natural wellness items, and artisan goods from over 40 local makers and growers. 









Interested in Participating in 2027




APPLICATIONS FOR VENDOR SPACES IS NOW OPEN














Visit the Plant Doctor



Have questions about the health or care of your indoor plant(s)? Looking for help on how to repot your plant? Bring in your plant(s) or a photo, and our horticulturists will provide you with an on-the-spot assessment and treatment. Examples of services offered include: Pruning, repotting, leaf cleaning and pest removal. 



Please note: If your plant is HEAVILY infested with pests, you should keep it at home and only bring in a photo. This service is ideal for small or young plants. We will not be able to help you unload/load your plant. 









Free Plant & Seed Swap



Bring as many plants as you wish to trade. If there isn’t anything of interest on the table when you arrive, add your plant(s) and take a ticket to redeem later when you see something new you’d like to try.  



Drop by the Weston Family Library, which houses our Seed Library. You can borrow seeds for FREE! If you have extra seeds, package and label them to add to our seed library collection. There will be a seed library assistant to assist you with your selections and contributions. 















Seasonal Plants & Seed Sales



Shop a curated selection of seeds, unique plants, and specialty offerings from trusted growers—perfect for getting a head start on your garden plans. Drop by the Garden Shop to learn more about our new online plant shop with at-home delivery, pre-order early-blooming hellebores, and sample a flight of local Ontario honey. 









Pop up Plant Cafe



Recharge with a coffee, tea, or freshly baked cookie, square, or scone. Gluten-free, Dairy-free & nut-free options available. Bistro seating is available. Operated by Daniel et Daniel. 















Free Garden Chats



Grow your gardening confidence with interactive sessions in the Weston Family Library led by the Toronto Master Gardeners. No registration required. 









Free Family Fun



Bring the whole family along! Kids can enjoy a drop-in, plant-themed craft to take home or, if you prefer a quiet moment, roast marshmallow over the outdoor firepit or simply relax together and cuddle with a book in our cozy indoor corners. 














Ways you can make this event more sustainable




TBG will have waste stations for reuseable, recyclable and compostable materials with hands-on volunteers to assist.



Bring your water bottle and take advantage of our complimentary water station, bring your mug, plate, or cutlery.

title: Global Philosophy Research Interest Group Talk (Jeannie Miller, University of Toronto)
location: Jackman Humanities Building, Room 418, 170 St. George Street, Toronto, Ontario, M5R 2M8, Canada
description:
The Global Philosophy Research Interest Group is delighted to welcome as guest speaker Jeannie Miller, an associate professor in the Department of Near and Middle Eastern Studies at the University of Toronto. Her book, The Quibbler: Al-Jahiz’s Equivocations in Kitab al-Hayawan and Beyond is a study of the Arabic writings of al-Jahiz, a foundational 9th-century author and analyzes al-Jahiz’s literary style and unique voice as a performative demonstration of good thinking, according to his definition. She is currently working on several interconnected studies of the reception and afterlife of Abbasid texts in premodern Islamicate contexts, using manuscripts as evidence. How were these texts read before the modernizing movements of the 19th and 20th centuries and the advent of a modern notion of “literature”?

title: Everest Base Camp Yoga Trek: Discover the Land, People & Spirit of Nepal
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
**This is definitely a bucket list type of trip. It embodies adventure and the romance of traveling to far off places. It is also tempered with safety and do-ability.**
The actual dates are Apr 10-26, 2027 and the trip is 17 days/16 nights.

We have done this adventure three times already, in 2021, 2023 and 2025, and everybody had a blast! [CLICK HERE to see attendee photos of the EBC trek](https://photos.app.goo.gl/jtHi3tTjVhYGjtc19)

WE HAVE MADE CHANGES BASED UPON EXPERIENCE.

1. **We are ADDING** Yoga and Meditation, and a local expert TO BE WITH US to guide in Buddhist practice and local culture.
2. **We are ADDING** two days while going up to better acclimatize.
3. **We are ADDING** a HELLICOPTER FLIGHT from our highest camp back to start point AND REMOVING two days going down by taking the flight.

To clarify. We are NOT going up to the top of Everest (29,000’)
We are going to Everest Base Camp at 17,600’
Our starting elevation will be in Lukla at 9,400’

You need to be of average or better fitness. If you can manage walking 3-6 hours a day, up and down a hill while carrying a light daypack, you will be OK! If you are very fit and work out and train, you will be at the front.

Professional guides to lead, and Yaks to carry our gear are included. And a Yak Herder too!!

All that is left for us to carry is our water, snacks and camera.

*But I don't have the needed gear?!*
Sleeping bag and parka, rated to -10C are provided and walking poles too!

*Does this include food?*
All meals on the trek potion are included.

*What is lodging like?*
We are sleeping in a series of "Tea Houses" along the route. You will have a bed in a shared room with roommate (from the group). Sorry, a solo room will not be available on this trip. We will pair up everybody.

*How dangerous is this? What if I get sick or hurt?*
This is NOT the summiting Everest with people dying from bad choices. We will be walking on an established, well used trail the entire time, and NOT on snow or ice. Stats from past years show that 30,000 people a year do the EBC Trek. With all that said, . . . **our trip INCLUDES emergency insurance.** We are also Certified Wilderness First Responders.
**Plain and simple, safety is our primary goal. We will have an experienced guide and porters, and we will be along the entire way.**

*How much does this cost?*
**Everest Base Camp Trip US$3750 - 17 Days, land only (airfare not included)**
For this trip we don’t offer single occupancy and we match you with a roommate if you don't have one.

*RSVP to this event shows your interest, but does not hold your space.*
*The only way to secure your spot for this trip is a US$250 deposit for the land portion:* ***[CLICK HERE FOR SECURE DEPOSIT LINK](https://www.paypal.com/instantcommerce/checkout/A3DBBZGZVRNL4)***
*Deposit is refundable up to 90 days before the departure (less PayPal fees).*

For more information fill out this form: [https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)

Land Cost includes:

* Airport pick up and drop off 4 times
* 3 nights at Kathmandu hotel
* 13 nights Tea House accommodation during the trek.
* Kathmandu / Lukla Flights
* All entries, required permits and taxes
* Guide, Assistant guides and Porters
* Food and drinks during the trek
* Helicopter ride back from Gorakshep to Lukla
* Sim Card
* Sleeping bag, down jacket, hiking poles
* Welcome and Farewell dinner
* Sightseeing Tour in Kathmandu

This is the adventure of a lifetime!

It is done in a safe manner and includes lots with no surprises.
**To receive detailed itinerary, inclusions etc [CLICK HERE and fill out our google form.](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)**[ ](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)

AND/OR if you ***have questions?***
***[Message direct to Anna](https://secure.meetup.com/messages/?new_convo=true&member_id=131297062) (flights, itinerary, payments)***
***[Message Direct to Marc](https://secure.meetup.com/messages/?new_convo=true&member_id=273063881) (hiking information)***
AND/OR
***We do a Zoom Q & A (every other) Wed 6:00-7:30 PM***
***[CLICK HERE FOR THE Zoom Event](https://www.meetup.com/moretoexplore/events/296044209/)***
***[CLICK HERE for Google Form to get Reminder for the zoom](https://forms.gle/6Zs4GMhsN7ZD8ugW6)***

*NOTE: The "land portion" of this trip starts in Kathmandu on Apr 25 and ends on Mar 11. This event is longer than Meetup date range.*

SOT 2000318-10

As a meetup group we have gone to EBC, Kilimanjaro, Machu Picchu, Galapagos and other bucket list place. Come alone and leave with new lifelong friends.

Live the adventure instead of only dreaming it!

title: Postgres Conference 2027: Celebrating 20 Years of Community & Innovation! 🐘🎉
description:
Toronto Postgres
Join us as Postgres Conference turns 20! We are marking two decades of community-driven database excellence by gathering developers, DBAs, architects, and maintainers from around the globe who build, manage, and scale Postgres in production.

**📍 Venue:** San Jose Marriott, San Jose, California
📅 **Dates:** Apr 21, 2027 – Apr 23, 2027

**Two Decades of Real-World Engineering**
Reaching this milestone is a testament to the strength and resilience of open source engineering. Our community continues to push data systems forward, from core protocol advancements and a thriving extension ecosystem to autovacuum tuning, vector workloads, high availability, and data security.

## **Interested in Speaking? 📢**

Help shape our 20th anniversary program! We invite practitioners, researchers, and community members to submit speaker proposals. Share your hard-won production lessons, architecture strategies, security and compliance insights, post-mortems, or technical benchmarks with our global audience.

## **Conference Tracks**

Our comprehensive, multi-day, multi-track program offers deep technical sessions and holistic professional growth:

* **Essentials:** Fundamental concepts, best practices, and foundational knowledge for new and growing Postgres users, including secure configuration and access control basics..
* **Dev:** Application design, ORMs, query optimization, advanced SQL features, and secure coding practices such as preventing SQL injection and using row-level security.
* **Ops:** High availability, replication, backup & recovery, performance tuning, and infrastructure management, along with hardening, encryption, auditing, and compliance.
* **Extensions:** Extending Postgres functionality, custom extension development, and ecosystem integration, plus security tooling like pgaudit and extension supply chain safety.
* **AI:** Vector embeddings, pgvector, LLM integration, AI-driven data pipelines, data sovereignty, governance, and protecting sensitive data used in AI workloads.
* **Professional Development & Wellness:** Career growth, engineering leadership, mental health, and maintaining work-life balance.
* **Life & Fun:** Community stories, creative technical pursuits, and social networking activities.

**How to Submit Your Proposal**
Ready to share your knowledge with the Postgres community? Submit your proposal at [https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027/program/proposals/new](https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027/program/proposals/new)

**Visit the official conference portal to learn more about Postgres Conference 2027:**
**👉 [https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027 ](https://postgresconf.org/conferences/2027)**

**Questions?**
Reach out via [organizers@postgresconf.org](mailto:organizers@postgresconf.org) with any general questions or guidance regarding your proposal.

**Interested in Sponsoring?**

title: Unforgettable Croatia! The Pearls of the Dalmatian Coast - Split, Dubrovnik..
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
Join our Meetup group on this exciting tour of beautiful Croatia - a country blessed with both, transparent sapphire waters and glamourous old towns. A blissful vacation to a country full of beauty and history with an awesome group of active and fun people! Create lifelong friendships on our tours! *Come alone, leave with friends!*

From north to south, we will start with Croatia's charming capital, Zagreb. Visit the amazing Plitvice Lakes National Park, with its cascading waterfalls. Explore the former Roman citadel of Split with Diocletian's famous palace. Marvel at the UNESCO World Heritage city of Dubrovnik, boasting the largest and best preserved city walls in Europe. Check out the filming locations of Game of Thrones. Relax on Croatia's stunning Dalmatian coast, overlooking the crystal blue Adriatic Sea. Spend a couple of days on the sun drenched islands of Hvar and Korčula. Be our own boat crew for a day, while sailing to the famous Blue cave and 5 more islands.

For a detailed Day By Day itinerary:
**[Click Here](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)**[ to fill out our info request form](https://forms.gle/cQdqYw74gAYqphXX8)

The trip cost includes:

* 2 Nights Zagreb at Hotel Dubrovnik or similar
* 2 Night Split at AC Hotel by Marriott or similar
* 2 Nights Hvar at Podstine Hotel or similar
* 3 Nights Dubrovnik at Hotel Royal Neptunor similar
* Arrival and Departure Transfers
* Transportation throughout the tour
* Ferry tickets Hvar - Korcula - Dubrovnik
* Boat Charter for a day with visits to the Blue Cave and 5 islands
* Bus Transportation from Zagreb to Split
* Plitvice Lakes National Park Tour
* Zagreb Sightseeing and Tasting Tour
* Split Walking Tour
* Korčula Wine and Food Tour
* Dubrovnik Game of Thrones Tour

title: Bucket List Spain w/ Running of the Bulls
description:
20s 30s Toronto Social & Activities
**Enjoy Spain at its best! Dine at the oldest restaurant in the world, visit iconic museums such as Prado and Guggenheim, be amazed at Gaudi's architecture, taste pinxtos, sip good Spanish wine and view the Running of the Bulls from our own private balcony!**

This is just a little taste of what awaits us on this awesome culinary and cultural adventure!

*Spain is truly a magical and fascinating country - full of history, culture and oh . . . so much good food and fun time!!!*
*We get to travel as locals, mostly by train between the cities AND at the best time of year to be able to experience in person The Running Of The Bulls in Pamplona.*

We visit:

* Madrid
* Bilbao
* San Sebastian
* Pamplona RUNNING OF THE BULLS
* Barcelona

*Guided tours in each city, breakfast daily and several dinners, museum entrances, tasting menus, Running of the Bulls w/balcony view, transportation throughout the trip and much more!*

We travel as a group and have all travel arrangements taken care of. The trip’s structure also gives you the free time and flexibility to cater to your own interests. We have included sightseeing tours, museum visits, a-la-carte dinners, our own balcony to see the Running of the Bulls with the best and safest possible view, but you also have the independence to enjoy the beautiful cities at your own pace. The idea is simple: come alone, meet like-minded people, share unforgettable moments, and create lasting friendships—all without the rigid structure of a “one size fits all” tour.

[CLICK HERE](https://photos.app.goo.gl/F6Cyqavg7D9udncF9) to see photos from our previous Spain adventures!

**Price per person, double occupancy: US$5100**
(We match roommates for those who wish to share and save)

**[Click Here for Secure Deposit Link](https://www.paypal.com/instantcommerce/checkout/ULNGV9DYDGECC)**

Deposit is refundable up to 90 days before the departure (less PayPal fees).

**[Click Here and Fill out this Form if you are making a Deposit](https://forms.gle/XMbepMFnBbGwYS468)**

*\*\*What’s Included\*\**
• 12 nights in first-class hotels in central locations
• Daily breakfast
• Welcome dinner at Casa Botín in Madrid (est. 1725), recognized by the Guinness Book of Records as the oldest restaurant in the world
• Authentic Basque foodie (pintxos) tour in Bilbao
• Transportation between all cities throughout the itinerary
• Arrival and departure transfers (airport, hotels, and train stations)
• City sightseeing tours in Madrid and Barcelona
• Entrance tickets and guided visits to major highlights, including the Prado Museum, Guggenheim Museum, and Sagrada Familia
• Hands-on paella cooking class with sangria in Madrid
• Private balcony access for a front-row (and safe) viewing of the Running of the Bulls in Pamplona
• Services of your tour leaders throughout the trip

In addition to the services listed above, what’s truly included is a thoughtfully designed experience with great value, smooth logistics, a fun group atmosphere, and the opportunity to create lasting friendships and unforgettable memories.

*\*\*Not Included\*\**
x International airfare (we are happy to assist with arrangements)
